3_4_Sit-Up: Get down on your back with your knees bent and hook your feet under something that holds them in place.
Put your hands behind your head or at its sides. With your back resting on the floor, you are in the starting position.
Lift your upper body toward your knees by bending at the hips and curling your spine.
Stop at the top when your upper body is upright, at a right angle to the floor. Then go back down, but only three quarters of the way.
Do as many repetitions as your plan calls for.
90_90_Hamstring: Get down on your back and stretch one leg out flat on the floor.
Bring the other leg up until both the hip and the knee are bent to 90 degrees. If you need to, hold the leg steady with your hands. Start from here.
Straighten that leg so it points up into the air and hold it there for a moment. Then bend it back to where you started.
Ab_Crunch_Machine: Set the machine to a light resistance and take a seat. Hook your feet under the pads and take hold of the top handles. Rest your triceps on the arm pads with your elbows bent to 90 degrees. Start from here.
Crunch your upper body down and raise your legs in one movement, breathing out as you go. Tip: Move slowly and with control. Let your abs do the work and keep your legs and feet relaxed.
Hold for a second, then breathe in and go back slowly to where you started.
Do as many repetitions as your plan calls for.
Ab_Roller: Kneel down on the floor with the ab roller in both hands.
Set the roller down on the floor ahead of you, so that you rest on your hands and knees like in a push-up from the knees. Start from here.
Roll the wheel forward in a straight line, slowly, until your body is stretched out long. Tip: Go as low as you can while your body stays off the floor. Breathe in on the way out.
Hold the stretch for a moment, then breathe out and pull yourself back to where you started. Tip: Take your time and keep your abs braced the whole way.
Adductor: Get down on your front and put one leg on a foam roll.
Turn that leg until your inner thigh rests on the roll. Put as much of your weight on it as you can bear.
Let the inner thigh muscles go as loose as you can and roll back and forth from hip to knee. Stay on each tight spot for 10-30 seconds. Then do the other leg.
Adductor_Groin: Get down on your back and point your feet up at the ceiling.
Let your partner take hold of your feet or ankles. Spread your legs as wide as they go. Start from here.
Try to press your legs together for 10 seconds or longer while your partner holds them apart.

Then let your leg muscles go loose while your partner pushes your feet further apart, only as far as feels comfortable. Tell your partner as soon as the stretch is enough, so you do not overstretch or hurt yourself.
Advanced_Kettlebell_Windmill: With one arm, clean a kettlebell and press it overhead.

Keep that arm locked out the whole time and push your hips out toward the side of the raised kettlebell. Put your free arm behind your back and turn your feet to a forty-five degree angle away from the arm holding the weight.
Go down as low as you can.
Hold for a second, then come back up the same way to where you started.
Air_Bike: Get down on your back and press your lower back into the floor. Put your hands beside your head, and take care not to pull on your neck during the exercise. Then raise your shoulders off the floor as in a crunch.
Lift your knees until your thighs point straight up and your lower legs are parallel to the floor. Start from here.
Pedal slowly as if on a bike: kick your right leg forward and pull your left knee in at the same time. Breathe out and crunch to the side so your right elbow comes close to your left knee.
Breathe in and come back to where you started.
Keep pedalling and crunch to the other side, so your left elbow comes close to your right knee, breathing out.
Go on switching sides like this until you have done all the repetitions planned for each side.
All_Fours_Quad_Stretch: Get down on your hands and knees. Raise one leg from the floor and take its foot in your hand.
Hold the foot or ankle in your hand with the knee bent all the way, so you feel the stretch in the quadriceps and hip flexors.
Concentrate on opening your hips and pushing them down toward the floor. Stay there for 10-20 seconds, then change sides.
Alternate_Hammer_Curl: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand and your arms hanging straight down. Keep your elbows near your body.
Turn your palms in so they face your body. Start from here.

Keep your upper arm still, breathe out and curl the right dumbbell forward by tightening the biceps. Go on until the biceps is fully tightened and the dumbbell is level with your shoulder. Squeeze the biceps there for a second. Tip: Nothing but the forearm should move.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell slowly to where you started.
Do the same with your left hand. Both sides together count as one repetition.
Go on switching hands like this until you have done the planned number of repetitions.
Alternate_Heel_Touchers: Get down on your back with bent knees and your feet flat on the floor, about 18-24 inches from each other. Stretch your arms out along your sides. Start from here.
Breathe out, crunch your upper body about 3-4 inches up and forward toward the right, and touch your right heel. Hold the squeeze for a second.
Breathe in and return slowly to where you started.

Breathe out, crunch about 3-4 inches up and forward toward the left, and touch your left heel, holding the squeeze for a second. Breathe in as you return to the start. Once you have touched both heels, you have done 1 repetition.
Go on switching sides like this until you have done all the planned repetitions.
Alternate_Incline_Dumbbell_Curl: Take a seat on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand and your arms hanging straight down. Tip: Hold your elbows near your body. Start from here.

Keep your upper arm still, breathe out and curl the right dumbbell forward by tightening the biceps. Turn your hand on the way up until the palm faces upward. Go on until the biceps is fully tightened and the dumbbell is level with your shoulder. Squeeze the biceps there for a second. Tip: Nothing but the forearm should move.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell slowly to where you started.
Do the same with your left hand. Both sides together count as one repetition.
Go on switching hands like this until you have done the planned number of repetitions.
Alternate_Leg_Diagonal_Bound: Stand comfortably with one foot a little ahead of the other.
Push off from your front leg and drive the other knee forward and up as high as you can before you land. With every bound, try to travel as far to the side as possible.
A line on the ground can help you judge how far you get from one side to the other.
Do the same again, pushing off from the other leg.
Alternating_Cable_Shoulder_Press: Set both pulleys to the lowest point of the tower and pick a suitable weight.
Take the handles and bring them up to shoulder height with your palms turned forward. Start from here.
With your chest and head held high, straighten one elbow and press that handle straight up over your head.
Hold briefly at the top, lower the handle to the start and do the same on the other side.
Alternating_Deltoid_Raise: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, arms down at your sides.
With a slight bend in your elbows, lift the dumbbells straight forward up to shoulder height. Do not swing or use momentum.
Lower the dumbbells back to your sides.
For the next repetition, lift the dumbbells sideways, out from your body, up to roughly shoulder height.
Lower them to the start again and keep switching between the front raise and the side raise.
Alternating_Floor_Press: Get down on your back on the floor with a kettlebell beside each shoulder.
Bring first one kettlebell and then the other into place on your chest. Grip them by the handles with your palms turned forward.
Straighten both arms so you hold the kettlebells over your chest. Then bring one kettlebell down to your chest, turning that wrist toward the kettlebell that stays locked out.
Press the kettlebell back up and do the same with the other arm.
Alternating_Hang_Clean: Set two kettlebells down between your feet. For the starting position, push your hips back and look straight in front of you.

Clean one kettlebell up to your shoulder while the other hangs in your straight arm. To clean it, straighten your legs and hips and pull the kettlebell up toward your shoulder, turning your wrist on the way.
Let the cleaned kettlebell come down to the hang and clean the other one. Keep going like this.
Alternating_Kettlebell_Press: Clean two kettlebells up to your shoulders. To do that, straighten your legs and hips and pull the kettlebells up toward your shoulders, turning your wrists on the way.
Straighten one elbow to press that kettlebell straight up over your head, turning it until your palm faces forward. Keep the other kettlebell still at your shoulder.
Bring the pressed kettlebell back down to the start and press with the other arm right away.
Alternating_Kettlebell_Row: Set two kettlebells down ahead of your feet. Bend your knees a little and push your hips back as far as they go. Lean forward into the starting position and grip both kettlebells by their handles.
Lift one kettlebell from the floor and keep hold of the other. Pull the shoulder blade of the working side back and bend the elbow to bring the kettlebell up toward your stomach or ribs.
Put the kettlebell of the working arm back down and do the same with the other arm.
Alternating_Renegade_Row: Set two kettlebells on the floor roughly shoulder width apart. Get into a push-up position on your hands and toes with your body in one straight line, holding yourself up on the kettlebell handles. A wide foot stance may give you more support.
Press one kettlebell into the floor and row the other one: pull the shoulder blade of the working side back, bend the elbow and bring the kettlebell up to your side.
Put the kettlebell back on the floor and row with the other hand. Do several reps like this.
Ankle_Circles: Hold on to something sturdy, such as a squat rack.

Raise your right leg just about 2 inches off the floor and move your big toe in a circle, as if you were drawing a large circle with it. Tip: Each circle counts as 1 repetition. Keep breathing normally while you move.
Once the right foot is finished, do the same with your left leg.
Ankle_On_The_Knee: Lying on your back, bend both knees and leave your feet flat on the floor.
Rest the ankle of one leg on the knee of the other.
Take hold of the lower leg's thigh or knee and draw both legs in toward your chest. Keep your shoulders and neck relaxed. Stay there for 10-20 seconds, then change sides.
Anterior_Tibialis-SMR: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and your feet flat on the ground.

Take a massage stick or a rolling pin and press it into the muscles along the outer side of your shin. Roll from just under the knee down to just over the ankle and stay on each tight spot for 10-30 seconds. Then do the other leg.
Anti-Gravity_Press: Behind the head end of an incline bench, lay a bar on the floor.
Get on the bench with your chest down. Take the barbell off the floor with an overhand grip. Bend your elbows as in a reverse curl until the bar is close to your chest. Start from here.
Straighten your elbows to press the bar out ahead of your head. Your arms stay parallel to the floor during the whole movement.
Bring the bar back to the start and repeat until the set is done.
Arm_Circles: Stand and stretch both arms straight out to your sides. They should be parallel to the floor and at a 90-degree angle to your body. Start from here.
With each stretched arm, slowly begin to draw circles roughly 1 foot across. Keep breathing normally while you move.
Keep circling with your arms stretched out for around ten seconds. Then circle the other way.
Arnold_Dumbbell_Press: Take a seat on a bench that supports your back. Hold two dumbbells ahead of you at roughly upper chest height, elbows bent and palms turned toward you. Tip: Keep your arms close beside your body. The start should look like the top of a dumbbell curl.
To start the movement, lift the dumbbells and turn your palms on the way up until they face forward.
Keep pressing until your arms are straight above your head. Breathe out during this part.

Hold for a second at the top, then bring the dumbbells down to the start while turning your palms back toward you. Tip: Your left arm turns counter clockwise and your right arm clockwise. Breathe in during this part.
Do as many repetitions as your plan calls for.
Around_The_Worlds: Get down on your back on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms turned up to the ceiling. Tip: Hold your arms parallel to the floor, beside your thighs. Keep a slight bend in your elbows so you do not hurt yourself. Start from here.
Sweep the dumbbells in a half circle from beside your thighs to above your head. Your arms stay parallel to the floor through the whole movement. Breathe in during this part.
Breathe out and sweep the weights back the same way to the start.
Atlas_Stone_Trainer: With this trainer you can build strength for Atlas Stones when you have no stones to hand. It is usually built from bar ends or heavy pipe.
Put the weight you want on the bar. Stand with one foot on either side of it, bend at the hips and wrap your arms around the implement.
Straighten your hips to pull the weight up past your knees. Once it is above the knees, you can lap it: sit back, rest it on your thighs and hug it tight against your chest.
To finish, straighten your hips and knees and lift the weight as high as you can. For the next repetition, bring it back to your lap or down to the floor.
Atlas_Stones: Stand with the stone between your feet. Bend at the hips and wrap your arms around the stone from top to bottom, trying to get your fingers under it. Many stones have a small flat spot underneath, which makes them easier to hold.
Pull the stone in against your body and push through the rear half of your feet to lift it off the ground.
When the stone is past your knees, lap it: sit back and pull it onto the top of your thighs.

Stay low and roll the stone high up onto your chest while you change your grip to reach over the top of it. Stand up by driving your hips through. Step close to the loading platform, lean back and straighten your hips to get the stone as high as you can.
Axle_Deadlift: Step up to the bar until it sits over the middle of your feet. Stand with your feet roughly hip width apart. Bend at the hips and grip the bar at shoulder width, letting your shoulder blades move forward. An over/under grip is the usual choice.

Once your feet and grip are set, breathe in deeply. Then drop your hips and bend your knees until your shins touch the bar. Look ahead, lift your chest, arch your back and push through your heels to start the weight moving up.
When the bar is past your knees, pull it back hard: squeeze your shoulder blades together and drive your hips forward to meet the bar.
Hinge at the hips to bring the bar down, steering it all the way to the ground.
Back_Flyes_-_With_Bands: Loop a band around a fixed post, such as the upright of a squat rack.
Take the band's handles and step back until the band is under more tension.

Raise your arms and stretch them straight out ahead of you. Tip: Keep your arms straight, parallel to the floor and at a right angle to your body. Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and flat on the floor. Start from here.
Breathe out and open your arms out to the sides and back. They stay straight and parallel to the floor. Go on until your arms point straight out to your sides.
Hold briefly, then breathe in and bring your arms back to the start.
Do as many repetitions as your plan calls for.
Backward_Drag: Put the weight you want on a sled and fasten a rope or straps to it that you can hold.
Start walking backwards over the set distance. Lean back and push through your legs in short steps to move as fast as you can.
Backward_Medicine_Ball_Throw: A partner makes this exercise work best. Without one, you can throw the ball and fetch it yourself, or throw it at a wall.
Stand a few meters ahead of your partner, both of you looking the same way. Hold the ball between your legs to start.
Drop into a squat, then drive up hard the other way until you are fully stretched, and throw the ball over your head back to your partner.
Your partner can roll the ball back to you. Do as many repetitions as you want.
Balance_Board: Put a balance board on the floor in front of you.
Step onto it and try to find your balance.
Stay balanced for as long as you like.
Ball_Leg_Curl: Get down on your back on the floor and put your feet up on the ball.
Move the ball until your ankles rest on top of it with your legs straight. Start from here.
Lift your hips off the floor so your weight rests on your shoulder blades and your feet.
Bend your knees and tighten your hamstrings to roll the ball as near to you as possible.
Hold briefly, then go back to where you started.
Band_Assisted_Pull-Up: Loop the band through itself around the middle of the pull-up bar. Different bands give you more or less help.
Pull the free end of the band down and put one bent knee into the loop. Make sure it cannot slip out. Grip the bar medium to wide. Start from here.
Tighten your lats and bend your elbows to pull yourself up. Drive your elbows down to your sides. Pull so the bar comes in front of you and try to get your chin above it. Do not swing or jerk.
Hold briefly, then go back to where you started.
Band_Good_Morning: Take a 41 inch band and stand on one end of it with your feet a little apart. Bend at the hips and loop the other end behind your neck. Start from here.
With straight legs, straighten your hips until you stand almost upright.
Go back down to the start and make sure your back does not round on the way.
Band_Good_Morning_Pull_Through: Put the band around a post. Stand a short distance away and put the other end around your neck. You can use your hands to keep the band in place.
Bend at the hips and push your butt back as far as it goes. With a flat back, lean forward to roughly 90 degrees. Bend your knees only a little.
Drive your hips through to stand up again and return to the start.
Band_Hip_Adductions: Fasten a band around a solid post or a similar object.
Stand with your left side toward the post and step into the band with your right foot so it sits around the ankle.
Stand tall and hold on to the post if you need to. Start from here.
With your knee straight, lift your right leg out to the side as far as it goes.
Come back to the start and do the number of reps you want.
Band_Pull_Apart: Hold the band in both hands with your arms stretched straight out ahead of you.
Start with a reverse fly: move your hands apart and out to your sides.
Keep your elbows straight while you pull, until the band reaches your chest. Make sure your shoulders stay back throughout.
Hold briefly at the end, then go back to the start with control.
Band_Skull_Crusher: Fix a band low on a rack or on the bench itself. Then lie down on the bench with your head in line with the band.
Grip the band and lift your elbows until your upper arms are at a right angle to the floor. With your elbows bent, the band should be above your head. Start from here.
Keep your upper arms where they are and straighten your elbows until your arms are straight. Hold briefly at the top, then go back to the start.
Barbell_Ab_Rollout: Get into a push-up position, but with your hands on an Olympic barbell that has 5-10 lbs on each side, not on the floor. Start from here.

Keep a slight arch in your back, breathe out, lift your hips and roll the bar toward your feet. Tip: Your glutes should rise as you move, your abs should stay tight and your back should hold its posture the whole time. Your arms also stay at a right angle to the floor through the whole movement. Otherwise your shoulders and back do more of the work than your abs.
Squeeze for a second at the top, then breathe in and roll the bar slowly forward again to the start.
Do as many repetitions as your plan calls for.
Barbell_Ab_Rollout_-_On_Knees: Kneel down on the floor holding an Olympic barbell that has 5-10 lbs on each side.
Set the bar down on the floor ahead of you, so that you rest on your hands and knees like in a push-up from the knees. Start from here.
Roll the bar forward in a straight line, slowly, until your body is stretched out long. Tip: Go as low as you can while your body stays off the floor. Breathe in on the way out.
Hold the stretch for a second, then breathe out and pull yourself back to where you started. Tip: Take your time and keep your abs braced the whole way.
Barbell_Bench_Press_-_Medium_Grip: Get down on your back on a flat bench. Take a medium grip, one that puts your forearms and upper arms at a 90-degree angle halfway through the movement. Lift the bar out of the rack and hold it straight above you with locked arms. Start from here.
Breathe in and bring the bar down slowly until it touches the middle of your chest.

Hold briefly, then breathe out and press the bar up to the start. Concentrate on pressing with your chest muscles. At the top, lock your arms, squeeze your chest and hold for a second before you slowly lower again. Tip: The way down should ideally take about twice as long as the way up.
Do as many repetitions as your plan calls for.
After the last one, put the bar back into the rack.
Barbell_Curl: Stand tall and hold a barbell with your hands shoulder width apart. Your palms face forward and your elbows stay near your body. Start from here.
Keep your upper arms still, breathe out and curl the bar forward by tightening your biceps. Tip: Nothing but your forearms should move.
Go on until your biceps are fully tightened and the bar is level with your shoulders. Stay there for a second and squeeze your biceps hard.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly to where you started.
Do as many repetitions as your plan calls for.
Barbell_Curls_Lying_Against_An_Incline: Lie against an incline bench with a barbell in your hands and let your arms hang down in a horizontal line. Start from here.
With your upper arms still, curl the bar as high as it goes and squeeze your biceps. Breathe out during this part. Tip: Nothing but your forearms should move. No swinging with the arms.
Squeeze for a second, then breathe in and lower slowly to the start. Tip: Go down the whole way.
Do as many repetitions as your plan calls for.
Barbell_Deadlift: Step up to a loaded barbell.

With your back as straight as you can keep it, bend your knees, lean forward and take the bar with a medium, shoulder-width overhand grip. This is where the exercise starts. Tip: If the bar is hard to hold this way, use a mixed grip or wrist straps.

Holding the bar, breathe out and start the lift by pushing with your legs while you bring your upper body upright in the same movement. Once upright, push your chest out and tighten your back by drawing your shoulder blades back. Picture a soldier standing at attention.

To go back down, bend your knees and lean your upper body forward from the waist in the same movement, with your back straight. Once the plates touch the floor you are at the start again and ready for the next repetition.
Do the number of repetitions your program sets.
Barbell_Full_Squat: For safety, do this exercise inside a squat rack. Set the bar on the rack slightly higher than your shoulders. With the height right and the plates on, duck under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders, a little below the neck.
Grip the bar with one hand on each side. Unrack it by driving up with your legs while you bring your torso upright.

Take a step back from the rack. Stand in a medium stance, feet shoulder width apart and toes turned out a little. Look ahead the whole time and keep your back straight. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly: bend your knees and sit your hips back, head up and posture straight. Go down until your hamstrings rest on your calves.
Breathe out and drive the bar up, pressing your heels or midfoot into the floor. Straighten your legs and extend your hips until you are back in the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Barbell_Glute_Bridge: Sit on the floor with a loaded barbell across your legs. A thick bar or a pad around the bar makes this exercise far less uncomfortable. Roll the bar until it sits right over your hips, then lie flat on your back.
Start by pushing through your heels and lifting your hips straight up against the bar. Your upper back and your heels carry your weight.
Raise your hips as high as you can, then lower them the same way to the starting position.
Barbell_Guillotine_Bench_Press: Take a medium grip, one where your forearms and upper arms form a 90-degree angle halfway through the movement. Unrack the bar and hold it directly above your neck with locked arms. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until it is roughly 1 inch above your neck.

Pause for a second, then breathe out and press the bar back up to the starting position with your chest muscles. Lock your arms, squeeze your chest at the top, hold for a second and lower slowly again. The way down should last at least twice as long as the way up.
Do the prescribed number of repetitions.
Put the bar back in the rack once you have finished.
Barbell_Hack_Squat: Stand tall with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a barbell behind you, arms fully extended. Tip: Grip the bar at shoulder width with your palms turned backward. Wrist wraps can help you hold the bar more securely. This is your starting position.
Keep your head and gaze up and your back straight. Breathe in and squat down slowly until your upper thighs are level with the floor.
Breathe out and stand back up, pushing mostly through your heels and tensing your thighs.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Barbell_Hip_Thrust: Sit on the floor with a bench right behind you and a loaded barbell across your legs. A thick bar or a pad around the bar makes this exercise far less uncomfortable.
Roll the bar until it sits right over your hips. Lean back on the bench so its top edge is close to your shoulder blades.

Start by pushing through your feet and lifting your hips straight up against the bar. Your shoulder blades and your feet carry your weight. Raise your hips as high as you can, then lower them the same way to the starting position.
Barbell_Incline_Bench_Press_-_Medium_Gri: Lie down on an incline bench. Take a medium grip, one where your forearms and upper arms form a 90-degree angle halfway through the movement. Unrack the bar and hold it directly above you with locked arms. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until it touches your upper chest.

Pause for a second, then breathe out and press the bar back up to the starting position with your chest muscles. Lock your arms at the top, squeeze your chest, hold for a second and lower slowly again. Tip: The way down should last at least twice as long as the way up.
Do the prescribed number of repetitions.
Put the bar back in the rack once you have finished.
Barbell_Incline_Shoulder_Raise: Lie down on an incline bench. Take a medium grip, a little wider than your shoulders. Unrack the bar and hold it directly above you with straight arms. This is your starting position.
With your arms still straight, breathe out and push the bar higher by moving your shoulder blades forward, so your shoulders come off the bench.
Breathe in and let the bar sink back to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Barbell_Lunge: For safety, do this exercise inside a squat rack. Set the bar on the rack slightly lower than your shoulders. With the height right and the plates on, duck under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders, a little below the neck.
Grip the bar with one hand on each side. Unrack it by driving up with your legs while you bring your torso upright.

Move back from the rack. Take a step forward with your right leg and sink down through your hips, torso upright and balance under control. Breathe in on the way down. Note: Your knee must not travel forward past your toes as you lower, because that strains the knee joint unnecessarily.
Breathe out and push yourself up, mostly through your heel, until you are back in the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions, then do the same with your left leg.
Barbell_Rear_Delt_Row: Stand tall and hold a barbell with a wide grip, wider than your shoulders, and overhand, palms turned toward your body.

Bend your knees a little and lean forward, keeping the natural arch in your back. Let your arms hang down in front of you with the bar. When your torso is parallel to the floor, turn your elbows out, away from your body. Tip: Your torso and arms should form the letter "T". You are now ready to start.

Keep your upper arms at a right angle to your torso. Breathe out and pull the barbell up to your upper chest, squeezing your rear delts. Tip: Done correctly, the movement looks like a bench press turned upside down. Do not let your biceps do the work. Concentrate on the rear delts and use your arms only as hooks.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly to where you started.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Barbell_Rollout_from_Bench: Put a loaded barbell on the floor close to the end of a bench. Kneel on the bench with both legs and grip the barbell at medium to narrow width. This is your starting position.
Start by extending your hips so the bar rolls forward slowly. While it rolls, open your shoulders until the bar is above your head. Keep your arms straight for the whole movement.
Once the bar is as far forward as you can get it, come back to the starting position.
Barbell_Seated_Calf_Raise: Roughly 12 inches ahead of a flat bench, set down a block.
Take a seat on the bench with the balls of both feet resting on the block.
Ask a helper to lay a barbell across your upper thighs, roughly 3 inches above the knees, and to keep it there. You start each rep from here.
Breathe out and push up onto your toes as high as you can, squeezing your calves.
Hold the contraction for a second, then lower slowly to the starting position. Tip: Stretch your calves as far as you can to get the most out of the exercise.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Barbell_Shoulder_Press: Sit on a bench with a backrest inside a squat rack. Set the barbell slightly higher than your head. Take it with a pronated grip, palms turned forward.
With your grip at the right width, take the barbell and press it overhead until your arms are locked. Hold it at about shoulder level, a little in front of your head. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and bring the bar down slowly to your shoulders.
Breathe out and press the bar back up to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Barbell_Shrug: Stand tall with your feet shoulder width apart. Hold a barbell in front of you with both hands in a pronated grip, palms turned toward your thighs. Tip: Place your hands slightly wider than your shoulders. Wrist wraps can help you hold the bar more securely. This is your starting position.
Breathe out and pull your shoulders up as high as they go. Hold the contraction for a second. Tip: Do not try to raise the barbell with your biceps.
Breathe in and lower slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Barbell_Shrug_Behind_The_Back: Stand tall with your feet shoulder width apart. Hold a barbell behind your back with both hands in a pronated grip, palms turned backward. Tip: Place your hands slightly wider than your shoulders. Wrist wraps can help you hold the bar more securely. This is your starting position.
Breathe out and pull your shoulders up as high as they go. Hold the contraction for a second. Tip: Do not try to raise the barbell with your biceps. Your arms stay extended the whole time.
Breathe in and lower slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Barbell_Side_Bend: Stand tall with a barbell resting across the back of your shoulders, a little below the neck. Set your feet shoulder width apart. This is your starting position.

With a straight back and your head up, breathe in and lean to the right as far as you can, moving only at the waist. Hold for a second, then breathe out and straighten up to the starting position. Tip: Everything else in your body stays still.
Do the same movement to the left. Hold for a second and straighten up to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Barbell_Side_Split_Squat: Stand tall with a barbell resting across the back of your shoulders, a little below the neck. Set your feet wide apart and turn the foot of your lead leg out to the side. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and sink toward the side of the turned-out foot. Bend the knee and hip of your lead leg and leave the other leg only slightly bent.
Breathe out and straighten the hip and knee of your lead leg to come back to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of reps, then do the same with the other leg.
Barbell_Squat: For safety, do this exercise inside a squat rack. Set the bar on the rack slightly lower than your shoulders. With the height right and the plates on, duck under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders, a little below the neck.
Grip the bar with one hand on each side. Unrack it by driving up with your legs while you bring your torso upright.

Take a step back from the rack. Stand in a medium stance, feet shoulder width apart and toes turned out a little. Look ahead the whole time and keep your back straight. This is your starting position. Note: The medium stance used here trains the legs as a whole, but you can pick any of the three squat stances.

Breathe in and lower the bar slowly by bending your knees and hips, head up and posture straight. Go down until your upper legs and calves form an angle of slightly under 90 degrees. Tip: Done correctly, the front of your knees and your toes lie on one imaginary vertical line. If your knees move beyond that line, past your toes, you strain the knee unnecessarily and the form is wrong.
Breathe out and drive the bar up, pressing your heels into the floor and straightening your legs until you are back in the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Barbell_Squat_To_A_Bench: For safety, do this exercise inside a squat rack. Start by putting a flat bench or a box behind you. The bench teaches you to push your hips back and to reach the right depth.
Next, set the bar on the rack at the height that suits you. With the height right and the plates on, duck under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders, a little below the neck.
Grip the bar with one hand on each side. Unrack it by driving up with your legs while you bring your torso upright.

Take a step back from the rack. Stand in a medium stance, feet shoulder width apart and toes turned out a little. Look ahead the whole time, because looking down throws you off balance, and keep your back straight. This is your starting position. Note: The medium stance used here trains the legs as a whole, but you can pick any of the three squat stances.

Breathe in and lower the bar slowly: bend your knees and push your hips back, head up and posture straight. Go down until you lightly touch the bench behind you. Tip: Done correctly, the front of your knees and your toes lie on one imaginary vertical line. If your knees move beyond that line, past your toes, you strain the knee unnecessarily and the form is wrong.
Breathe out and drive the bar up, pressing your heels into the floor. Straighten your legs and extend your hips until you are back in the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Barbell_Step_Ups: Rest a barbell across the back of your shoulders, a little below the neck, and stand upright behind a raised platform, such as the step a spotter uses behind a flat bench. This is your starting position.

Set your right foot on the platform. Breathe out and step up by straightening the hip and knee of your right leg. Push mostly through the heel to lift your body, then bring your left foot onto the platform too.
Breathe in and step down with your left leg by bending the hip and knee of your right leg. Then set your right foot beside the left one, so you stand where you started.
Do the recommended number of repetitions leading with the right leg, then do the same with the left.
Barbell_Walking_Lunge: Stand with a barbell across your upper back and your feet shoulder width apart.
Take a step forward with one leg and bend both knees so your hips sink. Go down until your back knee almost touches the floor. Stay upright and keep your front knee over your front foot.
Push through the heel of your front foot and straighten both knees to come back up.
Bring your back foot forward into the next step and do the lunge on the other leg.
Battling_Ropes: You need a heavy rope fixed at its middle 15-20 feet away from you. Stand facing the anchor and hold one end in each hand, arms extended at your sides. This is your starting position.
Start by whipping one arm up to shoulder level as fast as you can.
While that arm falls back to the starting position, bring the other arm up.
Keep switching between left and right, snapping the ropes up and down at top speed.
Bear_Crawl_Sled_Drags: Put on a harness or a loose weight belt and hook the chain to the back of it, so your back is turned to the sled. Bend down and set your hands on the ground, with a flat back and bent knees. This is your starting position.
Start by pushing with your legs, left and right in turn. Your hands keep you balanced and help with the pulling. Aim for a flat back while you cover the given distance.
Behind_Head_Chest_Stretch: Sit on the floor with a straight back. Your partner stands behind you.
With your hands behind your head, drive both elbows backwards as far as they go while your partner holds them. You start from here.
With your hands still behind your head, gently try to bring your elbows forward for 10 seconds or longer. Your partner keeps your elbows from moving.
Then relax your muscles and let your partner gently draw your elbows back as far as feels comfortable. Tell your partner when the stretch is enough, so you avoid overstretching or injury.
Bench_Dips: Put a bench behind your back. It stands crosswise to your body and you face away from it. Hold its edge with your hands shoulder width apart and your arms fully straight. Stretch your legs out in front of you, bent at the waist and at a right angle to your torso. This is your starting position.

Breathe in and lower your body slowly by bending your elbows, until your upper arms and forearms form an angle of slightly under 90 degrees. Tip: Keep your elbows as close in as you can during the whole movement. Your forearms point down at all times.
Push your torso back up with your triceps until you reach the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Bench_Jump: With a box or bench 1-2 feet ahead of you, take a shoulder-width stance. Every jump starts from here.
Dip into a shallow squat to load the jump and swing your arms back.
Explode out of the squat: extend your hips, knees and ankles and jump as high as you can. Swing your arms forward and up.
Clear the bench and land with bent knees, letting your legs absorb the impact.
Turn to face the other way and jump back over the bench.
Bench_Press_-_Powerlifting: Lie on the bench with your head past the bar if you can. Pull your feet in under you and arch your back. Use the bar to take some of your weight, lift your shoulders off the bench, draw them back and squeeze your shoulder blades together. Push with your feet to press your traps into the bench. Keep your body this tight for the whole movement.

Whatever your grip width, your hands should cover the ring on the bar. Take the bar out of the rack without letting your shoulders roll forward. Concentrate on squeezing the bar and trying to pull it apart.
Bring the bar down to the lower chest or upper stomach, with bar, wrist and elbow kept in one line the whole time.
Pause when the barbell touches your torso, then press it up as hard as you can. Keep your elbows tucked in until lockout.
Bench_Press_-_With_Bands: Take a flat bench and fix a band under the bench leg closest to your head.
With the band firmly fixed, take one handle in each hand, then lie back on the bench.
Straighten your arms so you hold the handles in front of you, shoulder width apart.
At shoulder width, turn your wrists forward until your palms point away from you. This is your starting position.
Lower the handles slowly until your elbows are bent to 90 degrees. Stay in full control the whole time.

Breathe out and press the handles up with your chest muscles. Lock your arms at the top, squeeze your chest, hold for a second and lower slowly. Tip: The way down should last at least twice as long as the way up.
Do the number of repetitions your training program prescribes.
Bench_Press_with_Chains: Shorten the leader chain to the length you want. Hang the chains on the sleeves of the bar.

Lie on the bench with your head past the bar if you can. Pull your feet in under you and arch your back. Use the bar to take some of your weight, lift your shoulders off the bench, draw them back and squeeze your shoulder blades together. Push with your feet to press your traps into the bench. Keep your body this tight for the whole movement. Whatever your grip width, your hands should cover the ring on the bar.

Take the bar out of the rack without letting your shoulders roll forward. Concentrate on squeezing the bar and trying to pull it apart. Bring the bar down to your lower chest or upper stomach. Bar, wrist and elbow stay in one line at all times.
Pause when the barbell touches your torso, then press it up as hard as you can. Keep your elbows tucked in until lockout.
Bench_Sprint: Stand on the floor and rest one foot on a bench or box, heel near the edge.
Drive off the foot that is up on the bench and straighten the hip and knee as you go.
Land with the other foot on the box while the first foot goes back down to where it started.
Keep switching feet until the set is done.
Bent-Arm_Barbell_Pullover: Take a barbell with your hands shoulder-width apart and lie down on a flat bench.
Hold the bar right above your chest, elbows bent. That is the starting position.
Keep the same bend in your elbows and breathe in while you slowly move the bar in an arc to behind your head, until your chest feels stretched.
From there, breathe out and guide the bar along the same arc back to the starting position.
Pause for one second at the start, then repeat for the number of repetitions planned.
Bent-Arm_Dumbbell_Pullover: Stand a dumbbell upright on a flat bench.

Check that the dumbbell stands safely at the top end of the bench. Then lie across the bench so your body and the bench form a cross, with only your shoulders resting on the pad. Your hips are lower than the bench, your knees are bent and your feet stand firmly on the floor. Your head is off the bench too.

Take the dumbbell in both hands and hold it right above your chest, elbows bent. Both palms press against the underside of one end of the dumbbell. That is the starting position. Caution: Only use a dumbbell that is firmly put together. If the plates are loose, the dumbbell can come apart and land on your face.
Lock your elbows at that bend and breathe in while you slowly move the dumbbell in an arc to behind your head, until your chest feels stretched.
From there, breathe out and guide the dumbbell along the same arc back to the starting position.
Pause for one second at the start, then repeat for the number of repetitions planned.
Bent-Knee_Hip_Raise: Lie on your back on the floor, arms resting beside your body.
Bend your knees to about 75 degrees and raise your feet roughly 2 inches above the floor.

Pull your knees toward you with your lower abs, keeping the 75 degree bend in your legs. Keep going until your pelvis rolls back and your hips come up off the floor. Breathe out during this part. Tip: You finish with your knees above your chest.
At the top, tighten your abs for one second. Then breathe in and come back slowly to the starting position. Tip: Stay in control of the movement the whole time.
Do as many repetitions as your plan recommends.
Bent_Over_Barbell_Row: Hold a barbell with a pronated grip, palms turned down. Bend your knees a little and hinge forward at the waist with a straight back, until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Tip: Keep your head up. The barbell hangs right in front of you, your arms at a right angle to the floor and to your torso. This is your starting position.

Keep your torso still, breathe out and pull the barbell toward you. Your elbows stay close to your body and your forearms do nothing more than hold the weight. At the top, squeeze your back muscles and pause briefly.
Breathe in and lower the barbell slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Bent_Over_Dumbbell_Rear_Delt_Raise_With_: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, facing an incline bench.

With a straight back and its natural arch, lean forward until your forehead rests on the bench. Let your arms hang down in front of you at a right angle to the ground, palms turned toward each other. Your torso is parallel to the floor. This is your starting position.

Keep your torso leaning forward and still, and your arms straight with a slight bend at the elbows. Breathe out and raise the dumbbells straight out to the sides until both arms are parallel to the floor. Caution: Do not swing your torso and do not pull your arms backward instead of out to the side.
Hold the contraction at the top for one second, then lower the dumbbells slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Bent_Over_Low-Pulley_Side_Lateral: Choose a weight, then take the low pulley's handle in your right hand.

Hinge at the waist until your torso is almost parallel to the floor. Bend your legs slightly and rest your left hand on the lower part of your left thigh. Your right arm hangs from the shoulder in front of you, elbow slightly bent. This is your starting position.
Breathe out and lift your right arm out to the side, elbow still slightly bent, until it is parallel to the floor and level with your right ear.
Breathe in and let the weight return slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions, then do the same with the other arm.
Bent_Over_One-Arm_Long_Bar_Row: Load one end of an Olympic barbell. Wedge the other end into the corner between two walls, or block it with a heavy object on the floor, so the barbell cannot slip backward.
Lean forward until your torso is as near to parallel with the floor as you can manage. Keep a slight bend in your knees.
Take the bar with one hand right behind the plates on the loaded side and rest your other hand on your knee. This is your starting position.

Breathe out and pull the bar straight up, elbow tucked in to work the back as much as possible, until the plates touch your lower chest. Squeeze your back muscles on the way up and hold for a second at the top. Tip: Your torso must not swing at all. Only your arm moves.

Lower the bar slowly to the starting position and feel a good stretch in your lats. Tip: The plates should not touch the floor. For the best range of motion, small plates (25 lb) work better than larger ones (such as 35-45 lb).
Do the recommended number of repetitions, then change arms.
Bent_Over_Two-Arm_Long_Bar_Row: Load one end of an Olympic barbell. Wedge the other end into the corner between two walls, or block it with a heavy object on the floor, so the barbell cannot slip backward.
Lean forward until your torso is as near to parallel with the floor as you can manage. Keep a slight bend in your knees.
Take the bar with both hands right behind the plates on the loaded side. This is your starting position.

Breathe out and pull the bar straight up, elbows tucked in to work the back as much as possible, until the plates touch your lower chest. Squeeze your back muscles on the way up and hold for a second at the top. Tip: You can hook a stirrup handle or a double-handle cable attachment under the end of the bar and pull on that.

Lower the bar slowly to the starting position and feel a good stretch in your lats. Tip: The plates should not touch the floor. For the best range of motion, small plates (25 lb) work better than larger ones (such as 35-45 lb).
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Bent_Over_Two-Dumbbell_Row: Take one dumbbell in each hand, palms turned toward your body. Soften your knees and hinge forward at the waist with a straight back until your upper body is nearly parallel to the floor. Tip: Hold your head up. Let your arms hang straight down, at a right angle to the floor and to your torso, so the dumbbells are right in front of you. That is the starting position.

Hold your upper body still and breathe out as you pull the dumbbells up to your sides. Your elbows stay near your body, and your forearms do nothing more than hold the weights. At the top, tighten your back muscles and pause for one second.
Breathe in and let the dumbbells sink slowly back to the starting position.
Do as many repetitions as your plan recommends.
Bent_Over_Two-Dumbbell_Row_With_Palms_In: Take one dumbbell in each hand, palms turned toward one another. Soften your knees and hinge forward at the waist with a straight back until your upper body is nearly parallel to the floor. Tip: Hold your head up. Let your arms hang straight down, at a right angle to the floor and to your torso, so the dumbbells are right in front of you. That is the starting position.
Hold your upper body still and breathe out as you pull the dumbbells up to your sides, drawing your shoulder blades toward each other. At the top, tighten your back muscles and pause for one second.
Breathe in and let the dumbbells sink slowly back to the starting position.
Do as many repetitions as your plan recommends.
Bent_Press: Bring a kettlebell up to your shoulder with a clean: straighten your legs and hips while you lift the kettlebell toward the shoulder, letting your wrist turn on the way up. That is the starting position.

Lean your body away from the kettlebell side and keep going until your free hand can reach the floor. Watch the kettlebell the whole time. While you lean, straighten your elbow to push the weight straight up, so your arm stays at a right angle to the floor.
Stand back up tall with the kettlebell overhead. Lower it to your shoulder again and repeat for as many repetitions as you want.
Bicycling: Get on the bike and set the saddle to suit your height before you start.
Bicycling_Stationary: Get on the bike and set the saddle to suit your height before you start.

Pick what you want from the menu. The display may only switch on once you begin to pedal. Choose between the manual setting and one of the programs. Most bikes let you enter your age and weight to estimate how many calories you burn while training. You can change the resistance level at any point during the workout. Hold the handles to track your heart rate, which helps you stay at a suitable intensity.
Board_Press: Lie down on the bench and, if you can, slide up until your head is past the bar. Use one to five boards cut from 2x6 lumber and screwed together. A training partner can hold them, bands can fix them, or you simply slip them under your shirt.

Pull your feet in under you and arch your back. Hang some of your weight on the bar, lift your shoulders off the bench and pull them back so the shoulder blades squeeze together. Push with your feet to press your traps into the bench. Stay this tight for the whole lift.

Grip as you would for a normal bench press, or at shoulder width to put the work on the triceps. Take the bar out of the rack without letting your shoulders roll forward. Bar, wrist and elbow stay in one line throughout. Squeeze the bar hard and try to pull it apart.
Bring the bar down onto the boards, then press it up as forcefully as you can. Keep your elbows tucked until your arms lock out.
Body-Up: Get into a plank on the floor: your weight rests on your toes and forearms, and your torso forms a straight line. Set your forearms shoulder-width apart. That is the starting position.
Press your palms hard into the floor and straighten your elbows to lift your body up. Keep your torso stiff while you do it.
Bend your elbows and let your forearms sink slowly back to the floor.
Body_Tricep_Press: Set a bar in a rack at the height of your chest.
Stand and grip the bar at shoulder width. Walk back a yard or two, feet together, arms straight, so that you lean on the bar. That is the starting position.
Bend your elbows to bring your body down toward the bar.
Hold briefly, then straighten your elbows to push yourself back.
When bodyweight gets easy, drape chains over your shoulders to make it harder.
Bodyweight_Flyes: Lay two EZ bars loaded with the same weight side by side on the floor. Check that they can roll.
Get into a push-up position above the bars: toes and hands carry your weight, arms straight, body in one line.
Put both hands on the bars; you start from here.
Slowly and with control, slide your hands outward from the centre of your body so the bars roll apart. Breathe in during this part.
Once the bars are as far apart as you can manage, pull them together again to get back to the start. Breathe out as you do it.
Bodyweight_Mid_Row: Grip a pull-up bar with a medium to wide grip, palms turned away from you. Hang, pull your knees up to your chest, lean back and bring your legs over to your side of the bar. That is the starting position.
Start with straight arms. Bend your elbows and pull your shoulder blades back to lift your body until your legs touch the bar.
Hold for a moment, then come back to the starting position.
Bodyweight_Squat: Set your feet shoulder-width apart and stand tall. If you like, put your hands behind your head. That is the starting position.
Start by bending at the knees and hips, moving your hips backward as if to sit.
Go all the way down if you can, then quickly come up again to the starting position. During the squat, hold your head and chest high and press your knees outward.
Bodyweight_Walking_Lunge: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, hands resting on your hips.
Take a step forward with one leg and bend both knees so your hips sink. Go down until the back knee almost reaches the floor. Stay upright, and keep the front knee over the front foot.
Push through the heel of the front foot and straighten both knees to stand up again.
Bring the back foot forward into the next step and do the lunge on the other leg.
Bosu_Ball_Cable_Crunch_With_Side_Bends: Fix a standard handle to each arm of a cable machine and move both pulleys to the lowest setting.
Take a half balance ball and put it centred in front of the cable machine.
Lie back on the half ball so your lower back curves over it. Your backside is near the floor but does not touch it.
Reach back with both hands and take hold of one cable handle in each.
Set your feet wide apart. Stretch your arms straight out in front of you, between your knees, with your hands level with your knees.
Keep your arms straight and in line with the cable's upward angle. Crunch your torso up without letting your arms drop or bend.
Hold your arms rigid. Sink slowly back to the start, your back curved over the half ball and your abs lengthened.
Repeat this sequence until you cannot do another repetition.
At that point, keep your abs tight and lift your torso into a plank position, so your back comes up off the half ball.
Bring your straight arms down to your sides. Now bend sideways, left and right in turn, reaching for your heels. This finisher works your obliques.
Bottoms-Up_Clean_From_The_Hang_Position: Stand upright holding a kettlebell in one hand to start.
Swing the kettlebell backward with power, then drive it forward just as powerfully. Squeeze the handle as hard as you can and bring the kettlebell up to your shoulder.
Bottoms_Up: Lie on the floor on your back, legs straight and arms beside your body. That is the starting position.

Bend your hips and knees to draw your knees toward your chest. Then stretch your legs straight up so they stand at a right angle to the floor. Tilt and lift your pelvis so your glutes leave the floor.
Hold for a moment, then come back to the starting position.
Box_Jump_Multiple_Response: Stand relaxed in front of the box or platform, about one arm's length from it. Your arms hang by your sides and your knees are slightly bent.
Swing your arms to help the take-off and jump up and forward. Land on top of the box or platform with both feet at once.
Drop or jump straight back down to where you started, then go through the sequence again.
Box_Skip: Set up several boxes in a row, roughly 8 feet from one to the next.
Face the first box, one leg a little behind the other.
Push off with the back leg and try to get your hips as high as you can.

As soon as you land on the box, swing the other leg forward and up to win height and distance, and leap off the box. Land in the gap between the first two boxes on the same leg that touched down on the first box.
After that, move on to the following box and do the same again.
Box_Squat: With a box you can squat to the depth you want and build explosive strength in the squat. Set up in a power rack and put a box of suitable height behind you. Most people pick a height at which their thighs are parallel to the floor, but a higher or lower box works too if you want.

Step under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders. Pull your shoulder blades together and turn your elbows forward, as if to bend the bar over your shoulders. Lift the bar out of the rack with your lower back firmly arched and step back into place. A wider stance puts more work on the back, glutes, adductors and hamstrings; a narrower one builds the quads more. Look straight ahead.

Tighten your back, shoulders and core. Start going down by pushing your knees and backside out. Move your hips back until you sit on the box. Your shins are best at a right angle to the floor. Stop once you are on the box and relax your hip flexors. Never bounce off the box.
Keep your weight on your heels and press your feet and knees outward. Drive up from the box, leading with your head. Keep rising and stay tight from head to toe.
Box_Squat_with_Bands: Set up in a power rack and put a box of suitable height behind you. Loop the bands over the bar sleeves and fix them to band pegs, to the rack or to dumbbells so the tension is right. If you use dumbbells, secure them so they cannot shift, and check that they are heavy enough for your bands. Extra plates can weigh the dumbbells down. For more tension, widen the base on the floor or choke the bands. Most people pick a box height at which their thighs are parallel to the floor, but a higher or lower box works too if you want.

Step under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders. Pull your shoulder blades together and turn your elbows forward, as if to bend the bar over your shoulders. Lift the bar out of the rack with your lower back firmly arched and step back into place. A wider stance puts more work on the back, glutes, adductors and hamstrings; a narrower one builds the quads more. Look straight ahead.

Tighten your back, shoulders and core. Start going down by pushing your knees and backside out. Move your hips back until you sit on the box. Your shins are best at a right angle to the floor. Stop once you are on the box and relax your hip flexors. Never bounce off the box.

Keep your weight on your heels and press your feet and knees outward. Drive up from the box, leading with your head. Keep rising and stay tight from head to toe. Put the barbell back in the rack carefully.
Box_Squat_with_Chains: Set up in a power rack and put a box of suitable height behind you. Most people pick a height at which their thighs are parallel to the floor, but a higher or lower box works too if you want.

For the chains, first loop the leader chain over the sleeves of the bar. Clip the heavy chain on with a snap hook. Set the leader chain's length so that a few links still rest on the floor when you stand at the top.

Step under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders. Pull your shoulder blades together and turn your elbows forward, as if to bend the bar over your shoulders. Lift the bar out of the rack with your lower back firmly arched and step back into place. A wider stance puts more work on the back, glutes, adductors and hamstrings; a narrower one builds the quads more. Look straight ahead.

Tighten your back, shoulders and core. Start going down by pushing your knees and backside out. Move your hips back until you sit on the box. Your shins are best at a right angle to the floor. Stop once you are on the box and relax your hip flexors. Never bounce off the box.
Keep your weight on your heels and press your feet and knees outward. Drive up from the box, leading with your head. Keep rising and stay tight from head to toe.
Brachialis-SMR: Lie on one side and rest your upper arm on the foam roller. Keep the upper arm roughly in line with your body, the outer side of the biceps pushing into the roller.
Lift your hips from the floor so your arm and feet carry your weight. Stay there for 10-30 seconds, then change sides.
Bradford_Rocky_Presses: Sit on a military press bench and hold a bar at shoulder height with a pronated grip, palms turned forward. Tip: Grip wider than your shoulders, so that forearm and upper arm form a 90-degree angle when the barbell comes down. That is the starting position.
With the right grip on the barbell, press it up above your head until your arms lock.
Breathe in and slowly bring the bar down behind your head.
Breathe out and press the bar up again to where it started.
Breathe in and slowly bring the bar down to the starting position. That counts as one repetition.
Keep alternating like this until you have done the recommended number of repetitions.
Butt-Ups: Get into a pushup position, except that your elbows are on the floor and your weight rests on the forearms. Bend the arms to a 90 degree angle.
Round your back outward a little instead of holding it perfectly straight.
Push your glutes up toward the ceiling and tighten your abs hard to bring your ribcage and hips closer together. You finish in a high bridge position. Breathe out during this part.
Breathe in and come down slowly to the starting position. Tip: Do not let your back sink toward the floor.
Do as many repetitions as your plan recommends.
Butt_Lift_Bridge: Lie on your back on the floor, hands beside you and knees bent. Set your feet about shoulder-width apart. That is the starting position.
Push mostly through your heels and raise your hips from the floor with a straight back. Breathe out as you go up and stay at the top for one second.
Breathe in and come down slowly to the starting position.
Butterfly: Take a seat on the machine and press your back flat against the pad.
Grip the handles. Tip: Set the machine so your upper arms are parallel to the floor. That is the starting position.
Slowly bring the handles together and squeeze your chest in the middle. Breathe out as you do it and hold the squeeze for one second.
Breathe in and go back slowly to the start, until your chest muscles are fully stretched.
Do as many repetitions as your plan recommends.
Cable_Chest_Press: Choose a suitable weight, sit down and take the handles. Hold your upper arms at roughly 45 degrees to your body, head and chest high, elbows bent to about 90 degrees. That is the starting position.
Straighten your elbows and push the handles straight forward until they meet in front of you. Hold your shoulder blades pulled back throughout.
Pause with your arms fully straight, then go back to the start without letting the cables go slack.
Other ways to do it: with your back away from the pad, on an incline or decline, or one hand after the other.
Cable_Crossover: Set both pulleys high, above your head, choose the resistance and take one handle in each hand. This gets you ready for the starting position.

Step forward, in front of an imaginary straight line running between the two pulleys, and bring your arms together in front of you. Lean your torso slightly forward from the waist. That is the starting position.

Bend your elbows a little to spare the biceps tendon. Open your arms straight out to both sides in a wide arc until your chest feels stretched. Breathe in during this part. Tip: Your arms and torso stay fixed the whole time; only the shoulder joint moves.
Breathe out and bring your arms back to the start, following the same arc you used on the way out.
Pause for one second at the start, then repeat for the number of repetitions planned.
Cable_Crunch: Get on your knees under a high pulley fitted with a rope attachment.
Take hold of the rope and pull it down until your hands are beside your face.
Bend slightly at the hips and let the weight pull your lower back into an overextended arch. That is the starting position.
Keep your hips still. Tighten your abs and bend at the waist so your elbows move toward the middle of your thighs. Breathe out during this part and hold the squeeze for one second.
Breathe in and go back slowly to the start. Tip: Keep your abs under tension the whole time. And do not pick a weight so heavy that your lower back ends up doing most of the work.
Do as many repetitions as your plan recommends.
Cable_Deadlifts: Slide the pulleys to the bottom of the towers and choose a suitable weight. Stand exactly in the middle between the two uprights.
Bend your hips and knees and squat down until the handles are within reach.
Take the handles and start to rise. Push through your heels and straighten hips and knees, with your hands hanging at your sides. Hold your head and chest high the whole way.
Once you stand fully upright, go back down to the start and repeat.
Cable_Hammer_Curls_-_Rope_Attachment: Fit a rope to a low pulley, then face the machine, standing roughly 12 inches from it.
Hold the rope in a neutral grip, palms facing in. Stand up straight, keep the natural arch in your back and hold your torso still.
Tuck your elbows into your sides and leave them there for the whole movement. Tip: Your forearms are the only part that moves, never the upper arms. That is the starting position.
Breathe out and curl your arms up with your biceps until they touch your forearms. Tip: Elbows stay in, upper arms stay still.
Squeeze your biceps for 1 second, then slowly start lowering the weight to where it began.
Do as many repetitions as your plan recommends.
Cable_Hip_Adduction: Stand at a low pulley looking straight ahead, one leg beside the pulley and the other farther from it.
Clip the ankle cuff to the cable and strap it around the ankle of the leg beside the pulley.
Step out sideways from the weight stack into a wide stance and hold on to the bar of the pulley system.
Put your weight on the far foot, the one without the cuff, and let the cable draw the cuffed leg toward the low pulley. That is the starting position.
Use your inner thigh to bring the cuffed leg across in front of the far leg. Breathe out during this part.
Breathe in and go back slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions, then do the same with the other leg.
Cable_Incline_Pushdown: Lie on an incline bench with your head toward a high pulley machine that has a straight bar attached, facing away from it.

Reach overhead and take the straight bar at shoulder width with a pronated grip (overhand, palms down). Bring your arms out straight in front of you so the bar is about 2 inches from your upper thighs. That is the starting position.
With your upper arms held steady, raise your arms back in a half circle until the bar is directly above your head. Breathe in during this part.
Use your lats to return slowly to the start, and hold the squeeze when you get there. Breathe out while you do this.
Do as many repetitions as your plan recommends.
Cable_Incline_Triceps_Extension: Lie on an incline bench with your head toward a high pulley machine that has a straight bar attached, facing away from it.

Reach overhead and take the straight bar with a narrow pronated grip (overhand, palms down), hands closer than shoulder width. Hold your elbows tucked in at your sides. Your upper arms sit at an angle of about 25 degrees to the floor.
With your upper arms held steady, straighten your arms and tighten the triceps. Breathe out during this part and hold the squeeze for one second.
Return slowly to where you started.
Do as many repetitions as your plan recommends.
Cable_Internal_Rotation: Sit side-on next to a low pulley, legs crossed or stretched out in front, and take the single handle with the arm closest to the cable. Tip: If the pulley height can be changed, you can sit on a flat bench instead.
Rest your elbow against your side, bent to 90°, with the forearm pointing at the pulley. That is the starting position.

Rotate your shoulder inward to draw the handle toward your body until your forearm lies across your abs. The hand traces an imaginary half circle. Tip: Keep the forearm at a right angle to your torso the whole time.
Return slowly to where you started.
Do the recommended number of repetitions, then do the same with the other arm.
Cable_Iron_Cross: Set the pulleys high, choose the resistance and take one handle in each hand.
Stand exactly between the two pulleys, arms stretched out to the sides. Hold your head and chest high; your arms make the shape of a T. That is the starting position.
With your elbows kept straight, pull your arms straight down to your sides.
Pause at the point of strongest contraction, then let your arms go back to the start.
Carry on for the number of repetitions planned.
Cable_Judo_Flip: Fix a rope to a cable tower and move the pulley to its lowest position. Stand side-on to the cable in a wide stance and take the rope in both hands.
Turn your body away from the pulley and bring the rope over your shoulder, as if you were throwing someone in judo.
Move your weight from one foot to the other while you turn and crunch forward, pulling the cable down.
Go back to the start and repeat until you cannot do another repetition.
Then set up on the other side and go through the same sequence there.
Cable_Lying_Triceps_Extension: Lie back on a flat bench and take the straight bar of a low pulley in a narrow overhand grip. Tip: It is simplest if a partner passes you the bar once you are lying down.
Stretch your arms out so the bar sits above your torso, with arms and torso at a 90-degree angle. This is your starting position.
Bend your elbows to bring the bar down, keeping your upper arms still and your elbows tucked in. Stop when the bar gently touches your forehead. Inhale during this part.
Tighten your triceps and press the bar back up to where you started. Breathe out during this part.
Pause for one second with the triceps contracted, then repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Cable_One_Arm_Tricep_Extension: Stand right in front of the weight stack and take a single handle on the high pulley in your right hand with an underhand (supinated) grip, palm facing up.

Pull the handle down until your upper arm and elbow are fixed against your side. The angle between upper arm and forearm should be acute (under 90 degrees). Your free arm can rest at your waist, and for better balance you can put one leg forward and the other back. This is your starting position.
Tighten your triceps and bring the handle down beside you until the arm is straight. Exhale as you do so. Tip: Move only the forearm. The upper arm stays still the whole time.
Squeeze your triceps and stay in this contracted position for one second.
Let the handle return slowly to the starting position.
Do the planned number of repetitions, then do the same with the other arm.
Cable_Preacher_Curl: Roughly 2 feet ahead of a pulley machine, set up a preacher bench.
On the low pulley, fit a straight bar.
Take a seat at the preacher bench, elbow and upper arms pressed firmly on the pad's top, and let someone pass you the bar from the low pulley.
Hold the bar and stretch your arms out fully on the pad. This is your starting position.
Curl the weight up towards your shoulders and squeeze your biceps hard at the top. Breathe out as you curl, and stay at the top for one second.
Lower the weight slowly back to the starting position.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Cable_Rear_Delt_Fly: Set the pulleys to a suitable height, above your head, and choose the weight.
Cross the cables in front of you: your right hand takes the left pulley, your left hand the right one. You start from here.
Start by drawing your arms back and out to the sides, keeping them straight throughout.
Pause when you reach the end of the movement, then bring the handles back to the start.
Cable_Reverse_Crunch: Lay a mat on the floor in front of a low pulley cable, and fit an ankle strap to that cable.
With your feet pointing toward the pulley, sit down and fasten the cable around your ankles.
Lie back, lift your legs and bend your knees to 90 degrees. Legs and cable should be in one line; if they are not, move the pulley up or down until they are.
Hands behind your head, pull the knees in toward your torso and lift the hips off the floor.
Hold briefly, then lower your hips slowly and with control and return your legs to the 90-degree angle you started from. Your abs should stay under tension even in the resting position.
Keep doing this movement until failure.
Cable_Rope_Overhead_Triceps_Extension: On the pulley machine, fit a rope to the bottom pulley.

Hold the rope in both hands with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and stretch your arms so your hands are straight above your head. Keep your elbows close to your head, your arms perpendicular to the floor and your knuckles pointing to the ceiling. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms still, lower the rope slowly behind your head. Breathe in as you do so, and pause once your triceps are fully stretched.
Tighten your triceps and breathe out to come back to the starting position.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Cable_Rope_Rear-Delt_Rows: Sit at a low pulley row station just as you would for seated cable rows for the back.
Fix a rope to the pulley and hold it with an overhand grip. Stretch your arms out parallel to the floor, elbows pointing outwards.
Push your hips back until the knees bend slightly, with the lower back kept upright. You start from here.

Pull the rope to your upper chest, just under the neck, with your elbows high and out to the sides. Exhale and keep pulling until your elbows are slightly behind your back. Tip: Throughout the movement your upper arms stay horizontal, perpendicular to the torso and parallel to the floor.
Return to the start, with arms stretched out and shoulders reaching forward. Breathe in during this part.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Cable_Russian_Twists: Clip on a standard handle and set the pulley to a middle height.
Lie on a stability ball at a right angle to the cable and take the handle in one hand. Be about an arm's length from the pulley, so the weight keeps the cable taut.
Using both hands, take the handle and straighten your arms completely above your chest. The pulley belongs directly in line with your hands, so raise or lower it if it is not.
Keep your hips up and your abs tight. Turn your torso away from the pulley by a full quarter turn. Your body should form a flat line from head to knees.
Hold briefly, then return slowly and with control to the starting position. Even at rest the cable should still pull sideways.
Carry on with the same movement until you reach failure.
Then change your position and do the same sequence on the other side.
Cable_Seated_Crunch: With your back to a high pulley, sit on a flat bench.

Take the rope attachment in both hands, palms facing each other, and hold your hands firmly over both shoulders. Tip: Let the weight pull your lower back into a slight hyperextension. This is your starting position.
Keep your hips still and bend at the waist so that your elbows move towards your hips. Exhale as you do so.
Breathe in and return slowly to the starting position.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Cable_Seated_Lateral_Raise: Stand midway between two low pulleys facing each other and put a flat bench directly behind you, at a right angle to you, so that its narrow end is the one behind you. Choose the weight for each pulley.
Next, sit on the edge of the flat bench behind you, feet set ahead of your knees.
Lean forward with a flat back until your torso rests on your thighs.

Ask a partner to pass you the single handles of the pulleys. With the weight chosen, take the left pulley in your right hand and the right pulley in your left. The cables should run under your knees; your arms are stretched out, palms facing each other, elbows slightly bent. This is the starting position.

Without changing the shape of your arms, lift your upper arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor, at shoulder height. Breathe out as you lift and hold the contraction for one second.
Breathe in and lower your arms slowly to the starting position.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions. Tip: Throughout the exercise keep your upper arms perpendicular to your torso and your elbows fixed at an angle of 10 to 30 degrees.
Cable_Shoulder_Press: Slide the cables to the bottom of the towers and choose a suitable weight.
Position yourself right between the uprights. Take hold of the cables and bring them to shoulder height, palms turned forward. You start from here.
With head and chest up, straighten your elbows and press the handles straight overhead.
Pause at the top, then come back to the starting position and repeat.
Cable_Shrugs: Take a bar attached to a low pulley with an overhand grip (palms facing down), shoulder width apart or a little wider.
Stand upright near the pulley, holding the bar with your arms stretched out in front of you. This is your starting position.

Breathe out and raise the bar by pulling your shoulders up as high as you can. Hold the top for one second. Tip: Keep your arms straight the whole time. Do not let your biceps help with the lift. Only your shoulders move up and down.
Bring the bar back down to where you started.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Cable_Wrist_Curl: Begin by setting a flat bench in front of a low pulley fitted with a straight bar.
Take the bar with an underhand grip (palms up), narrow to shoulder width, and lift it so your forearms rest on top of your thighs. Your wrists should hang just past your knees.
Begin by curling your wrists up as you breathe out. Hold the contraction for one second.
Breathe in and lower your wrists slowly to the starting position.
Keep your forearms still: the wrists are the only part that needs to move in this exercise.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Calf-Machine_Shoulder_Shrug: Get into the calf machine with the shoulder pads above your shoulders. Keep your torso straight and let your arms hang naturally at your sides. This is your starting position.
