Breathing out, lift your shoulders toward your ears and stay in the squeeze for a full second.
Breathe in and return slowly to the starting position.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Calf_Press: Set the seat so your legs are just slightly bent at the start. Press the balls of your feet firmly on the platform.
Choose a suitable weight and take hold of the handles. This is your starting position.

Straighten your knees to extend your legs, lifting the weight only just off the stack. Your ankles should be fully flexed with your toes pointing up. Now push down through the balls of your feet as far as you can.
Pause briefly, then reverse the movement and repeat.
Calf_Press_On_The_Leg_Press_Machine: Sit in a leg press machine and set your feet on the platform straight in front of you, in a medium stance at shoulder width.

Release the safety bars that hold the weighted platform and push the platform up until your legs are fully stretched out in front of you, without locking your knees. Note: On some leg press machines you can leave the safety bars in place for more safety. If yours allows this, it is the preferred way to do the exercise. Torso and legs should form an exact 90-degree angle. Now carefully set your toes and the balls of your feet on the lower part of the platform, heels hanging over the edge. Your toes can point forward, outwards or inwards. This is your starting position.

Breathe out and push the platform by lifting your heels: extend your ankles as high as you can and tighten your calves. Keep your knees still at all times; they must never bend. Hold the contraction for one second before you lower again.
Breathe in and return slowly to the start: lower your heels by bending the ankles until your calves are stretched.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Calf_Raise_On_A_Dumbbell: Hold on to something sturdy for balance and stand on the handle of a dumbbell. A dumbbell with round plates is best because it rolls: you have to work harder to steady yourself, which makes the exercise more effective.
Roll your foot a little forward to get a good stretch in the calf. This is your starting position.

Rise onto the calf, rolling your foot over the top of the handle until the calf is fully extended. Breathe out as you rise. Tighten the calf hard at the top and hold for one second. Tip: Roll the dumbbell a little backward on the way up.
Breathe in and roll the dumbbell a little forward on the way down for a better stretch.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Calf_Raises_-_With_Bands: Take an exercise band and stand on it with your toes. Check that the band is equally long between foot and arm on both sides.

Holding the band's handles, bring your arms up beside your head as though you were about to do a shoulder press: palms forward, elbows bent and out to the sides. This puts tension on the band. This is your starting position.
With your hands staying at your shoulders, breathe out and rise onto your toes, tightening your calves hard at the top.
Hold the contraction for one second, then lower slowly to the starting position.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Calf_Stretch_Elbows_Against_Wall: Stand a couple of feet from a wall, facing it.
Lean into the wall and let your forearms carry your weight.
Try to keep your heels on the floor. Hold for 10-20 seconds. Stepping further from the wall makes the stretch harder, stepping closer makes it easier.
Calf_Stretch_Hands_Against_Wall: Stand several feet from a wall, facing it. Take a staggered stance with one foot in front.
With heel, hip and head in one straight line, lean forward and put your hands on the wall.
Try to keep the heel down on the floor. After 10-20 seconds, change sides.
Calves-SMR: Sit on the floor and put a foam roller under your lower leg. Cross the other leg over it, or set it on the floor so that it carries part of your weight. This is your starting position.

Put your hands beside or just behind you and push down to lift your hips off the floor, so that most of your weight rests on the calf. Roll from below the knee to above the ankle and stop for 10-30 seconds at tense spots. Repeat with the other leg.
Car_Deadlift: The apparatus for this event usually has handles for a neutral grip, though some have a straight bar that you lift like a normal deadlift. It can be loaded with a vehicle or with other heavy objects such as tractor tires or kegs.

Stand centred between the handles if squatting is your strength, or a couple of inches further back if deadlifting is. Set your feet about hip width apart. Hinge at the hips to take the handles. Once feet and grip are set, take a deep breath, then drop your hips and bend your knees.
Look straight ahead, keep your chest up and your back arched, and push through your heels to lift the weight. As it rises, squeeze your shoulder blades together and push your hips forward.
Hinge at the hips to bring the weight down, steering it to the ground.
Car_Drivers: Stand upright and hold a weight plate with both hands at 3 and 9 o'clock. Your palms face each other and your arms are stretched straight out in front of you. This is your starting position.
Start by turning the plate as far as you can to one side, the way you would turn a steering wheel.
Then turn it back the other way, right over to the other side.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Carioca_Quick_Step: Feet a few inches apart, left arm raised, relaxed and athletic: that is how you start.
Take a quick step behind with your right foot and pull the knee up.
Drive your arms back up as you pull the right knee, and make sure the knee travels straight up and down. Do not turn your feet, and keep looking forward while you move sideways.
Cat_Stretch: Get down on the floor on hands and knees.
Draw your belly in, let your head drop, and round your spine, lower back, shoulders and neck.
Catch_and_Overhead_Throw: Stand facing a wall or a partner.
With both hands, bring the ball behind your head, stretch as far as you can and throw it forward with force.
Follow through with the throw and be ready to catch the rebound. When throwing at a wall, stand close enough to catch the rebound and aim slightly higher than you would with a partner.
Chain_Handle_Extension: For this exercise you need two cable handles, a flat bench and chains. Clip the handles to the middle of the chains and lie on the bench. Your elbows should point straight up.
Start by straightening your elbows, with your upper arms still and your wrists pronated.
Hold briefly at lockout, then go back the same way to where you started.
Chain_Press: First connect the chains to the cable handles. Lie on the flat bench as you would for a dumbbell press, with wrists pronated and arms perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
Bend your elbows to lower the chains, so that part of the chain comes to rest on the floor.
Keep going until your elbows are at a 90 degree angle, then reverse by straightening your elbows to lockout.
Chair_Leg_Extended_Stretch: Sit up straight in a chair and hold the sides of the seat.
Lift one leg, straightening the knee and flexing the ankle as you go.
Slowly take that leg out to the side as far as it goes, then bring it back to the middle and lower it.
Do the same with the other leg.
Chair_Lower_Back_Stretch: On a chair, sit up straight.
Lean to one side with your arm reaching over your head. Your free hand can hold the chair.
Stay for 10 seconds, then do the same on the other side.
Chair_Squat: First set the bar at the height that suits you best. With the bar loaded, step underneath and rest it across the back of your shoulders.
Grip the bar with your hands facing forward, unlock it, then straighten your legs to take it off the rack.

Walk your feet about 18 inches in front of the bar. Stand shoulder width apart with your toes turned slightly out. Keep looking forward and hold your spine neutral or slightly arched. This is your starting position.
Bend your knees to lower the bar slowly, staying upright with your head up. Go down until the angle between thigh and lower leg is less than 90 degrees.
Breathe out and raise the bar: push your heels into the floor, straighten your knees and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Chair_Upper_Body_Stretch: Sit on the front edge of a chair and hold its back.
With a straight back, straighten your arms and pull your upper body forward until you feel a stretch. Hold for 20-30 seconds.
Chest_And_Front_Of_Shoulder_Stretch: Stand with your legs together and hold a bodybar or a broomstick to begin.
Grip the pole a little wider than shoulder width and hold it in front of you, palms facing down.
Raise the pole over and behind your head, carefully.
Chest_Push_from_3_point_stance: Squat down into a three point stance, one hand on the floor and your back flat. The medicine ball lies directly in front of you.
Start by taking your first step while drawing the ball to your chest and setting both hands for the throw.
On the second step, release the ball forward explosively, as hard as you can.
Chest_Push_multiple_response: Kneel facing a wall, or work with a partner. Hold the ball in both hands, tight against your chest.
Make the pass by driving your hips explosively forward and out while pushing the ball as hard as you can.
Follow through by letting yourself fall forward and catch yourself on your hands.
Return to upright at once. Repeat for the number of repetitions you want.
Chest_Push_single_response: Kneel and hold the medicine ball in both hands, tight against your chest.
Make the pass by driving your hips explosively forward and out while pushing the ball as far as you can.
Follow through by letting yourself fall forward and catch yourself on your hands.
Chest_Push_with_Run_Release: Take an athletic stance: knees bent, hips back, back flat, the medicine ball held near your legs. You start from here.
Pull the medicine ball in to your chest during your first step.
On the second step, push the ball forward explosively and sprint 10 yards straight after letting it go. With real speed you can catch your own pass!
Chest_Stretch_on_Stability_Ball: Get down on hands and knees beside an exercise ball.
Rest your elbow on top of the ball with the arm out to the side. This is your starting position.
With your elbow kept on top of the ball, sink your torso toward the floor. Stay in the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then do the other arm.
Childs_Pose: Get down on hands and knees and walk your hands forward.
Sink your buttocks back until you sit on your heels. Let your arms drag over the floor as you sit back, so that your whole spine is stretched.

When you have settled onto your heels, put your hands beside your feet and relax. "Breathe" into your back, with your forehead resting on the floor. Do not use this position if your knees give you problems.
Chin-Up: Take the pull-up bar with a grip narrower than shoulder width, palms turned toward your torso.

Hang with both arms stretched out, holding the bar at the grip width you chose. Keep your torso as straight as you can, with a curve in your lower back and your chest pushed out. This is your starting position. Tip: A torso kept as straight as possible gives the biceps the most work and the back the least.

Breathe out and pull yourself up until your head is about level with the bar. Focus on doing the movement with your biceps. Keep your elbows close to your body. Tip: The upper torso stays rigid as it travels; only the arms move. The forearms do nothing but hold the bar.
Squeeze your biceps for one second at the top, then lower yourself slowly to the starting position, where your arms are fully stretched. Breathe in during this part.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.
Chin_To_Chest_Stretch: Interlock your fingers at the back of your head with both hands, thumbs pointing down and elbows pointing straight ahead. Pull your head slowly down toward your chest and hold for 20-30 seconds.
Circus_Bell: A circus bell is a very large dumbbell whose handle is thick. Start with it between your feet and take the handle in both hands.
Clean it by straightening your hips and knees to bring it to the shoulder you prefer, and let go with the other hand.

Make sure one head of the dumbbell sits behind your shoulder, so that it does not throw you off balance. To get it overhead, dip by bending your knees, then drive up and press the dumbbell overhead, leaning slightly away from it.
Guide the bell carefully back to the floor, with as much control as you can. This event is best done on a thick rubber mat, which protects the floor from damage.
Clean: Set a barbell on the floor close to your shins and take it with an overhand (or hook) grip just outside your legs. Drop your hips with your weight on your heels, back straight, head facing forward, chest up and shoulders slightly in front of the bar. This is your starting position.

Start the first pull by pushing through your heels and straightening your knees. Keep the angle of your back unchanged and your arms straight. Move the weight with control until it is above the knees.

The second pull follows; it gives the clean most of its acceleration. When the bar nears mid-thigh, start to extend your hips. As in a jump, extend hips, knees and ankles to accelerate, and use that speed to send the bar upward. You should not need to pull actively with your arms to accelerate the weight: when the second pull ends, your body is fully extended and leaning slightly back, and your arms are still straight.

Once fully extended, move into the third pull: shrug aggressively and bend your arms, elbows up and out. At the peak of the extension, pull yourself down aggressively and rotate your elbows under the bar. Catch the bar in a front squat position; how deep depends on how high the bar was when the third pull ended. Rack the bar on your protracted shoulders, where it lightly touches the throat, with your hands relaxed. Keep descending to the bottom of the squat, which helps the recovery.
Recover at once by pushing through your heels, with your torso upright and elbows up. Keep going until you are standing.
Clean_Deadlift: Stand with the barbell near your shins. Place your feet straight below your hips and turn them out a little. Take the bar about shoulder-width apart, with both hands overhand or with a hook grip. Squat down to the bar. Fully extend your spine; the angle of your back should put your shoulders in front of the bar and keep your back as upright as possible.
Start by pushing into the floor with the front of your heels. Keep the angle of your back the same while the bar moves up. Push your knees out to the sides so they stay out of the bar's way.
Once the bar is past your knees, finish the lift: push your hips towards the bar until hips and knees are straight.
Clean_Pull: Stand so the barbell lies on the floor near your shins and grip it just outside your legs, overhand or with a hook grip. Drop your hips and put your weight on your heels. Keep a straight back, look ahead, lift your chest and set your shoulders slightly ahead of the bar. This is your starting position.

Start the first pull: push through your heels and straighten your knees. Do not change the angle of your back, and keep your arms straight with your elbows out. Bring the bar up under control until it is above your knees.

Now follows the second pull, where the clean gets most of its acceleration. Once the bar nears mid-thigh, start to open your hips. Speed up as if you were jumping: extend hips, knees and ankles and let that speed carry the bar up. You should not have to pull actively with your arms to speed the weight up. When the second pull ends, your body is fully stretched and leans back a little, and your arms are still straight. Make the full extension violent and abrupt, and do not hold it longer than you need to.
Clean_Shrug: Hold the bar shoulder-width apart, with both hands overhand or with a hook grip, so that it hangs at mid-thigh. Keep your back straight and lean it forward a little.
Pull your shoulders up towards your ears. You can usually load more weight here than in a clean, but do not load so much that the movement gets slower.
Clean_and_Jerk: Stand so the barbell lies on the floor near your shins and grip it just outside your legs, overhand or with a hook grip. Drop your hips and put your weight on your heels. Keep a straight back, look ahead, lift your chest and set your shoulders slightly ahead of the bar. This is your starting position.
Start the first pull: push through your heels and straighten your knees. Do not change the angle of your back and keep your arms straight. Bring the bar up under control until it is above your knees.

Now follows the second pull, where the clean gets most of its acceleration. Once the bar nears mid-thigh, start to open your hips. Speed up as if you were jumping: extend hips, knees and ankles and let that speed carry the bar up. You should not have to pull actively with your arms to speed the weight up. When the second pull ends, your body is fully stretched and leans back a little, and your arms are still straight.

Once you are fully extended, go into the third pull: shrug hard and bend your arms, elbows high and out. At the highest point of the extension, pull yourself down hard and turn your elbows under the bar while you do it. Catch the bar in a front squat; how deep depends on how high the bar was when the third pull ended. Rest the bar on your shoulders, which are pushed forward, so that it lightly touches your throat, and keep your hands loose. Keep sinking to the bottom of the squat, which makes it easier to come back up.
Come up at once: push through your heels, hold your torso upright and your elbows high. Keep going until you are standing.

The jerk is the second phase and brings the weight overhead. You stand with the bar resting on the front of your shoulders and start with the dip. Set your feet straight below your hips and bend your knees, but do not let your hips travel back. Dip only a little, then change direction with as much power as you can.
Push through your heels and build as much speed and force as you can. Make sure to get your head out of the bar's way when it leaves your shoulders.

The moment your feet come off the floor, bring them into the receiving position as fast as you can. For the short time your feet are not pushing against the platform, your effort to push the bar up drives you down. Split your feet, one forward and one back. Catch the bar overhead with locked arms. Come back to standing.
Clean_and_Press: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees inside your arms. Keep your back flat and bend your knees and hips until you can take the bar with fully straight arms, in a pronated grip a little wider than your shoulders. Turn your elbows out to the sides. Keep the bar near your shins. Bring your shoulders over the bar or a little in front of it. Set your back flat. This is your starting position.

Start the pull by straightening your knees. Bring your hips forward and lift your shoulders at the same speed, so the angle of your back does not change. Keep lifting the bar straight up, close to your body.

Once the bar is past your knees, extend ankles, knees and hips with force, much like a jump. Keep guiding the bar with your hands while you do so: shrug your shoulders and use the momentum of the movement to pull the bar as high as you can. Keep the bar close to your body and your elbows out.

At the highest point your feet should leave the floor, and you begin to pull yourself under the bar. How exactly this works may change a little with the weight you use. Drop into a squat while you pull yourself under the bar.

When the bar reaches its highest point, turn your elbows around and under it. Rest the bar across the front of your shoulders, keep your torso upright and bend your hips and knees to absorb the bar's weight.
Rise to full height with the bar held in the clean position.
Keep your feet where they are, breathe out and press the bar overhead. Bring the bar down under control.
Clean_from_Blocks: Rest the barbell on boxes or stands at the height you want and grip it just outside your legs, overhand or with a hook grip. Drop your hips and put your weight on your heels. Keep a straight back, look ahead, lift your chest and set your shoulders slightly ahead of the bar. This is your starting position.
Start the first pull: push through your heels and straighten your knees. Do not change the angle of your back, and keep your arms straight with your elbows turned out.

Once you are fully extended, move into the receiving position: shrug hard and bend your arms, elbows high and out. Pull yourself down hard and turn your elbows under the bar while you do it. Catch the bar in a front squat; how deep depends on how high the bar was when the third pull ended. Rest the bar on your shoulders, which are pushed forward, so that it lightly touches your throat, and keep your hands loose. Keep sinking to the bottom of the squat, which makes it easier to come back up.
Come up at once: push through your heels, hold your torso upright and your elbows high. Keep going until you are standing. Put the weight back on the boxes for the next rep.
Clock_Push-Up: Get face down on the floor and carry your weight on your hands and toes.
Straighten your arms fully and set your hands about shoulder-width apart. Hold your body in a straight line for the whole movement. This is your starting position.
Bend your elbows to go down and bring your chest towards the floor.
At the bottom, change direction: straighten your elbows and push up as fast as you can, until you leave the floor. Try to "jump" 12-18 inches to one side.
While you speed up on the way up, move your outside foot away from the direction you travel in. As you leave the floor, turn your body by about 30 degrees for the next repetition.
Come back to the starting position and repeat. Work your way around the full circle until you are back at the point where you began.
Close-Grip_Barbell_Bench_Press: Lie down on a flat bench. Take the bar with a close grip, about shoulder-width, lift it out of the rack and hold it straight above you with locked arms. This is your starting position.

Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until it touches the middle of your chest. Tip: Unlike in a regular bench press, keep your elbows close to your torso the whole time, so the triceps work as much as possible.

Pause for a second, then breathe out and push the bar back to the starting position with your triceps. Lock your arms at the top, hold for a second and then start to lower slowly again. Tip: Going down should take at least twice as long as coming up.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.
Once finished, return the bar to the rack.
Close-Grip_Dumbbell_Press: Stand a dumbbell upright on a flat bench.

Make sure the dumbbell stays safely in place on top of the bench. Lie across the bench, at a right angle to it, with only your shoulders on the surface. Keep your hips lower than the bench, bend your legs and set your feet firmly on the floor.
Take the dumbbell with both hands and hold it straight above your chest with your arms extended. Press both palms against the underside of the dumbbell's sides. This is your starting position.
Bring the dumbbell down to your chest to start the movement.
Straighten your elbows to come back to the starting position.
Close-Grip_EZ-Bar_Curl_with_Band: Fix a band to each end of the bar. Pick up the bar and put one foot on the middle of the band. Stand upright and hold the EZ bar with a narrow, supinated grip. Keep your elbows close to your torso. This is your starting position.
Hold your upper arms in place and bend your elbows to curl. Breathe out while you lift the weight.
Keep curling until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is level with your shoulders. Stay there for a second and squeeze your biceps hard.
Breathe in and slowly lower the bar to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Close-Grip_EZ-Bar_Press: Load an EZ bar with a suitable weight and lie on a flat bench with it.
Lift the bar with a narrow grip and hold it straight above your torso, elbows in. Your arms should be at a right angle to the floor. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and bring the bar down to your lower chest. Keep your elbows in during the movement.
Breathe out and push the bar back up with your triceps: straighten your elbows until you are back in the starting position.
Close-Grip_EZ_Bar_Curl: Stand with an upright torso and hold an EZ curl bar at the inner, closer handles. Your palms face forward and, because of the bar's shape, tilt slightly inwards. Keep your elbows close to your torso. This is your starting position.
Keep your upper arms still, breathe out and curl the weight forward by contracting your biceps. Tip: Only your forearms should move.
Keep curling until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is level with your shoulders. Stay there for a second and squeeze your biceps hard.
Breathe in and slowly lower the bar to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Close-Grip_Front_Lat_Pulldown: Sit at a pulldown machine that has a wide bar on the top pulley. Adjust the knee pad of the machine to your height. The pads keep the resistance on the bar from lifting your body.

Take the bar with your palms facing forward, in the prescribed grip. Note on grips: For a wide grip, set your hands wider apart than your shoulders. For a medium grip, set them as far apart as your shoulders, and for a close grip narrower than your shoulders.

With both arms extended in front of you and the bar held at the grip width you chose, lean your torso back by about 30 degrees, arch your lower back and push your chest out. This is your starting position.

Breathe out and pull the bar down until it touches your upper chest; draw your shoulders and upper arms down and back to do so. Tip: Once you are fully contracted, focus on squeezing your back muscles. Your upper torso should stay still; only your arms should move. Your forearms should only hold the bar and do nothing else, so do not try to pull the bar down with them.

Hold the contraction for a second with your shoulder blades squeezed together. Then slowly let the bar rise to the starting position, where your arms are fully extended and your lats fully stretched. Breathe in during this part of the movement.
Do this motion again for the prescribed number of repetitions.
Close-Grip_Push-Up_off_of_a_Dumbbell: Get down on the floor and put your hands on a dumbbell standing upright. Carry your weight on your toes and hands, keep your torso rigid, your elbows in and your arms straight. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and lower your body by letting your elbows bend. Stay in a straight line; do not let your hips rise or sag.
Straighten your elbows to push yourself back up to the starting position. Breathe out during this step.
Pause in the contracted position, then repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.
Close-Grip_Standing_Barbell_Curl: Take a barbell in both hands with the palms turned up, a few inches between them.

Stand with a straight torso and your head up. Set your feet about shoulder-width apart and keep your elbows close to your torso. This is your starting position. Tip: Your upper arms and elbows stay still for the whole movement.

Curl the bar up in a half circle until your forearms touch your biceps. Breathe out during this part of the movement and squeeze your biceps hard for a second at the top. Tip: Do not bend your back or swing while you lift the weight. Only your forearms should move.
Breathe in and slowly lower back to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Cocoons: Lie on your back on the floor. Keep your legs straight and stretch your arms out behind your head. This is your starting position.

For the movement, pull your knees towards your chest and tilt your pelvis so your glutes lift off the floor. Round your spine while you do so and bring your arms back over your head, so that you crunch at the same time.
Pause briefly, then go back to the starting position.
Conans_Wheel: Once the weight is loaded, take the end of the implement in a Zercher hold. Rest the bar in the crook of your elbows and hold on to your wrist. Try not to let the weight rest on your forearms.

Start by lifting the weight off the ground. Stay tight and upright while you begin to walk in short, fast steps. Look up and away while you turn in a circle. Do not hold your breath during the event. Keep walking until you have completed one full turn or more.
Concentration_Curls: Take a seat on a flat bench, a dumbbell on the floor in front of you between your legs. Spread your legs, knees bent, feet on the floor.

Pick the dumbbell up with your right arm. Rest the back of your right upper arm on top of the inside of your right thigh. Turn your palm until it faces forward, away from your thigh. Tip: Keep your arm extended and the dumbbell above the floor. This is your starting position.

Keep your upper arm still, breathe out and curl the weight forward by contracting your biceps. Only your forearm should move. Keep curling until your biceps is fully contracted and the dumbbell is level with your shoulder. Tip: At the top, make sure your little finger is higher than your thumb. That ensures a good contraction. Stay in the contracted position for a second and squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and slowly lower the dumbbell to the starting position. Caution: Do not swing at any time.
Do the recommended number of repetitions, then do the same with the left arm.
Cross-Body_Crunch: On your back, lying flat, bend the knees about 60 degrees.
With your feet flat on the floor, put your hands loosely behind your head. You start from here.

Now curl up and bring your right elbow and shoulder across your body; at the same time, pull your left knee in towards your left shoulder. Reach with your elbow and try to touch the knee. Breathe out during this movement. Tip: Try to lift your shoulder towards the knee, not only the elbow. What matters is to contract your abs during the movement, not merely to move the elbow.
Breathe in and lower back to the starting position. Then repeat with your left elbow and your right knee.
Keep alternating like this until you have done all prescribed repetitions.
Cross_Body_Hammer_Curl: Stand upright and hold a dumbbell in each hand. Let your hands hang at your sides, palms facing in.

Keep your palms facing in and do not twist your arm. Breathe out and curl the dumbbell in your right hand up towards your left shoulder. Touch your shoulder with the top of the dumbbell and hold the contraction for a second.
Breathe in and slowly lower the dumbbell the same way it came up. Then do the same movement with your left arm.
Keep alternating like this until each arm has done the recommended number of repetitions.
Cross_Over_-_With_Bands: Fasten an exercise band around a fixed post.
Turn your back to the post, take the handles at both ends of the band and step far enough forward to put tension on the band.

Lift your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor and at a right angle to your torso, so that torso and arms look like the letter "T". Your palms face forward. Keep your arms extended with a slight bend at the elbows. This is your starting position.
Keep your arms straight, breathe out and bring them forward across your chest in a half circle while you tense your pecs. Hold the contraction for a second.
Breathe in and slowly go back to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Crossover_Reverse_Lunge: Take a shoulder-width stance; you start from here.
Do a rear lunge: take one foot back and bend your hips and your front knee. While you do so, turn your torso across your front leg.
Pause briefly, go back to the starting position and repeat on the other side. Keep alternating.
Crucifix: In the crucifix you hold weights still out to your sides for time. You can practise the event with dumbbells, but it is best to practise with one of the implements actually used, such as axes and hammers, because it feels different.

Start standing and lift your arms out to the sides with the implements in your hands. Keep your arms parallel to the ground. In competition, judges or sensors tell you when you drop below parallel. Hold for as long as you can. Usually the weights should be heavy enough for you to fail within 30-60 seconds.
Crunch_-_Hands_Overhead: Lie on the floor with a flat back and bend your knees so that hamstrings and calves form an angle of about 60 degrees.
With your feet flat on the floor, reach your arms overhead and cross your palms. You start from here.

Curl your upper body forward until your shoulder blades are just off the floor. Keep your arms in line with your head, neck and shoulders the whole time. Do not move them forward out of that line. Breathe out during this part of the movement and hold the contraction for a second.
Breathe in and slowly lower to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Crunch_-_Legs_On_Exercise_Ball: Lie on your back, flat, knees bent at a 90 degree angle and feet resting on an exercise ball.
Set the feet three to four inches apart, toes turned inward until they touch.
With your elbows in, rest your hands lightly at the sides of your head. Tip: Do not lock the fingers behind your head.
To isolate the abdominal muscles better, press the small of your back down into the floor. You start from here.

Start rolling your shoulders off the floor and keep pressing your lower back down as hard as you can. Your shoulders should rise only about four inches from the floor, and your lower back should stay on the floor. Breathe out during this part of the movement. At the top of the contraction, squeeze your abdominals hard and hold for a second. Tip: Concentrate on moving slowly and under control. Never use momentum.
Breathe in and slowly lower to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Crunches: Lie flat on your back, either with your feet flat on the ground or with your feet on a bench and your knees bent to 90 degrees. With your feet on a bench, set them three to four inches apart and turn your toes in until they touch.
Next, rest your hands lightly at the sides of your head, elbows kept in. Tip: Fingers should not be locked behind the head.
Press the small of your back into the floor to isolate your abdominals better, and start rolling your shoulders off the floor.

Keep pressing your lower back down as hard as you can while you contract your abdominals and breathe out. Your shoulders should rise only about four inches from the floor, and your lower back should stay on the floor. At the top, squeeze your abdominals hard and hold the contraction for a second. Tip: Concentrate on moving slowly and under control - using momentum only cheats yourself.
After holding for one second, breathe in and slowly come down to the starting position again.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Cuban_Press: Stand and hold a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated grip. Lift your upper arms until they are parallel to the floor and let your forearms hang down in the "scarecrow" position. This is your starting position.

To start the movement, rotate your shoulders outwards so the arm turns through 180 degrees. Keep your upper arms where they are and rotate until your wrists are straight above your elbows and your forearms are at a right angle to the floor.
Now press the dumbbells up: extend your elbows until your arms are straight overhead.
Breathe in and go back to the starting position by doing the steps in reverse.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Dancers_Stretch: Take an upright seat on the floor.
With the knee kept bent, cross the right leg over the left, which stays straight and down on the floor.
Rest your right hand on the floor and lay your left arm on the right leg.
Turn your upper body to the right and stay there for 10-20 seconds, then change sides.
Dead_Bug: Lie on your back and stretch your hands up towards the ceiling.
Raise feet, knees and hips until each is at 90 degrees.

Breathe out hard to pull your ribcage down and press your back flat on the floor; tilt your pelvis up and squeeze your glutes. Keep this position for the whole movement. This is your starting position.
Start the exercise by reaching one leg out: straighten the knee and hip until the leg is just above the floor.
Keep your lumbar spine and pelvis in position during the movement, because your back will want to arch.
Staying tight, bring the working leg back to where it started.
Do the same on the other side and alternate until the set is done.
Deadlift_with_Bands: Short bands are simply looped over the bar before you begin; step into them as you set up for the deadlift. Long bands have to be anchored to something secure, for example a rack or heavy dumbbells.

Once your feet and your grip are set, take a big breath, then drop your hips and bend your knees until your shins touch the bar. Look ahead, keep your chest up and your back arched, and start pushing through your heels to move the weight up. When the bar is past your knees, pull it back hard: squeeze your shoulder blades together while you push your hips forward into the bar.
Bring the bar down by hinging at the hips, and steer it to the ground.
Deadlift_with_Chains: Fix the chains to the sleeves of the bar, or simply drape their middle over the bar, so that the weight grows more as you lift.

Step up to the bar so that it is centred over your feet. Set your feet about hip-width apart. Bend at the hips and grip the bar shoulder-width apart; let your shoulder blades move forward. Usually you take an overhand grip, or a mixed grip with one hand over and one under for heavier sets. Once your feet and your grip are set, take a big breath, then drop your hips and bend your knees until your shins touch the bar.

Look ahead, keep your chest up and your back arched, and start pushing through your heels to move the weight up. When the bar is past your knees, pull it back hard: squeeze your shoulder blades together while you push your hips forward into the bar.
Hinge at the hips so the bar comes down, steering it until it reaches the ground.
Decline_Barbell_Bench_Press: Hook your legs under the pads at the foot of a decline bench, then ease yourself back until you are lying down.

Take the bar with a medium-width grip, one that puts your forearms and upper arms at a 90-degree angle halfway through the movement. Unrack it and hold it directly above you with locked arms, which should be at a right angle to the floor. That's your starting position. Tip: To spare your rotator cuff, ask a spotter to help you get the barbell out of the rack.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until it touches your lower chest.

Pause for a second, then breathe out and drive the bar back up to the starting position with your chest muscles. Lock your arms, squeeze your chest at the top for a second, and then begin to lower slowly again. Tip: The way down should last at least twice as long as the way up.
Do the prescribed number of repetitions.
Once you have finished, set the bar back in the rack.
Decline_Close-Grip_Bench_To_Skull_Crushe: Hook your legs under the pads at the foot of a decline bench, then ease yourself back until you are lying down.

Take the bar with a close grip, a little narrower than shoulder width. Unrack it and hold it directly above you with locked arms and your elbows tucked in. Your arms should be at a right angle to the floor. That's your starting position. Tip: To spare your rotator cuff, ask a spotter to help you get the barbell out of the rack.
Breathe in and bring the bar down to your lower chest. Keep your elbows tucked in the whole way.
Breathe out and press the bar up to the starting position again, letting your triceps do the pushing.

Hold your upper arms still and breathe in while you lower the bar slowly: swing your forearms towards you in a half circle until the bar lightly touches your forehead. Keep breathing in during this part.
Tighten your triceps and breathe out to raise the bar to the starting position again.
Go through steps 3-6 again until you have done the recommended number of repetitions.
Decline_Crunch: Hook your legs under the pads at the foot of a decline bench and lie back.
Next, with your elbows in, let your hands rest lightly at the sides of your head. Tip: Fingers are not to be locked behind the head.
Press the small of your back into the bench so that your abdominals work in isolation, and start curling your shoulders up from the bench.

Keep pressing your lower back down as hard as possible while you tighten your abdominals and breathe out. Lift your shoulders only about four inches; your lower back stays on the bench. At the top, squeeze your abdominals hard for a second. Tip: Move slowly and under control. Using momentum only cheats you of the work.
When the one-second squeeze is over, breathe in and lower yourself slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Decline_Dumbbell_Bench_Press: Hook your legs under the pads at the foot of a decline bench and lie back, holding one dumbbell in each hand on your thighs. Your palms face each other.
Lying down now, bring the dumbbells to shoulder width in front of you.
From there, turn your wrists forward until your palms point away from you. That's your starting position.
Breathe out and lower the weights slowly to your sides. Stay in full control of the dumbbells the whole time. Tip: Your forearms should stay at a right angle to the floor during the entire motion.

Breathe out and press the dumbbells up with your chest muscles. Lock your arms at the top, squeeze your chest for a second, and then begin to lower slowly. Tip: The way down should last at least twice as long as the way up.
Do the number of repetitions your training program prescribes.
Decline_Dumbbell_Flyes: Hook your legs under the pads at the foot of a decline bench and lie back, holding one dumbbell in each hand on your thighs. Your palms face each other.

When you are lying down, bring the dumbbells up in front of you, shoulder width apart. Your palms face each other, and your arms are fully stretched and at a right angle to the floor. That's your starting position.

Bend your elbows slightly to keep strain off the biceps tendon, then open your arms to both sides in a wide arc until your chest feels a stretch. Breathe in during this part. Tip: The arms themselves stay fixed throughout; only the shoulder joint moves.
Squeeze your chest muscles and breathe out while you bring your arms up to the starting position again. Tip: Follow the same arc you used on the way down.
Stay in the contracted position for a second, then do the prescribed number of repetitions.
Decline_Dumbbell_Triceps_Extension: Hook your legs under the pads at the foot of a decline bench and lie back, holding one dumbbell in each hand on your thighs. Your palms face each other.

When you are lying down, bring the dumbbells up in front of you, shoulder width apart. Your palms face each other, and your arms are fully stretched and at a right angle to the floor. That's your starting position.

Hold your upper arms still with your elbows in and breathe in while you lower the dumbbells slowly: swing your forearms towards you in a half circle until your thumbs are beside your ears. Keep breathing in during this part.
Tighten your triceps and breathe out to raise the dumbbells to the starting position again.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Decline_EZ_Bar_Triceps_Extension: Hook your legs under the pads at the foot of a decline bench, then ease yourself back until you are lying down.

Take the EZ bar with a close grip, a little narrower than shoulder width. Unrack it and hold it directly above you with locked arms and your elbows tucked in. Your arms should be at a right angle to the floor. That's your starting position. Tip: To spare your rotator cuff, ask a spotter to help you get the bar out of the rack.

Hold your upper arms still and breathe in while you lower the bar slowly: swing your forearms towards you in a half circle until the bar lightly touches your forehead. Keep breathing in during this part.
Tighten your triceps and breathe out to raise the bar to the starting position again.
Carry on until you have done the recommended number of repetitions.
Decline_Oblique_Crunch: Hook your legs under the pads at the foot of a decline bench, then ease yourself back until you are lying down.
Measured from the floor, your torso should end up at about 35-45 degrees: lift your upper body off the bench that far.
One hand goes beside your head, the other on your thigh. You start from here.

From there, lift your upper body slowly and turn your torso to the left. Breathe out and keep curling up until your right elbow meets your left knee. Stay in this contracted position for a second. Tip: Keep your abs tight and the movement slow and controlled.
Breathe in and lower your body slowly to the starting position.
When you have done one set of the recommended repetitions on the right, change to your left side. Tip: Concentrate on truly twisting your torso and on feeling the contraction at the top.
Decline_Push-Up: Lie face down on the floor, set your hands about 36 inches apart and hold your torso up on straight arms. Put your feet up on a box or bench. That's your starting position.
Breathe in and lower your body until your chest is just above the floor.
Next, exhale and push your upper body back up to where you started, squeezing the chest as you go.
Pause briefly in the contracted position at the top, then lower yourself again and do as many repetitions as you need.
Decline_Reverse_Crunch: Lie back on a decline bench and grip the top of it with both hands. Make sure your body does not slide down from there.
Use your abs to keep your legs parallel to the floor, with knees and feet together. Tip: Stretch your legs out fully, leaving only a slight bend in the knees. That's your starting position.
Breathe out and draw your legs towards your torso while you roll your pelvis backwards and lift your hips from the bench. When the movement ends, your knees touch your chest.
Stay contracted for a second, then breathe in and return your legs to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Decline_Smith_Press: Set a decline bench under the Smith machine. Put the bar at a height you can reach lying down with your arms nearly straight. Take a pronated grip wider than shoulder width, unlock the bar and hold it directly above you with straight arms. That's your starting position.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the bar under control until it lightly touches your torso.
Pause briefly, then straighten your elbows to return the bar to the starting position, breathing out on the way.
Do the prescribed number of repetitions.
At the end of the set, lock the bar into the rack again.
Deficit_Deadlift: Set up a platform or weight plates to stand on, usually 1-3 inches high. Step up to the bar so that it sits over the middle of your feet, which are roughly hip width apart. Hinge at the hips and grip the bar at shoulder width, letting your shoulder blades move forward. Normally you take an overhand grip, or a mixed grip for heavier sets.

Once your feet and grip are set, take a deep breath, then drop your hips and bend your knees until your shins touch the bar. Look ahead, keep your chest up and your back arched, and push through your heels to start lifting the weight. When the bar has cleared your knees, pull it back forcefully: squeeze your shoulder blades together and drive your hips forward into the bar.
To lower, hinge at the hips and guide the bar down to the floor.
Depth_Jump_Leap: You need two boxes or benches for this drill: one 12 to 16 inches high, the other 22 to 26 inches high.
Stand on one of the boxes with your arms at your sides, your feet together and slightly over the edge. Set the other box about two or three feet in front of you, facing you.
Step off the first box, land on both feet and take off from both feet in the same instant.
Rebound up and forward as hard as you can, using your arms and a full stretch of your body to jump onto the higher box. Let your legs absorb the landing again.
Dip_Machine: Sit firmly in the dip machine, choose the weight and take a tight hold of the handles.
Keep your elbows in by your sides so that the triceps do most of the work. Your elbows should be bent to 90 degrees.
Tighten your triceps and breathe out while you push your arms down until they are straight. Tip: At the bottom, leave a small bend in your arms so the triceps stay under tension.
Breathe in and let your arms rise slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Dips_-_Chest_Version: You need a set of parallel bars. To reach the starting position, support your body above the bars on straight, locked arms.
Breathe in and lower yourself slowly, leaning your torso forward by about 30 degrees and letting your elbows flare out a little, until your chest feels a slight stretch.
When you feel that stretch, breathe out and use your chest to lift your body to the starting position again. Tip: Squeeze your chest for a second at the top.
Do the prescribed number of repetitions.
Dips_-_Triceps_Version: To reach the starting position, support your body above the bars on straight arms that are almost locked.

Breathe in and lower yourself slowly. Keep your torso upright and your elbows close to your body, which puts more of the work on the triceps. Go down until your upper arms and forearms form a 90-degree angle.
Breathe out and press your torso up with your triceps until you are in the starting position again.
Do the prescribed number of repetitions.
Donkey_Calf_Raises: You need a donkey calf raise machine. Begin by placing your lower back and hips under its padded lever. The pad should rest on the area of your tailbone.

Hold the side handles with both arms and set the balls of your feet on the calf block so that your heels hang over the edge. Point your toes forward, inward or outward, depending on which area you want to work, and straighten your knees without locking them. That's your starting position.

Breathe out and lift your heels: extend your ankles as far up as you can and flex your calves. Keep your knees still the whole time; they must not bend at any point. Stay in the contracted position for a second before you go down.
Breathe in and return slowly to the starting position: let your heels sink and your ankles bend until your calves are stretched.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Double_Kettlebell_Alternating_Hang_Clean: Two kettlebells go between your feet. Send your butt back with your eyes straight ahead, and you are in the starting position.
Clean one kettlebell up to your shoulder while you keep hold of the other one.
In one fluid motion, bring the upper kettlebell down and drive the lower kettlebell up.
Double_Kettlebell_Jerk: Take one kettlebell in each hand, gripping it by the handle.

Clean the kettlebells to your shoulders: extend your legs and hips and pull the weights up towards your shoulders. Turn your wrists on the way so that your palms face forward. That's your starting position.
Bend your knees to dip your body, with your torso kept upright.
Change direction at once and push through your heels, in effect jumping to build momentum.
At the same time, straighten your arms and press the kettlebells overhead to lockout, letting the momentum of your body move the weights.
Land with your feet split, one in front and one behind.
With the weights still overhead, stand up and bring your feet together. Lower the weights for the next repetition.
Double_Kettlebell_Push_Press: Bring two kettlebells to your shoulders with a clean.
Dip into a squat of a few inches and quickly reverse the movement. Let the momentum of your legs drive the kettlebells overhead.
When your arms are locked out, bring the kettlebells down to your shoulders and repeat.
Double_Kettlebell_Snatch: Set two kettlebells behind your feet. To pick them up, bend the knees and sit back.
Forcefully swing the kettlebells through between your legs, then reverse the direction.
Drive your hips through and lock the kettlebells out overhead in a single unbroken motion.
Double_Kettlebell_Windmill: Set one kettlebell in front of your front foot, then clean and press another kettlebell overhead with the opposite arm. To clean it to your shoulder, extend your legs and hips and pull the kettlebell up towards your shoulders. Turn your wrist on the way so that your palm faces forward.

Keep the overhead kettlebell locked out the whole time and push your hips out towards the side of that kettlebell. Turn your feet out at a forty-five degree angle away from the arm holding the locked-out kettlebell.
Hinge at the hip to one side with your hips pushed out, and lean slowly until you can pick up the kettlebell from the floor. Keep your eyes on the kettlebell above your head the whole time.
Once you have picked the kettlebell up, pause for a second, then reverse the movement until you are in the starting position again.
Double_Leg_Butt_Kick: Stand with a slight bend in your knees.
Drop quickly into a shallow squat by bending your hips and knees, then extend at once and jump as high as you can.
On the way up, bend your knees to tuck your heels and try to touch your buttocks with them.
Land with your knees only partly bent and let your legs absorb the impact.
Downward_Facing_Balance: On top of an exercise ball, lie face down.
With your stomach resting on the ball, walk the hands forward on the floor and raise your legs, straightening elbows and knees.
Drag_Curl: Take a barbell with a supinated grip (palms facing forward), and bring the elbows back and close to your torso. You start from here.

Breathe out and curl the bar up while your elbows stay back: 'drag' the bar upwards so that it touches your torso the whole way. Tip: Your elbows are not pinned to your sides here; you move them backwards instead. Do not raise your shoulders either.
Return slowly to the starting position, with the bar touching your torso all the way.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Drop_Push: Set up low boxes or other platforms with 2-3 feet between them.
Get into a push-up position between them, with your hands on the boxes holding you up.
Keeping good posture, push up and drop from the platforms, bringing your hands in to shoulder width. Cushion the landing by absorbing the impact with your arms.
Dumbbell_Alternate_Bicep_Curl: Stand with your torso upright and one dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight. Keep your elbows close to your torso and your palms turned towards your thighs.

Hold your upper arm still and curl the right weight, turning your palm until it faces forward. From there, breathe out and keep tightening the biceps until it is fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level. Stay there for a second and squeeze the biceps. Tip: Nothing but the forearm should move.
Breathe in and slowly lower the dumbbell to the starting position. Tip: Turn your palm back on the way down so that it faces your thigh again, as at the start.
Do the same with your left hand. Both sides together count as one repetition.
Keep alternating like this until you have done the recommended number of repetitions.
Dumbbell_Bench_Press: Lie back on a flat bench, holding one dumbbell in each hand on your thighs. Your palms face each other.
Give the dumbbells a push with your thighs and bring them up one after the other, until you hold them in front of you at shoulder width.

From there, turn your wrists forward until your palms point away from you. The dumbbells sit just beside your chest, and your upper arms and forearms form a 90-degree angle. Stay in full control of the dumbbells the whole time. That's your starting position.

Breathe out and press the dumbbells up with your chest. Lock your arms at the top, squeeze your chest for a second, and then begin to lower slowly. Tip: Ideally, the way down lasts about twice as long as the way up.
Do the number of repetitions your training program prescribes.
Dumbbell_Bench_Press_with_Neutral_Grip: Lie back on a flat bench holding one dumbbell per hand. Pull your shoulder blades back and plant your feet flat on the floor.
Hold a neutral grip, with your palms facing each other, and start with your arms stretched straight above you at a right angle to the floor. That's your starting position.
Start the movement by bending your elbows and letting your upper arms sink out to the sides. Go down until the dumbbells are level with your torso.
Pause, then straighten your elbows and come back to the starting position.
Dumbbell_Bicep_Curl: Stand tall with one dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight. Hold your elbows close to your torso and turn your palms until they face forward. That's your starting position.

Keep your upper arms still, breathe out and curl the weights by tightening your biceps. Carry on lifting until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Pause briefly there and squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and slowly bring the dumbbells down to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Dumbbell_Clean: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and one dumbbell in each hand.
Bend your hips and knees and push your hips back to lower the weights until they reach the floor. That's your starting position.

Start the movement with an explosive jump upward: extend your hips, knees and ankles to accelerate the weights. Hold the dumbbells with a neutral grip and keep your arms straight until your body is fully extended.
Once fully extended, bend your hips and knees again and catch the weights in a squat. Let your arms bend and guide the dumbbells to your shoulders.
Having caught the weights in the squat, straighten your hips and knees and finish standing, with the dumbbells on your shoulders.
Dumbbell_Floor_Press: Lie on the floor with a dumbbell in each hand. You may bend your knees. Start with your arms fully stretched and the weights above you.
Bring the weights down until your upper arms touch the floor. Tuck your elbows in to emphasise triceps size and strength, or angle your arms out to the sides to focus on your chest.
Pause at the bottom, then straighten your elbows and bring the weights together at the top.
Dumbbell_Flyes: Lie back on a flat bench, holding one dumbbell in each hand on your thighs. Your palms face each other.

Give the dumbbells a push with your thighs and bring them up one after the other, until you hold them in front of you at shoulder width with your palms facing each other. Raise them as if you were pressing them, but stop and hold just short of lockout. That's your starting position.

Bend your elbows slightly to keep strain off the biceps tendon, then open your arms to both sides in a wide arc until your chest feels a stretch. Breathe in during this part. Tip: The arms themselves stay fixed throughout; only the shoulder joint moves.
Squeeze your chest muscles and breathe out while you bring your arms up to the starting position again. Tip: Follow the same arc you used on the way down.
Stay in the contracted position for a second, then do the prescribed number of repetitions.
Dumbbell_Incline_Row: Lean forward against an incline bench, ready to take a neutral grip.
Pick up one dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip and start with straight arms. That's your starting position.
Pull your shoulder blades back and bend your elbows to row the dumbbells up to your sides.
Pause at the top, then go back to the starting position.
Dumbbell_Incline_Shoulder_Raise: Sit on an incline bench with one dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.

Raise your legs to kick the weights up to your shoulders, and lean back. Hold the dumbbells above your shoulders with straight arms. Your arms are at a right angle to the floor, your palms face forward and your knuckles point to the ceiling. That's your starting position.
With your arms straight and locked, breathe out and lift the dumbbells by raising your shoulders off the bench.
Breathe in and return the dumbbells to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Dumbbell_Lunges: Stand with an upright torso and a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. That's your starting position.

Take a step forward with your right leg, about 2 feet in front of the foot that stays behind, and lower your upper body, keeping your torso upright and your balance steady. Breathe in on the way down. Note: Do not let your knee travel forward past your toes when you go down, because that puts needless stress on the knee joint. Keep your front shin at a right angle to the ground.
Push off, mostly through your heel, and breathe out while you come back to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions, then do the same with your left leg.
Dumbbell_Lying_One-Arm_Rear_Lateral_Rais: Hold a dumbbell in one hand and lie chest down on an adjustable bench set to a slight incline, about 15 degrees measured from the floor. You can grip the leg of the bench with your free hand for stability.
Turn the hand with the dumbbell to a neutral position, palm facing your torso, and keep that arm extended with a slight bend in the elbow. That's your starting position.

Breathe out and lift the arm with the dumbbell out to the side until your elbow reaches shoulder height and your arm is about parallel to the floor. Tip: Keep the arm at a right angle to your torso and extended during the whole movement. Also stay contracted for a second at the top.
Breathe in and slowly bring the dumbbell down to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Dumbbell_Lying_Pronation: Lie face down on a flat bench. Hold a dumbbell with one arm and fold the other hand on the bench so that your head can rest on it.
Bend the elbow of the arm with the dumbbell until your upper arm and forearm form a 90-degree angle.

Lift the upper arm until your forearm is at a right angle to the floor and your upper arm is at a right angle to your torso. Tip: Your upper arm should be parallel to the floor and also form a 90-degree angle with your torso. That's your starting position.

Breathe out and rotate your forearm outward so that the dumbbell rises forward, keeping the 90-degree bend between upper arm and forearm. Carry on with this outward rotation until your forearm is parallel to the floor, then stay contracted for a second.
Breathe in and return slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Dumbbell_Lying_Rear_Lateral_Raise: Set an adjustable bench to a slight incline, about 15 degrees from the floor, and lie on it chest down with a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang extended with a small bend in the elbows and turn your hands to a neutral grip, palms toward your torso. This is your starting position.

Breathe out and lift your arms out to the sides until the elbows reach shoulder height and the arms are about parallel to the floor. Tip: Keep the arms extended and at a right angle to your torso the whole way. Hold the squeeze at the top for one second.
Breathe in and bring the dumbbells down slowly to where you started.
Do the recommended number of repetitions, then change to the other arm.
Dumbbell_Lying_Supination: Lie on your side on a flat bench. Hold a dumbbell in one hand, and fold the other arm on the bench so your head can rest on it.
Bend the elbow of the working arm until upper arm and forearm form a 90-degree angle.

Lift the upper arm until the forearm is parallel to the floor and at a right angle to your torso (Tip: The forearm then points straight out in front of you). The upper arm stays still against your torso, parallel to the floor and in line with your torso at all times. This is your starting position.

Breathe out and rotate the forearm outward, so the dumbbell travels upward in a half circle while the elbow keeps its 90 degree bend. Keep rotating until the forearm points to the ceiling, perpendicular to the floor and to your torso. Hold the squeeze there for one second.
Breathe in and return slowly to the starting position.
Complete the recommended number of repetitions, then change arms.
Dumbbell_One-Arm_Shoulder_Press: With a dumbbell in hand, either stand up straight or sit down, resting the dumbbells upright on your thighs; for sitting, use a military press bench or a utility bench with back support.
Clean the dumbbell to shoulder height. Your free hand can stay stretched out to the side, rest at your waist or hold on to something fixed.
Turn your wrist until the palm faces forward. This is your starting position.
Breathe out and press the dumbbell overhead until the arm is completely straight.
Pause for a second, then breathe in and lower it slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions, then change arms.
Dumbbell_One-Arm_Triceps_Extension: Pick up a dumbbell. You can sit on a military press bench or a utility bench with back support, the dumbbell standing upright on your thigh, or you can stand up straight.

Clean the dumbbell to shoulder height, then straighten the arm overhead so the whole arm is perpendicular to the floor and beside your head, with the dumbbell above you. Your free hand can stay stretched out to the side, rest at your waist, support the upper arm of the working side or hold on to something fixed.
Turn your wrist so the palm faces forward and the little finger points to the ceiling. This is your starting position.
Keep the upper arm still and lower the dumbbell slowly behind your head while you breathe in. Pause once the triceps is fully stretched.
Breathe out and tighten the triceps to bring the dumbbell back to the starting position. Tip: Only the forearm may move. The upper arm stays still beside your head the whole time.
Do the recommended number of repetitions, then change arms.
Dumbbell_One-Arm_Upright_Row: Take a dumbbell and stand tall with a straight back, the arm extended in front of you and the elbow slightly bent. This is your starting position. Tip: Let the dumbbell rest on the front of your thigh, palm turned toward the thigh.
Your other hand can stay stretched out to the side, rest at your waist or hold on to something fixed. This is your starting position.

Breathe out and raise the dumbbell with the side of your shoulder, keeping it close to your body on the way up. Lift until it is almost level with your chin. Tip: Lead the movement with the elbow, which stays higher than the forearm throughout the lift. Keep your torso still and pause for one second at the top.
Bring the dumbbell slowly back down to the starting position, breathing in as you do.
Do the recommended number of repetitions, then change arms.
Dumbbell_Prone_Incline_Curl: Take a dumbbell in each hand and lie chest down on an incline bench, shoulders close to the top end. Rest your knees on the seat, or straddle the bench with your legs out to the sides.
Let your arms hang straight down in front of you, perpendicular to the floor.
Keep the elbows tucked in at your sides and turn the palms to face forward. This is your starting position.
Tighten the biceps and curl the dumbbells up until the arms are fully bent, breathing out as you lift. Move only the forearms; the upper arms stay still the whole time.
Bring the dumbbells down until your arms are straight again.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Dumbbell_Raise: Take a dumbbell in each hand and stand tall with a straight back, arms extended at your sides and elbows slightly bent. This is your starting position. Tip: The dumbbells sit beside your thighs, palms turned to the rear.

Breathe out and raise the dumbbells with the side of your shoulders, keeping them at the sides of your body on the way up. Lift until they are almost level with your chin. Tip: Lead with the elbows, which stay higher than the forearms throughout the lift. Keep your torso still and pause for one second at the top.
Bring the dumbbells slowly back down to the starting position, breathing in as you do.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Dumbbell_Rear_Lunge: Stand with an upright torso and a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. This is your starting position.

Take a step back with the right leg, roughly two feet behind the left foot, and sink down while your torso stays upright and you keep your balance. Breathe in on the way down. Tip: Do not let the front knee travel past your toes as you descend, because that loads the knee joint more than it should. Keep the front shin perpendicular to the ground. Stay upright through the whole lunge; flexible hip flexors matter here. A long step works the gluteus maximus more, a short step the quadriceps.
Breathe out, push yourself up and come back to the starting position. Tip: Push off the ball of the foot to stress the quadriceps. Press through the heel to target the glutes instead.
Then do the same with the other leg.
Dumbbell_Scaption: This is a corrective exercise that builds strength in the muscles stabilizing the shoulder blade. Let a light weight hang in each hand at your sides, thumbs pointing up.
Start by lifting your arms forward at an angle of about 30 degrees away from the center. Keep the arms completely straight during the movement.
Raise them until they are parallel to the ground, then lower them back to the start.
Dumbbell_Seated_Box_Jump: Set a box a couple of feet to the side of a bench. Sit on the bench facing the box and hold a dumbbell against your chest with both hands. This is your starting position.
Press your feet firmly into the ground, lean forward and jump up and forward by extending your hips and knees.
Land with both feet on the box and let your hips and knees bend to soften the impact.
Step back down and sit in the starting position again.
Dumbbell_Seated_One-Leg_Calf_Raise: About 12 inches from a flat bench, set a block on the floor.
Seated on a flat bench, rest a dumbbell roughly 3 inches above the knee on your upper left thigh.
Next, the ball of your left foot goes on the block. You start from here.
Breathe out and rise onto your toes as high as you can by tightening the calf. Hold the squeeze for one second.
Come back down slowly to the starting position and let the calf stretch as low as it will go.
Once the prescribed number of repetitions is done, switch to the right leg.
Dumbbell_Shoulder_Press: Sit on a military press bench or a utility bench with back support, a dumbbell in each hand. Stand the dumbbells upright on your thighs.
Bring the dumbbells up to shoulder height one after the other, kicking each into place with the help of your thigh.
Turn your wrists so both palms face forward. This is your starting position.
Breathe out and press the dumbbells up until they touch overhead.
Pause briefly in the contracted position at the top, then breathe in and lower the weights slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Dumbbell_Shrug: Stand upright with your arms straight at your sides and a dumbbell in each hand, palms turned toward your torso.

Breathe out and pull your shoulders up as high as they go to lift the dumbbells. Hold the squeeze at the top for one second. Tip: Keep the arms straight the whole time and do not let the biceps help with the lift. Nothing but the shoulders moves up and down.
Let the dumbbells come back down to where they started.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Dumbbell_Side_Bend: Stand tall with a dumbbell in your left hand, palm toward your torso, and your right hand on your waist. Set your feet shoulder width apart. This is your starting position.

With a straight back and your head up, bend to the right as far as you can, moving only at the waist. Breathe in while you bend. Hold for one second, then breathe out and straighten up to the starting position. Tip: The rest of your body stays still.
Do the same movement again, this time bending to the left. Hold for one second and return to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions, then move the dumbbell to the other hand.
Dumbbell_Squat: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms turned toward the sides of your legs.

Take a medium stance with your feet shoulder width apart and the toes turned out a little. Keep your head up the whole time, because looking down throws you off balance, and keep your back straight. This is your starting position. Note: This medium stance trains the legs as a whole; you can use any of the three stance widths instead.

Bend your knees and lower your torso slowly, staying upright with your head up. Go down until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Tip: Done correctly, the front of each knee stays on an imaginary vertical line with the toes. If the knees move beyond that line, past the toes, the knee is under more stress than it should be and the repetition was done wrongly.
Breathe out and rise again by pushing mainly through your heels into the floor, straightening the legs until you are back in the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Dumbbell_Squat_To_A_Bench: Stand tall with a flat bench behind you and a dumbbell in each hand, palms turned toward the sides of your legs.

Set your feet shoulder width apart in a medium stance, toes turned out a little. Your head stays up at all times, since a downward look costs you your balance, and your back stays straight. This is your starting position. Note: The medium stance works the legs as a whole; any of the three stance widths can be used in its place.

Bend your knees and lower your torso slowly, staying upright with your head up. Go down until you lightly touch the bench behind you. Breathe in during this part. Tip: Done correctly, the front of each knee stays on an imaginary vertical line with the toes. If the knees move beyond that line, past the toes, the knee is under more stress than it should be and the repetition was done wrongly.
Breathe out and come up by pushing mainly through your heels into the floor, straightening the legs until you are back in the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Dumbbell_Step_Ups: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms turned toward the sides of your legs.

Set your right foot on the raised platform. Step up by straightening the hip and knee of the right leg, driving mostly through the heel to lift your body, and bring the left foot onto the platform too. Breathe out during the effort of coming up.
Breathe in and step down with the left leg by bending the hip and knee of the right leg. Then set the right foot beside the left to stand as you did at the start.
Do the recommended number of repetitions leading with the right leg, then do them with the left.
Dumbbell_Tricep_Extension_-Pronated_Grip: Holding two dumbbells directly above your shoulders, lie on a flat bench. Extend the arms fully so they are at a 90 degree angle to your torso and the floor.
Turn your palms to face forward and keep the elbows tucked in. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbells slowly until they are close to your ears. The upper arms stay still and the elbows stay tucked in.
After that, breathe out and bring the weight back to where it started with your triceps.
Dynamic_Back_Stretch: Take a standing position, feet shoulder width apart. This is where you start.
With straight arms, swing them forward and up 5-10 times. Make each swing a little bigger until your arms reach above your head.
Dynamic_Chest_Stretch: Stand with your arms stretched straight out in front of you and your hands together. This is your starting position.
Keep the arms straight, pull them quickly back as far as they go and bring them together again, like a very wide clap. Do this 5-10 times and get faster as you go.
EZ-Bar_Curl: Stand tall and hold an EZ curl bar by the wide outer grips. Your palms face forward, tilted slightly inward by the shape of the bar. Tuck your elbows close to your torso. This is your starting position.
Keep the upper arms still, breathe out and curl the weight forward by tightening the biceps. Concentrate on moving the forearms only.
Keep lifting until the biceps is fully contracted and the bar reaches shoulder level. Hold this top position for a moment and squeeze the biceps.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
EZ-Bar_Skullcrusher: Pick up the EZ bar with a close grip and lie on the bench, holding it with your elbows tucked in. Your arms are perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
With the upper arms still, bend the elbows to lower the bar, breathing in as you do. Pause when the bar is right above your forehead.
Breathe out and straighten the elbows to bring the bar back to the starting position.
Elbow_Circles: Sit or stand, feet a little apart.
Put your hands on your shoulders, with the elbows pointing outward at shoulder height.
Draw a slow circle with your elbows. Breathe out as the circle begins and breathe in as you finish it.
Elbow_to_Knee: Lie on the floor with your left knee bent and your right leg crossed over it. Lock your hands behind your head and start with your shoulder blades on the ground. This is your starting position.
Curl your spine and twist your torso so the left elbow moves to the right knee.
Go back to the starting position, do the desired number of repetitions, then change sides.
Elbows_Back: With fingers pointing downward and elbows out, rest both hands on your lower back.
Now draw your elbows gently backward, trying to bring them together.
Elevated_Back_Lunge: Set a bar on a rack at shoulder height and load it with a suitable weight. Put a low raised platform behind you.
Set the bar on your upper back with the back kept arched and tight. Step up onto your raised platform with both feet. You start from here.
Start by taking a step backward with one leg. Bend your hips and knees to lower yourself until the knee touches the floor.
Pause, then straighten your hips and knees to rise, coming all the way back to the starting position before you change legs.
Elevated_Cable_Rows: Find a platform about 4-6 inches high, such as an aerobics step or a calf raise platform.
Put it on the cable row machine's seat.
Sit on it and set your feet on the front platform or crossbar of the machine. Your knees should be slightly bent, not locked.
Lean forward with your back in its natural alignment and take hold of the V-bar handles.

With straight arms, pull back until your torso is at a 90-degree angle to your legs. Arch your back slightly and push your chest out. Holding the bar in front of you, you should feel a good stretch in your lats. This is the starting position.

Keep your torso still and pull the handles toward you, arms close to your body, until they touch your abdominals. Breathe out as you pull. Squeeze your back muscles hard at this point and hold for one second, then breathe in and return slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Elliptical_Trainer: Step onto the elliptical and choose an option from the menu. Most machines offer a manual setting or programs you can run. You can usually enter your age and weight to get an estimate of the calories you burn during the session. Change the elevation to make the workout harder or easier.
Hold the handles to track your heart rate, which helps you stay at a suitable intensity.
