Exercise_Ball_Crunch: Lie back on an exercise ball so the curve of your lower back presses against the ball. Bend your knees and plant your feet firmly on the floor. Your upper torso hangs over the top of the ball. Keep your arms along your body or crossed over your chest, as both positions spare the neck, unlike placing the hands behind the head.
With the neck kept still at all times, bring your torso down into a stretch position. You start from here.

Keep your hips still, tighten the abdominals to bend at the waist, and curl your shoulders and trunk upward until you feel a strong contraction in your abdominals. Arms at your sides simply slide up along your legs; crossed arms stay on your chest. Your lower back never leaves the ball. Breathe out during the movement and hold the contraction for one second.
Breathe in and return to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Exercise_Ball_Pull-In: Put an exercise ball close by and get down on the floor in front of it in a push-up position, hands on the floor shoulder width apart.

Rest your lower shins on the ball. Tip: Your legs are now fully straight with the shins on the ball, and your upper body is in a push-up position, held up by your two straight arms. This is your starting position.
With a completely straight back and a still upper body, breathe out and draw your knees toward your chest so the ball rolls forward under your ankles. Squeeze your abs and hold there for one second.
Breathe in and straighten your legs slowly, rolling the ball back to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Extended_Range_One-Arm_Kettlebell_Floor_: Lie on the floor and set up a kettlebell to press with one arm, holding it by the handle. Bend the leg on the pressing side and bring its knee across the midline of your body.
Extend the elbow and bring the arm inward to press the kettlebell up above your body. Lower it to the starting position.
External_Rotation: Lie on your side on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand. Fold the other arm on the bench and rest your head on it.
Bend the elbow of the working arm to a 90-degree angle between upper arm and forearm. Tip: The arm stays parallel to your torso.

Bend the elbow with the upper arm kept still, so the forearm ends up parallel to the floor and at a right angle to your torso (Tip: The forearm then points straight out in front of you). The upper arm rests still against your torso, parallel to the floor and always in line with your torso. This is your starting position.

Breathe out and turn the forearm outward, lifting the dumbbell in a half circle and holding the 90 degree bend between upper arm and forearm. Go on turning until the forearm points to the ceiling, perpendicular to the floor and to your torso. Hold the contraction there for one second.
Breathe in and lower slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions, then change to the other arm.
External_Rotation_with_Band: Loop the band tightly around a post at the height of your elbow. Stand a couple of feet away with your left side toward the band.
Take the end of the band in your right hand and press the elbow firmly against your side. Holding a pad or foam roll between elbow and body is recommended to keep the elbow in place.
With the upper arm fixed, bend the elbow to 90 degrees so your hand reaches across the front of your torso. This is your starting position.
Rotate the arm outward as in a backhand stroke, without letting the elbow move.
Go as far as you can, pause, then come back to where you started.
External_Rotation_with_Cable: Set the cable to elbow height. Stand a couple of feet away with your left side toward the cable.
Take the handle in your right hand and press the elbow firmly against your side. Holding a pad or foam roll between elbow and body is recommended to keep the elbow in place.
With the upper arm fixed, bend the elbow to 90 degrees so your hand reaches across the front of your torso. This is your starting position.
Rotate the arm outward as in a backhand stroke, without letting the elbow move.
Face_Pull: Stand facing a high pulley fitted with a rope or two handles. Pull the weight straight toward your face and move your hands apart as you pull. Your upper arms stay parallel to the ground.
Farmers_Walk: Several kinds of implements work for the farmer's walk. If you have none, heavy dumbbells or short bars do the job too. Start by standing between the implements.
Grip the handles and lift them by pushing through your heels, with a straight back and your head up.
Walk with short, quick steps and remember to breathe. Cover a set distance, usually 50-100 feet, as fast as you can.
Fast_Skipping: Stand relaxed with one leg a little in front. This is your starting position.
Skip in a step-hop pattern: right-right-step, then left-left-step, and keep alternating from side to side.
For fast skips, stay close to the ground, cut the time in the air and move as quickly as you can.
Finger_Curls: Take a barbell in both hands with the palms up and the hands about shoulder width apart.
Set your feet flat on the floor, slightly wider than shoulder width apart. You start from here.
Open your fingers to lower the bar as far as you can. Let it roll down your hands and catch it with the last joints of the fingers.
Breathe out and close your hands to curl the bar up as high as you can. Hold the squeeze at the top.
Flat_Bench_Cable_Flyes: Put a flat bench between two low pulleys so that your chest lines up with the pulleys when you lie on it.
Lie flat on the bench with your feet kept on the floor.
Ask someone to pass you a handle for each hand. Hold each single handle with your palms up.
Stretch your arms out to the sides with the elbows slightly bent. Tip: This bend stays the same during the entire movement. Your arms are parallel to the floor. This is your starting position.

Draw the cables together, lifting your arms in a half circle in front of you until both hands meet at the top. Squeeze your chest and breathe out as you lift, and hold the squeeze at the top for one second. Tip: Done correctly, your arms at the top are perpendicular to your torso and the floor, and your hands touch above your chest.
Return slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Flat_Bench_Leg_Pull-In: Lie down on a flat bench, or on an exercise mat, so that your legs reach past the end.
Put your hands palms down beneath your glutes, or grip the bench at your sides (on a mat, rest the palms flat on the floor beside you). Stretch both legs out straight. This is your starting position.
Breathe out, bend the knees and draw your thighs in towards your midsection. Keep going until the knees are close to the chest, then hold the squeeze for one second.
Breathe in and slowly stretch the legs back out to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Flat_Bench_Lying_Leg_Raise: Lie flat on your back on a bench, legs stretched out past its end.
Put your hands palms down beneath your glutes, or grip the bench at your sides. This is your starting position.

Keep the legs as straight as you can, the knees only slightly bent and fixed in that position, and lift them until they stand at a 90-degree angle to the floor. Breathe out on the way up and hold the tension at the top for one second.
Then breathe in and bring your legs slowly down again to the starting position.
Flexor_Incline_Dumbbell_Curls: Grip each dumbbell near the end that is farther from you, so that more of the weight sits on the side nearest to you. (This works well for every dumbbell exercise for the biceps.) Then perform an ordinary incline dumbbell curl, with your wrists bent back as far as they go to take the strain off them.
Take a dumbbell in each hand and sit on an incline bench set to 45 degrees.

Let both arms hang at your sides with the elbows tucked in. Turn your palms to the front so the thumbs point away from your body. Tip: Hold this hand position for the whole movement; the hands must not twist on the way up. This is your starting position.

Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up together until the biceps are fully contracted. Tip: No swinging of the arms and no momentum; the motion stays controlled the whole time. Hold for one second at the top.
Breathe in and slowly return to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Floor_Glute-Ham_Raise: Do this exercise with a partner, or wedge your feet under something that will not move.
Start kneeling, with thighs and torso upright. A partner, if you have one, holds your feet down firmly so you stay in place. This is your starting position.
Let yourself sink forward by straightening at the knees. Take care that your hips do NOT bend as you go.

Put your hands out in front to catch yourself when you reach the floor. The movement is very hard and you may not manage it without help. Push off the floor lightly with your arms to help you back to the starting position.
Floor_Press: Set the J-hooks to a height from which you can unrack and rack the bar. Lie on the floor with your head close to the end of a power rack. Pull your shoulder blades together, keep them there and take the bar off the hooks.

Bring the bar down towards your lower chest or upper stomach. Squeeze it hard on the way and try to pull it apart. Keep your elbows tucked for the whole movement. Go down until your upper arms touch the ground, then pause so the weight neither slams nor bounces.
Drive the bar back up as quickly as you can. Bar, wrists and elbows stay in one line as you press.
Floor_Press_with_Chains: Set the J-hooks to a height from which you can unrack and rack the bar. Hang the chains straight over the ends of the bar and try to keep their ends clear of the plates.
Lie on the floor with your head close to the end of a power rack. Pull your shoulder blades together, keep them there and take the bar off the hooks.

Bring the bar down towards your lower chest or upper stomach. Squeeze it hard on the way and try to pull it apart. Keep your elbows tucked for the whole movement. Go down until your upper arms touch the ground, then pause so the weight neither slams nor bounces.
Drive the bar back up as quickly as you can. Bar, wrists and elbows stay in one line as you press.
Flutter_Kicks: Lie face down on a flat bench with your hips at its edge. Keep the legs straight and the toes well clear of the floor, lay your arms on the bench and grip its front edge.
Tighten your glutes and hamstrings, straightening your legs until they are level with the hips. You start from here.
Begin by raising your left leg above the right one.
Next, bring the left leg down while the right leg goes up.

Keep switching like this, as if you were kicking in water, until each leg has done the recommended number of repetitions. Stay in control of the movement the whole time. Tip: Breathe normally during this exercise.
Foot-SMR: With this exercise you stretch the fascia of the foot muscles. Sit down and take your shoes off. Take a foot roller or something similar, for example a short piece of PVC pipe, and set the arch of one foot on it. This is your starting position.
Push down hard and roll along the arch of the foot. Keep this up for 10-30 seconds, then change to the other foot.
Forward_Drag_with_Press: Fix a chain or rope attachment with two handles to the sled. Stand with your back to the sled and take one handle in each hand.

Start by taking one step forward. Lean forward and push through your legs and hips to move. Pause at every step and straighten your elbows to press the hands out in front of you. Then step on until you are back in the start position, ready for the next press.
Frankenstein_Squat: With this drill you learn where the bar and your body belong in the clean and the front squat.

Lay the barbell across the front of your shoulders, let go of it and stretch your arms out in front of you. Push the shoulders forward so they form a shelf; the bar should touch your throat. Only the shoulder blades move forward: do not round the thoracic spine.
Bend your knees and hips and sit down between your legs. Torso upright, arms up, shoulders forward: that way the bar stays where it is. Go all the way down, until your hamstrings touch your calves.
Stand back up by pushing through the front part of the heel and straightening your knees and hips.
Freehand_Jump_Squat: Fold your arms across your chest.
Set your feet shoulder width apart, head up and back straight.
Breathe in and squat down until your thighs are parallel to the floor or lower. Your back stays straight and your chest up.
Now push off mostly from the balls of your feet and jump straight up as high as you can, using your thighs like springs. Breathe out during the jump.
As soon as you land, drop straight into the next squat and jump again.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Frog_Hops: With your hands behind your head, squat down, torso upright and head up. You start from here.
Jump several feet forward without going higher than necessary. When your feet touch the ground, let your legs absorb the landing and jump again. Do this 5-10 times.
Frog_Sit-Ups: Lie flat on your back on the floor or an exercise mat, legs stretched out.
Bend your knees and let them drop outwards so the outer thighs rest near the floor or mat and the soles of your feet touch.
Press the two soles together and slide them as close to your body as you can. The outer thighs stay on the floor, or at least nearly touch it. Tip: Your legs should now form a diamond.
Next, cross your arms in front of you so each hand touches the opposite shoulder. You start from here.
Breathe out, press your lower back flat into the floor and curl your torso up. Tip: It feels like the first quarter of a sit-up. Hold at the top for one second.
Breathe in and slowly lower yourself to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Front_Barbell_Squat: For safety, do this exercise inside a squat rack. First set the bar in the rack at the height that suits your body. With the height right and the bar loaded, bring your arms up underneath the bar, elbows high and upper arms a little above parallel to the floor. Let the bar rest on top of your deltoids, cross your arms and hold the bar so you control it fully.
Take the bar out of the rack: push with your legs first and straighten your torso at the same moment.

Step back from the rack. Stand in a medium stance, feet shoulder width apart and toes turned out a little. Keep your head up the whole time, because looking down throws you off balance, and keep your back straight. This is your starting position. Note: The medium stance described here trains the legs as a whole; you can use any of the three stance widths instead.

Bend your knees and lower the bar slowly, posture straight and head up. Go down until the angle between thigh and calf is slightly under 90 degrees; at that point the thighs are below parallel to the floor. Breathe in on the way down. Tip: Done correctly, the front of each knee sits on an imaginary vertical line with the toes. Knees that travel beyond that line, past the toes, put needless stress on the joint, and the exercise is then done wrong.
Breathe out and raise the bar: press mostly through the middle of your foot into the floor, straighten your legs and come back to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Front_Barbell_Squat_To_A_Bench: For safety, do this exercise inside a squat rack. First put a flat bench behind you and set the bar in the rack at the height that suits your body. With the height right and the bar loaded, bring your arms up underneath the bar, elbows high and upper arms a little above parallel to the floor. Let the bar rest on top of your deltoids, cross your arms and hold the bar so you control it fully.
Take the bar out of the rack: push with your legs first and straighten your torso at the same moment.

Step back from the rack. Stand in a medium stance, feet shoulder width apart and toes turned out a little. Keep your head up the whole time, because looking down throws you off balance, and keep your back straight. This is your starting position. Note: The medium stance described here trains the legs as a whole; you can use any of the three stance widths instead.

Bend your knees and lower the bar slowly, posture straight and head up. Go down until your glutes touch the bench. Breathe in on the way down. Tip: Done correctly, the front of each knee sits on an imaginary vertical line with the toes. Knees that travel beyond that line, past the toes, put needless stress on the joint, and the exercise is then done wrong.
Breathe out and raise the bar: press mostly through your heels into the floor, straighten your legs and come back to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Front_Box_Jump: Set a box of suitable height 1-2 feet ahead of you and take a shoulder-width stance. You start from here.
Dip into a shallow squat to load the jump and swing your arms back.
Spring out of the dip: straighten hips, knees and ankles and jump as high as you can. Swing the arms forward and upward.
Land on the box with bent knees and let your legs take up the impact. You may jump back down to the ground, but it is better to step down one leg after the other.
Front_Cable_Raise: Set the weight on a low pulley machine. Take the single handle fixed to the low pulley in your left hand.
Turn your back to the pulley. Let the arm hang straight down at full length, the handle in front of your thigh and the palm turned towards the thigh. This is your starting position.

Keep your torso still, without swinging, and raise the left arm to the front. The elbow is slightly bent and the palm faces down all the way. Go up until the arm is a little above parallel to the floor. Breathe out during the lift and pause for one second at the top.
Breathe in and lower the arm slowly to the starting position.
When this arm has done the recommended number of repetitions, change sides and do the same with the right arm.
Front_Cone_Hops_or_hurdle_hops: Line up cones or other low obstacles in a row, a few feet from one another.
Take a shoulder-width stance in front of the first cone. You start from here.
Jump off both feet over the first cone and swing both arms with the jump.
Bend your knees to cushion the landing and bounce straight out of it over the next cone.
Carry on until you have cleared every cone.
Front_Dumbbell_Raise: Take a pair of dumbbells and stand with your torso straight. Hold the dumbbells at arm's length in front of your thighs, palms turned towards the thighs. This is your starting position.

Keep your torso still, without swinging, and raise the left dumbbell to the front. The elbow is slightly bent and the palm faces down all the way. Go up until the arm is a little above parallel to the floor. Breathe out during the lift and pause for one second at the top. Breathe in once the pause is over.
Lower that dumbbell slowly to the starting position and raise the right dumbbell at the same time.
Keep alternating like this until each arm has done the recommended number of repetitions.
Front_Incline_Dumbbell_Raise: Take a dumbbell in each hand and sit on an incline bench set somewhere between 30 and 60 degrees. Tip: Change the angle from time to time to work the muscle a little differently.
Reach your arms straight out in front of you, palms turned down, the dumbbells about 1 inch above your thighs. You start from here.

With the elbows locked, raise the dumbbells slowly and straight up until they are just above shoulder height. Squeeze for one second at the top, and breathe out during the lift. Tip: Your head stays back against the bench and your feet stay on the floor the whole time.
Breathe in and bring the arms down to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Front_Leg_Raises: Hold on to a chair or other support with one hand and stand beside it.
Swing one leg forward and keep it straight. Let it swing down and on behind you, as far back as your flexibility permits. Do this 5-10 times, then change legs.
Front_Plate_Raise: Stand straight and hold a weight plate with both hands at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions. The palms face each other. The arms are stretched and fixed, the elbows slightly bent, and the plate hangs in front of you near your waist, as low as it goes. Tip: The arms keep this position for the whole exercise. This is your starting position.

Breathe out and raise the plate slowly until it is just above shoulder level. Hold the tension for one second. Tip: Do not swing the weight and do not bend the elbows further. Your torso also stays still throughout.
Breathe in and lower the plate slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Front_Raise_And_Pullover: Lie on a flat bench and hold a barbell with your palms facing down and your hands about 15 inches apart.
Rest the bar on your upper thighs, straighten and lock your arms, but leave a slight bend in the elbows. You start from here.

Breathe in and lift the weight in a half circle with your arms kept straight. Carry on until the bar is on the far side, above your head. (Tip: The bar travels about 180 degrees.) Your arms should now be parallel to the floor, palms turned to the ceiling.
Breathe out and bring the barbell back the same way to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Front_Squat_Clean_Grip: First set the bar in a rack a little below shoulder level. Let it rest on top of your deltoids, pressed against the collarbones and just touching your throat. Hold it in a clean grip: only your fingers touch the bar and help keep it in place.

Take the bar out of the rack: push with your legs first and straighten your torso at the same moment. Step back from the rack and stand in a medium stance, feet shoulder width apart and toes turned out a little. Head and elbows stay up the whole time. This is your starting position.

Bend your knees and sit down between your legs. Go down until your hamstrings rest on your calves. Keep the knees in line with the feet: use your abductors deliberately to push the knees outwards as you squat.
Breathe out and raise the bar: press mostly through the heel or the middle of the foot into the floor, straighten your legs and come back to the starting position.
Front_Squats_With_Two_Kettlebells: Clean two kettlebells to your shoulders: straighten your legs and hips, pull the kettlebells up to the shoulders and turn your wrists as they rise.

Look straight ahead the whole time. Squat as deep as you can and pause at the bottom. Push your knees outwards on the way down. Sit between your legs with your torso upright and your head and chest up.
Push through your heels to stand up again, then repeat.
Front_Two-Dumbbell_Raise: Take a pair of dumbbells and stand with your torso straight. Hold the dumbbells at arm's length in front of your thighs, palms turned towards the thighs. This is your starting position.

Keep your torso still, without swinging, and raise both dumbbells to the front. The elbows are slightly bent and the palms face down all the way. Go up until the arms are a little above parallel to the floor. Breathe out during the lift and pause for one second at the top.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbells slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Full_Range-Of-Motion_Lat_Pulldown: Stand, or sit on a high bench, and take hold of two stirrup handles fixed to the high pulleys. Grip each with the opposite hand, so that your arms cross above you and your palms face forward.

Chest up, a slight arch in the lower back: pull the handles down as in an ordinary pulldown. The path is more of an arc here. Turn your hands as you pull, so that at the bottom the palms face each other and no longer forward. Go back slowly to the starting position and repeat.
Gironda_Sternum_Chins: Take the pull-up bar in an underhand grip, hands shoulder width apart.
Next, hang with fully extended arms, push your chest out and lean back. Tip: Stay leaning back through the whole movement. You start from here.

Pull yourself up to the bar. Keep your spine arched all the way and your head tilted back, as far from the bar as you can. Breathe out as you pull. Tip: Near the top, your hips and legs are at roughly a 45-degree angle to the floor.
Pull on until your collarbone has passed the bar and your lower chest, around the sternum, touches it. Hold for one second. Tip: When you have finished this part, your head is parallel to the floor.
Breathe in and slowly lower yourself to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Glute_Ham_Raise: First adjust the machine to your body. Lie face down with your feet between the rollers and against the footplate. Your knees should sit just behind the pad.

Begin at the bottom of the movement. Arch your back, keep it arched and bend your knees to start. Press your toes into the footplate as you do. Your upper body stays straight; carry on until you are upright.
Lower yourself under control to the starting position.
Glute_Kickback: Kneel on the floor or an exercise mat and bend forward at the waist. Stretch your arms out in front of you, at right angles to the torso, so that you are in a kneeling push-up position with the hands shoulder width apart. Look forward. Your knees are bent so that hamstrings and calves form a 90-degree angle. This is your starting position.

Breathe out and lift your right leg until the hamstrings are in line with your back; the knee keeps its 90-degree bend. Tense the glutes all the way and hold at the top for one second. Tip: At the end, the thigh should be parallel to the floor and the calf at a right angle to it.
Breathe in, return to where you started and repeat with the left leg.
Keep changing legs until you have done all the recommended repetitions.
Goblet_Squat: Hold a light kettlebell by the horns close to your chest while standing. You start from here.
Keeping a straight back, with chest and head up, sink between your legs until hamstrings meet calves.
Pause at the bottom and push your knees outwards with your elbows. Come back to the starting position and do 10-20 repetitions.
Good_Morning: Start with a bar in a rack at shoulder height. Take it across the back of your shoulders, as for a power squat, not on top of them. Keep your back tight, your shoulder blades squeezed together and your knees slightly bent. Step back from the rack.
Bend at the hips to begin: push them back and lean forward until your torso is almost parallel to the floor. Your back stays arched and your cervical spine properly aligned.
Turn the movement around: straighten your hips with the strength of your glutes and hamstrings. Carry on until you are back in the starting position.
Good_Morning_off_Pins: Start with a bar in a rack at about stomach height. Bend down under the bar and take it across the back of your shoulders, as for a power squat, not on top of them. At the right height, your bent-over torso is almost parallel to the floor. Keep your back tight, your shoulder blades squeezed together and your knees slightly bent. Your back stays arched and your cervical spine properly aligned.
Start the movement by straightening your hips with your glutes and hamstrings until you stand upright with the weight. Lower the weight slowly onto the pins again to return to the starting position.
Gorilla_Chin_Crunch: With an underhand grip (palms facing you) slightly wider than shoulder width, hang from a chin-up bar.
Bend your knees to 90 degrees: the calves are parallel to the floor, the thighs stay at a right angle to it. This is your starting position.

Breathe out and pull yourself up while you draw your knees up in a crunch until they reach chest height. Stop as soon as your nose is level with the bar. Tip: The crunch should be finished at exactly that moment too.
Begin to breathe in slowly and return to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Groin_and_Back_Stretch: Take a seat on the floor, knees bent and feet together.
Behind your head, interlock your fingers. You start from here.
Curl your upper body down and bring your elbows to the inner sides of your thighs. Pause briefly, then come back to the starting position, head up and back straight. Do 10-20 repetitions.
Groiners: Get into a pushup position on the floor; you start from here.
Jump forward with both legs so that your feet land beside your hands. Keep your head up during the jump.
Go back to the starting position and repeat the movement straight away, for 10-20 repetitions in all.
Hack_Squat: Lean back into the machine so your back rests on the back pad, and tuck your shoulders under the shoulder pads.
Set your feet on the platform about shoulder width apart, a medium stance, toes turned out a little. Tip: Keep your head up and your back pressed to the pad the whole time.
Take hold of the side handles and release the safety bars (on most machines you do this by turning the handles from facing forward to a diagonal position).

Extend your legs, but stop short of locking your knees. This is your starting position. Note: The medium stance described above is used here because it develops the legs overall, but any of the three foot stances is an option.

Bend your knees and let the sled come down slowly, staying upright with your head up and your back on the pad throughout. Go down until the angle between your thighs and calves is a little under 90 degrees, which is where your thighs drop below parallel to the floor. Breathe in on the way down. Tip: Done right, the front of your knees and your toes line up on an imaginary straight line that is perpendicular to the front. If your knees travel beyond that line, past your toes, they take unnecessary stress and the repetition was not done correctly.
Breathe out and drive the sled back up, pressing mostly through your heels, until your legs are straight again and you are back in the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Hammer_Curls: Stand tall with your torso upright, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging straight. Keep your elbows close to your body.
Turn your palms so they face your torso. This is your starting position.

Keep your upper arms still, breathe out and curl the weights forward by tightening your biceps. Lift until the biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells reach shoulder height. Pause briefly at the top and squeeze the biceps. Tip: Concentrate on holding your elbows in place so that only the forearms move.
After that short pause, breathe in and lower the dumbbells slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Hammer_Grip_Incline_DB_Bench_Press: Sit back on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand resting on your thighs, palms turned towards each other.
Kick the dumbbells up with the help of your thighs, one arm at a time, until you hold them at shoulder width.

Hold them there with a neutral grip, palms facing one another. Flare your elbows out so your upper arms are level with your shoulders (perpendicular to your torso), and bend the elbows so that upper arm and forearm form a 90-degree angle. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and lower the weights slowly to your sides. Stay in full control of the dumbbells the whole time.

Breathe out and press the dumbbells up with your chest muscles. Lock your arms at the top, hold for a second, then begin to lower slowly. Tip: The way down should take at least twice as long as the way up.
Do the prescribed number of repetitions.
When you finish, rest the dumbbells on your thighs again and then set them on the floor. That is the safest way to put the dumbbells down.
Hamstring-SMR: Sit down and stretch your legs out over a foam roll so it lies under the back of your thighs. Put your hands beside or behind you to help carry your weight. This is your starting position.
Push through your hands to lift your hips off the floor and shift your weight onto one leg on the roll. Let the hamstrings of that leg relax.
Roll from just below the hip to just above the back of the knee, stopping for 10-30 seconds wherever you find a tense spot. Then do the other leg.
Hamstring_Stretch: Lie on your back and raise one leg straight up so the hip is bent to ninety degrees. Leave the other leg flat on the floor.
Put a belt, band or rope around the ball of your foot. You start from here.
Create tension in the calves and hamstrings by pulling on the belt. Stay in the stretch for 10-30 seconds, then do the other leg.
Handstand_Push-Ups: Turn your back to the wall and bend at the waist, then set both hands shoulder width apart on the floor.

Kick up against the wall with straight arms. You should end upside down, arms and legs fully extended, your whole body as straight as you can keep it. Tip: On your first attempts, ask a spotter to help. Also keep your head facing the wall instead of looking down.
Breathe in and lower yourself slowly towards the floor until your head nearly touches it. Tip: Coming down slowly is extremely important, so that you do not injure your head.
Breathe out and press back up slowly until your elbows are almost locked.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Hang_Clean: Hold the bar with a double overhand or hook grip at shoulder width, letting it hang at mid-thigh. Keep your back straight and leaning slightly forward.
Extend your hips, knees and ankles explosively to drive the weight upward. At the same time, shrug your shoulders up towards your ears.
Recover straight away: push through your heels with your torso upright and your elbows high. Keep going until you are standing.
Hang_Clean_-_Below_the_Knees: Hold the bar with a double overhand or hook grip at shoulder width, letting it hang just under your knees. Keep your back straight and leaning slightly forward.

Extend your hips, knees and ankles explosively to drive the weight upward, shrugging your shoulders towards your ears as you go. Once you are fully extended, move into the third pull: shrug hard and bend your arms, elbows travelling up and out.

At the top of the extension, pull yourself down hard and whip your elbows under the bar. Catch the bar in a front squat position; how deep depends on how high the bar got by the end of the third pull. Rack the bar on your shoulders, which are pushed forward, so that it lightly touches your throat while your hands stay relaxed. Sink on down to the bottom of the squat, which helps with the recovery.
Recover straight away: push through your heels with your torso upright and your elbows high. Keep going until you are standing.
Hang_Snatch: Take a wide grip on the bar, overhand or hook. Stand with your feet right under your hips, toes turned out. Bend your knees slightly and lean your torso forward. Keep your spine fully extended and your head facing forward. Hold the bar at your hips. This is your starting position.
Extend your legs and hips explosively. At the top of the extension, shrug your shoulders and let your elbows bend out to the sides.
While your feet move to the receiving position, pull yourself hard under the bar and lift it overhead. Catch the bar with your body as low as possible and your arms fully extended above your head.
Stand up with the weight overhead. Then bring the weight back to the ground under control.
Hang_Snatch_-_Below_Knees: Take a wide grip on the bar, overhand or hook. Stand with your feet right under your hips, toes turned out. Bend your knees slightly and lean your torso forward. Keep your spine fully extended and your head facing forward. Hold the bar just under your knees. This is your starting position.
Extend your legs and hips explosively. At the top of the extension, shrug your shoulders and let your elbows bend out to the sides.
While your feet move to the receiving position, pull yourself hard under the bar and lift it overhead. Catch the bar with your body as low as possible and your arms fully extended above your head.
Stand up with the weight overhead, then lower it to the floor under control.
Hanging_Bar_Good_Morning: Set a bar in a rack at roughly stomach height, hanging from chains or suspension straps.

Bend forward under the bar and set it across the back of your shoulders, as for a power squat, not on top of your traps. At the right height your torso is nearly parallel to the floor when you are bent over. Tighten your back, squeeze your shoulder blades together and bend your knees slightly. Keep an arch in your back and your neck properly aligned with the spine.
Using glutes and hamstrings, extend through the hips to start the motion, and finish standing with the weight.
Lower the weight slowly to the starting position, where the chains carry it again.
Hanging_Leg_Raise: Hang from a chin-up bar with both arms fully extended above you, using a wide or medium grip. Let your legs hang straight down and tilt your pelvis slightly backwards. This is your starting position.
Lift your legs until they form a 90-degree angle with your torso. Breathe out as you lift, and hold the contraction for about a second.
Breathe in and return slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Hanging_Pike: With legs and feet together, hang from a chin-up bar using an overhand grip (palms facing away from you) slightly wider than shoulder width. Tip: Wrist wraps may help you hold on to the bar.
Bend your knees to 90 degrees and bring your thighs forward, so your calves are perpendicular to the floor and your thighs stay parallel to it. This is your starting position.
Breathe out and pull your legs up until your shins almost touch the bar above you. Tip: At the top, try to straighten your legs as far as you can.
Lower your legs as slowly as you can to the starting position. Tip: Never swing or use momentum.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Heaving_Snatch_Balance: This drill helps you learn the snatch. Start with a light weight resting across the back of your shoulders. Place your feet slightly wider than hip width with toes turned out, the same stance you would squat in.
Dip slightly at the knees and pop back up to unload the bar for a moment. Drive yourself under the bar, pushing it overhead while you drop into a full squat.
Heavy_Bag_Thrust: This exercise uses a heavy bag. Stand upright beside the bag, feet staggered and fairly wide apart, one hand on the bag at about chest height. You start from here.
Twist at the waist and shove the bag forward as hard as you can. Make the move fast, driving the bag away from your body.
When the bag swings back, catch it by reversing these steps.
High_Cable_Curls: Stand between two high pulleys and take a handle in each hand. Hold your upper arms parallel to the floor, palms facing you. This is your starting position.

Curl the handles in until they are beside your ears, tightening your biceps and breathing out as you do. Keep the upper arms still so that only the forearms move. Hold the contraction for a second and squeeze the biceps.
Let your arms return slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Hip_Circles_prone: Get down on your hands and knees. With good posture, lift one bent knee off the floor. This is your starting position.
Keep that knee bent and rotate the thigh bone in an arc, trying to draw a big circle with your knee.
Do this slowly for several repetitions, then switch sides.
Hip_Extension_with_Bands: Fasten one end of the band low on a post and the other end around one ankle.
Face the point where the band is anchored and hold the post to steady yourself.
With head and chest up, move the banded leg as far back as you can, keeping the knee straight.
Bring the leg back to where it started.
Hip_Flexion_with_Band: Fasten one end of the band low on a post and the other end around one ankle.
Turn your back to the point where the band is anchored.
With head and chest up, lift your knee to 90 degrees and pause.
Move the leg back to where it began.
Hip_Lift_with_Band: Pick a suitable band, secure it on both sides of you and lie down in the middle of the rack. If the rack has no pegs, you can anchor the band with heavy dumbbells or similar objects; just make sure they cannot move.
Shift until the band runs directly across your hips. Bend your knees and set your feet flat on the floor. Rest your hands on the floor or use them to hold the band in place.
With shoulders kept on the floor, push through the heels and lift your hips into the band as high as you can.
Hold briefly at the top, then come back to where you started.
Hug_A_Ball: Take an exercise ball between your legs, straddling it, and lower your hips towards the floor.

Wrap your arms around the ball to support your body. Move your legs so your feet are flat on the floor and your knees are above your ankles. Hold the ball firmly so that it cannot roll away and drop you back onto your buttocks.
Hug_Knees_To_Chest: On your back, draw both knees in until they reach your chest.
Your arms go under the knees. Holding over them would load the knee joints with too much pressure.
Gently pull your knees towards your shoulders. This stretches your glutes as well.
Hurdle_Hops: Line up hurdles or other small barriers in a row, a few feet apart.
Take a shoulder-width stance in front of the first hurdle. You start from here.
Jump over the first hurdle off both feet, swinging both arms as you take off.
Bend your knees to absorb the landing and rebound straight into the jump over the next hurdle. Carry on until you have cleared every hurdle.
Hyperextensions_Back_Extensions: On a hyperextension bench, lie face down with your ankles tucked securely under the footpads.
If the upper pad is adjustable, set it so your upper thighs lie flat on the wide pad and you have enough room to bend at the waist without being restricted.

Keep your body straight and cross your arms in front of you (the preferred way) or put them behind your head. This is your starting position. Tip: For extra resistance you can hold a weight plate in front of you under your crossed arms.

Bend forward slowly at the waist as far as you can with a flat back, breathing in as you go. Keep going until you feel a good stretch in your hamstrings and could not go further without rounding your back. Tip: Never round your back in this exercise. Some people can go further than others; what matters is going as far as your body allows without the back rounding.

Breathe in and slowly raise your torso to the initial position. Tip: Resist the urge to arch your back beyond a straight line. And do not swing your torso at any point, to protect your back from injury.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Hyperextensions_With_No_Hyperextension_B: Have someone hold your legs down and slide forward on a flat bench until your hips hang off its end. Tip: Your whole upper body should hang down towards the floor. The position is the same as on a hyperextension bench, but the range of motion is shorter because the flat bench is lower than a hyperextension bench.

Keep your body straight and cross your arms in front of you (the preferred way) or put them behind your head. This is your starting position. Tip: For extra resistance you can hold a weight plate in front of you under your crossed arms.

Bend forward slowly at the waist as far as you can with a flat back, breathing in as you go. Keep going until you almost touch the floor or feel a good stretch in your hamstrings, whichever happens first. Tip: Never round your back in this exercise.

Breathe out and slowly raise your torso to the initial position. Tip: Resist the urge to arch your back beyond a straight line. And do not swing your torso at any point, to protect your back from injury.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
IT_Band_and_Glute_Stretch: Lying on the floor, put a belt, rope or band around one foot and take that leg across your body to the opposite side, with the leg kept straight. That is the starting position.
Hold the foot clear of the floor and pull on the belt so that the tension draws your toes up. Hold for 10-20 seconds, then do the other side.
Iliotibial_Tract-SMR: Lie on your side with the lower leg resting on a foam roller between hip and knee. You can cross the other leg in front of you.
Put as much weight on the lower leg as you can tolerate; that leg does not have to touch the ground. Make sure the muscles of the leg being stretched are relaxed.
Roll the leg over the roller from hip to knee, stopping for 10-30 seconds on tense spots. Then do the opposite leg.
Inchworm: Stand, feet close together. With straight legs, reach down and put your hands on the floor directly in front of you. You start from here.
Walk your hands forward slowly, left and right in turn. Bend only at the hips and keep your legs straight.
Continue until you are in a pushup position, body parallel to the floor.
Now leave your hands where they are and walk your feet forward slowly in short steps of only a few inches.
Keep walking, legs straight, until your feet reach your hands.
Incline_Barbell_Triceps_Extension: Grip a barbell overhand (palms down), hands slightly narrower than shoulder width.
Set an incline bench to any angle between 45-75 degrees and lie back on it.
Raise the bar overhead with straight arms and elbows tucked in. Your arms should be above your head, in line with your torso. This is your starting position.

Lower the bar behind your head in a semicircle until your forearms touch your biceps, breathing in as you go. Tip: Keep your upper arms still and close to your head throughout. Only the forearms move.
Breathe out and tighten your triceps to return to the starting position. Hold the contraction for a second.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Incline_Bench_Pull: Take a dumbbell in each hand and lie face down on an incline bench set to roughly 30 degrees.
Let your arms hang fully extended at your sides, pointing to the floor.
Rotate your wrists into a pronated grip (palms down).
Next, flare your elbows out. You start from here.

Breathe out and pull the dumbbells up as if doing a bench press in reverse: bend your elbows and lift your upper arms while the forearms hang down. Keep going until your upper arms are level with your back. Tip: Your elbows travel out to the sides, and at the top your upper arms and torso should form the letter "T". Hold the contraction at the top for a second.
Breathe in and lower slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Incline_Cable_Chest_Press: Set a suitable weight, sit down and take the handles. Hold your upper arms at about 45 degrees to your body, head and chest up, elbows bent to about 90 degrees. This is your starting position.
Straighten your elbows to press the handles together straight ahead of you. Keep your shoulder blades pulled back during the movement.
Pause when your arms are fully extended, then return to the starting position without letting the cables go slack.
Incline_Cable_Flye: To set up for the starting position, move the pulleys to floor level (the lowest setting on the machine, below your torso).
Between the pulleys, set up an incline bench at 45 degrees. Choose a weight on each side, then take one pulley per hand.
Holding both handles, lie back on the bench and bring your hands together in front of your face with arms extended. This is your starting position.

Bend your elbows slightly, to spare the biceps tendon, and lower your arms out to both sides in a wide arc until your chest stretches. Breathe in during this part. Tip: The arms themselves stay fixed throughout; the movement happens only at the shoulder joint.
Breathe out and squeeze your chest to bring your arms back to the starting position. Hold the contraction for a second. Tip: Follow the same arc you used to lower the weights.
Do the prescribed number of repetitions.
Incline_Dumbbell_Bench_With_Palms_Facing: Sit back on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand resting on your thighs, palms turned towards each other.
Kick the dumbbells up with the help of your thighs, one arm at a time, until you hold them at shoulder width.

Hold them there with a neutral grip, palms facing one another. Flare your elbows out so your upper arms are level with your shoulders (perpendicular to your torso), and bend the elbows so that upper arm and forearm form a 90-degree angle. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and lower the weights slowly to your sides. Stay in full control of the dumbbells the whole time.

Breathe out and press the dumbbells up with your chest muscles. Lock your arms at the top, hold for a second, then begin to lower slowly. Tip: The way down should take at least twice as long as the way up.
Do the prescribed number of repetitions.
When you finish, rest the dumbbells on your thighs again and then set them on the floor. That is the safest way to put the dumbbells down.
Incline_Dumbbell_Curl: Sit back on an incline bench holding a dumbbell in each hand with arms hanging straight. Keep your elbows close to your torso and turn your palms to face forward. This is your starting position.

Keep your upper arms still, breathe out and curl the weights forward by tightening your biceps. Only the forearms move. Go on until the biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder height. Hold the contraction for a second.
Breathe in and slowly lower the dumbbells to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Incline_Dumbbell_Flyes: With a dumbbell in each hand, lie on an incline bench set no steeper than 30 degrees.
Stretch your arms up above you, elbows slightly bent.
Rotate your wrists so your palms face you. Tip: Your little fingers should be side by side. This is your starting position.

Breathe in and slowly lower your arms out to the sides, keeping them extended and rotating your wrists until your palms face each other. Tip: At the end of the movement your arms are at your sides and your palms face the ceiling.

Breathe out and reverse the motion to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position, rotating your hands until the little fingers are side by side again. Tip: The movement takes place only at the shoulder joint and the wrist. Nothing moves at the elbow.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Incline_Dumbbell_Flyes_-_With_A_Twist: With a dumbbell in each hand, lie on an incline bench set no steeper than 30 degrees.
Stretch your arms up above you, elbows slightly bent.
Rotate your wrists so your palms face you. Tip: Your little fingers should be side by side. This is your starting position.

Breathe in and slowly lower your arms out to the sides, keeping them extended and rotating your wrists until your palms face each other. Tip: At the end of the movement your arms are at your sides and your palms face the ceiling.

Breathe out and reverse the motion to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position, rotating your hands until the little fingers are side by side again. Tip: The movement takes place only at the shoulder joint and the wrist. Nothing moves at the elbow.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Incline_Dumbbell_Press: Sit back on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand resting on your thighs, palms turned towards each other.
Next, lift the dumbbells one at a time, helping them up with your thighs, until you can hold them at shoulder width.
With the dumbbells up at shoulder width, turn your wrists forward so your palms face away from you. This is your starting position.
Keep the dumbbells fully under control at all times. Then exhale and use your chest to press them up.
Lock your arms at the top, hold for a second, then begin lowering the weight slowly. Tip: Ideally, the way down takes about twice as long as the way up.
Do the prescribed number of repetitions.
When you finish, rest the dumbbells on your thighs again and then set them on the floor. That is the safest way to let go of the dumbbells.
Incline_Hammer_Curls: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand. Press your back firmly against the backrest and keep your feet together. Let the dumbbells hang straight down at your sides in a neutral grip. This is your starting position.
Start the movement by bending your elbows, trying to keep your upper arms still.
Curl to the top, pause, then lower slowly to the starting position.
Incline_Inner_Biceps_Curl: Take a dumbbell in each hand, then lean back against an incline bench.
Let your arms hang straight down beside you with the palms turned outward. That is the starting position.

Breathe out and curl the dumbbells up and out to the sides, with your forearms staying in line with the side of your shoulders. Stop when the weights reach shoulder height, beside your deltoids. Tip: At the top you should look much like someone striking a double biceps pose.
Squeeze for one second at the top, then breathe in and bring the dumbbells down slowly along the path they came up, until you are back at the start.
Do as many repetitions as your plan calls for.
Incline_Push-Up: Face a bench or a stable raised platform. Put your hands on its edge, a little more than shoulder width apart.

Step back onto the balls of your feet so that arms and body form straight lines, the arms at a right angle to the body. Bend your arms and bring your chest down to the edge of the bench or platform, with the body held straight.
Press up until your arms are straight. Repeat.
Incline_Push-Up_Close-Grip: Stand in front of a Smith machine bar or a stable raised platform set at a height that suits you.
Grip the bar with your hands right beside each other.
Walk your feet back until your arms and body are straight. That is the starting position.
Bend your arms and bring your chest down to the bar, holding the body in one straight line.
Straighten your elbows and push yourself up to the starting position again.
Incline_Push-Up_Depth_Jump: You need a box roughly 12 inches high for this drill, plus two thick mats or aerobics steps.
Set the steps just wider than your shoulders. Put your feet up on the box and your hands on the floor just inside the steps, so you are in an incline push-up position. That is the starting position.

Bend your elbows to lower yourself, then reverse quickly and push so hard that your hands leave the floor. While in the air, move your hands out onto the steps and bend your elbows to cushion the landing.
Do the same movement again to get back to the starting position.
Incline_Push-Up_Medium: Stand in front of a Smith machine bar or a stable raised platform set at a height that suits you.
Grip the bar with your hands roughly shoulder width apart.
Walk your feet back until your arms and body are straight. That is the starting position.
Bend your arms and bring your chest down to the bar, holding the body in one straight line.
Straighten your elbows and push yourself up to the starting position again.
Incline_Push-Up_Reverse_Grip: Stand in front of a Smith machine bar or a stable raised platform set at a height that suits you.
Grip the bar with your palms turned up and your hands roughly shoulder width apart.
Walk your feet back until your arms and body are straight. That is the starting position.
Bend your arms and bring your chest down to the bar, holding the body in one straight line.
Straighten your elbows and push yourself up to the starting position again.
Incline_Push-Up_Wide: Stand in front of a Smith machine bar or a stable raised platform set at a height that suits you.
Grip the bar with your hands further apart than your shoulders.
Walk your feet back until your arms and body are straight, the arms at a right angle to the body. That is the starting position.
Bend your arms and bring your chest down to the bar, holding the body in one straight line.
Straighten your elbows and push yourself up to the starting position again.
Intermediate_Groin_Stretch: Lie on your back, legs straight. Put a belt, rope or band around one foot and take that leg out to the side as far as it will go. That is the starting position.
Create tension in the groin and hamstring muscles by pulling gently on the belt. After 10-20 seconds, do the other side.
Intermediate_Hip_Flexor_and_Quad_Stretch: With a rope, belt or band looped around one foot, lie face down on the floor.

On the leg you are stretching, bend the knee and extend the hip while you pull on the belt with both hands. Knee and hip should lift off the floor, so that you feel tension in the hip flexors and quadriceps. Stay in the stretch for 10-20 seconds, then do the other leg.
Internal_Rotation_with_Band: Loop the band tightly around a post at elbow height. Stand a couple of feet from it with your right side towards the band.
Take the end of the band in your right hand and keep the elbow tight against your side. A pad or foam roll clamped under the elbow is recommended to hold it in place.
With the upper arm fixed, bend the elbow to 90 degrees so that your hand points away from your torso. That is the starting position.
Rotate the arm inward as in a forehand stroke, without letting the elbow move.
Go as far as you can, pause, then come back to the starting position.
Inverted_Row: Set a bar in a rack at about waist height. A Smith machine works too.
Grip the bar wider than shoulder width and hang beneath it. Keep your body straight, heels on the floor and arms fully stretched. That is the starting position.
Bend your elbows and pull your chest up to the bar. Draw your shoulder blades together while you pull.
Hold briefly at the top, then lower yourself to the starting position.
Carry on for as many repetitions as you want.
Inverted_Row_with_Straps: Attach a rope or suspension straps to a rack or another stable object. Take hold of the ends and hang from them lying face up. Keep your body straight, heels on the floor and arms fully stretched. That is the starting position.
Bend your elbows and pull your chest up to your hands. Draw your shoulder blades together while you pull.
Hold briefly at the top, then lower yourself to the starting position.
Carry on for as many repetitions as you want.
Iron_Cross: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart, a dumbbell in each hand. Raise your straight arms out to the sides to shoulder height, palms facing forward. That is the starting position.
Bend your knees and hips into a squat. On the way down, bring your straight arms together in front of your chest.
Stop when your thighs are about parallel to the floor, with your back straight and your chest up.
Push through your heels to stand up and open your arms out to the sides again. Repeat.
Iron_Crosses_stretch: Lie on your front with your arms stretched out to the sides and your palms flat on the floor. That is the starting position.
Bend one knee and swing that leg over the back of your body, trying to touch the floor close to the opposite hand.
Bring the leg straight back to the start and go quickly into the other leg. Keep alternating for 10-20 repetitions.
Isometric_Chest_Squeezes: Sitting or standing, bend your arms to 90 degrees and bring your palms together in front of your chest. Tip: Keep the hands open, palm against palm, with the fingers pointing forward (at a right angle to your torso).
Press the hands into each other and tense your chest. Build the tension gently and raise it little by little. Breathe normally throughout the contraction.
Hold for as many seconds as recommended.
Then let the tension go slowly.
Take the recommended rest, then repeat.
Isometric_Neck_Exercise_-_Front_And_Back: Keep head and neck neutral (the normal position, head upright and looking ahead) and put both hands on the front of your head.
Push gently forward, tensing the neck muscles, but do not let your head move. Build the tension gently and raise it little by little. Breathe normally throughout the contraction.
Hold for as many seconds as recommended.
Then let the tension go slowly.
Take the recommended rest, then repeat with your hands on the back of your head.
Isometric_Neck_Exercise_-_Sides: Keep head and neck neutral (the normal position, head upright and looking ahead) and put your left hand against the left side of your head.
Push gently to the left, tensing the neck muscles on the left, but do not let your head move. Build the tension gently and raise it little by little. Breathe normally throughout the contraction.
Hold for as many seconds as recommended.
Then let the tension go slowly.
After the recommended rest, do it again with the right hand on the right side of your head.
Isometric_Wipers: Get into a push-up position: weight on hands and toes, body straight, hands just wider than shoulder width. That is the starting position.
Shift your weight to one side as far as you can and let the elbow on that side bend while your body sinks.
Straighten the bent arm to push yourself up again, then drop to the other side.
Carry on for as many repetitions as you want.
JM_Press: Set up as you would for a close grip bench press: lie on a flat bench and hold a barbell at arm's length, arms fully extended and elbows in. Instead of holding the arms perpendicular to the torso, though, position the bar straight above your upper chest. That is the starting position.

From the fully extended position, bring the bar down as in a lying triceps extension, breathing in as you go. At the halfway point, let the bar roll back about one inch: move your upper arms towards your legs until they are perpendicular to the torso. Tip: Keep the bend in your elbows unchanged while the upper arms come forward.
Breathe out and push the bar up again with your triceps, as in a close grip bench press.
Return to the starting position and begin again.
Do as many repetitions as your plan calls for.
Jackknife_Sit-Up: Lie on your back on the floor (or on an exercise mat) with your legs straight and your arms stretched out behind your head. That is the starting position.

Breathe out and fold at the waist, lifting legs and arms at the same time until they meet in a jackknife position. Tip: Keep the legs straight and raise them to roughly 35-45 degrees from the floor; the arms stay straight and parallel to the legs. Your upper body should come off the floor.
Breathe in and bring arms and legs down to the starting position.
Do as many repetitions as your plan calls for.
Janda_Sit-Up: Get on the floor in the basic sit-up position: knees bent to ninety degrees, soles flat on the floor, arms crossed over the chest or at your sides. That is the starting position.

Tense your glutes and hamstrings hard, take a full breath, and come up slowly over a count of three to six seconds while you breathe out slowly. Tip: Tensing the glutes and hamstrings matters, because it switches off the hip flexors through what is called reciprocal inhibition: the muscles opposite to the tensed ones relax.
Breathe in and return slowly and under control to the starting position.
Do as many repetitions as your plan calls for.
Jefferson_Squats: Lay a barbell on the ground.
Step over the bar and stand at the middle of its length.
Bend your knees, keep your back straight, and take hold of the bar in front of you with your right hand. Use a neutral grip, the palm facing left.

Take hold of the bar behind you with your left hand, also in a neutral grip (palm facing right). Tip: Make sure the grip is even. Your torso belongs exactly over the middle of the bar: the right hand in front should be as far from your torso as the left hand behind you.
Stand up straight with the weight. Tip: Keep your feet shoulder width apart, toes turned out a little.

Bend your knees and squat, back straight, until your upper thighs are parallel to the floor. Tip: Hold your back as upright as you can and your head up. Do not let the knees travel beyond the toes. Breathe in on the way down.

Push through your feet to drive back up to the starting position. Tip: Let the bar hang at arm's length, elbows locked with a slight bend. Your arms are only hooks; do not lift with them. The thighs do the lifting, not the arms.
Jerk_Balance: With this drill you learn to drive yourself low enough in the jerk, and it corrects a habit of moving backward during the lift. Start with the bar racked in the jerk position: shoulders forward, torso upright, feet in a slight split.
Start as in a normal jerk: dip at the knees with your torso vertical, then drive up hard, so that momentum rather than your arms lifts the weight.
The rear foot stays where it is: push off it so your body moves forward into a full split while you jerk the weight. Then stand up, weight overhead, to recover.
Jerk_Dip_Squat: This exercise strengthens the dip phase of the jerk. Start with the bar racked in the jerk position, shoulders pushed forward to form a shelf and the bar lightly touching your throat. Set your feet directly under your hips and turn them out as far as is comfortable.

With your torso vertical, dip by bending the knees; let them travel forward and do not move your hips back. Do not dip too deep. Drive hard through your feet to bring the weight back to the starting position.
Jogging_Treadmill: Step onto the treadmill and choose the option you want from the menu. Most treadmills have a manual setting, or you can pick a program. Usually you can enter your age and weight so that the machine estimates the calories you burn. Change the incline to change how hard the workout is.

Treadmills are convenient, good for the cardiovascular system, and usually mean less impact than jogging outdoors. A person weighing 150 lb burns almost 250 calories in 30 minutes of jogging, against more than 450 calories when running. Keep a good posture while you jog and hold the handles only when you need to, for example when stepping off or checking your heart rate.
Keg_Load: For the keg load, set out the number of kegs you want some distance from the loading platform, usually 30-50 feet.
Take the near handle of the first keg and tip the keg on its side so that you can grip the opposite edge of its bottom. Lift it to your chest.

The higher you carry the keg, the faster you should get to the platform. Putting it on your shoulder is usually not allowed. Keep a firm grip on the keg. Move to the platform as fast as you can and load it, extending hips, knees and ankles to get the keg as high as possible.
Go back to the start for the next keg, and repeat until the event is finished.
Kettlebell_Arnold_Press: Clean a kettlebell to your shoulder: extend your legs and hips while you bring the kettlebell up to the shoulder. Your palm should face inward.
Eyes straight ahead, press the kettlebell out and overhead while turning the wrist, so the palm faces forward at the top.
Bring the kettlebell back to where it started, palm facing in.
Kettlebell_Dead_Clean: The kettlebell goes between your feet. Send your butt back with your eyes straight ahead, and you are in the starting position.
Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder: extend your legs and hips while you bring it up, and let the wrist rotate on the way.
Bring the kettlebell down with your back straight and your butt out, so the hamstrings stay loaded.
Kettlebell_Figure_8: Put a kettlebell between your legs and stand with your feet wider than shoulder width. Lean forward by pushing your backside out, with a flat back.
Lift the kettlebell and hand it between your legs to the other hand, which reaches in from behind the legs. Keep passing it back and forth for several repetitions.
Kettlebell_Halo: Stand upright, feet hip-width apart. Grip a kettlebell upside down by the horns so that the bell sits above your hands, close to your chest. Tighten your abdominals and glutes to keep the ribcage down. That is the starting position.
Take the kettlebell up past one ear and on around the back of your head, elbows staying close to the head.
Carry the circle on past the opposite ear and back down in front of your chest to where you started; the bell passes close to your body the whole way.
Do the prescribed number of circles one way, then the same number the other way.
Go slowly and hold your head, hips and lower back still. Take a lighter weight if your lower back arches or the bell drifts far from your head.
Kettlebell_Halo_With_Overhead_Extension: Stand upright, feet hip-width apart. Grip a kettlebell upside down by the horns so that the bell sits above your hands, close to your chest. Tighten your abdominals and glutes to keep the ribcage down. That is the starting position.
Take the kettlebell up past one ear and on around to the back of your head, elbows staying close to the head. Stop there for a moment.
From there, straighten your elbows and press the kettlebell overhead until your arms are straight. Your upper arms stay beside your head.
Under control, bend the elbows to bring the kettlebell back down to the pause position behind your head.
To finish one repetition, carry the circle on past the opposite ear and back down in front of your chest to where you started.

Change the direction of the circle with each repetition. Hold your head, hips and lower back still the whole time. If your lower back arches or you cannot get overhead without leaning back, take a lighter weight or do the halo and the extension as two separate exercises.
Kettlebell_Hang_Clean: Set the kettlebell down between your feet. With eyes straight ahead, send your butt back: this is the starting position.
Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder: extend your legs and hips while you bring it up, and let the wrist rotate on the way.
Lower the kettlebell until it hangs between your legs, with the hamstrings still loaded. Keep your head up the whole time.
Kettlebell_One-Legged_Deadlift: Take a kettlebell by the handle in one hand and stand on the leg of that same side.
Do a stiff legged deadlift on that leg, knee slightly bent: hinge at the hip while the free leg reaches out behind you for balance.
Keep lowering the kettlebell until your body is parallel to the floor, then come back upright.
Kettlebell_Overhead_Triceps_Extension: Take a kettlebell by the horns in both hands, feet hip-width apart. Push it overhead to extended arms, so that the bell hangs behind your hands.
Tighten your abdominals, upper arms vertical and close to your head. You start from here.
Let the kettlebell sink behind your head by bending the elbows. Go only as far as your shoulder mobility allows while the elbows do not flare outward.
Straighten your elbows to press the kettlebell back to the starting position. The upper arms do not move at any point.
While extending, hold the ribcage down and do not arch the lower back.
Kettlebell_Pass_Between_The_Legs: Put a kettlebell between your legs and stand comfortably. Lean forward by pushing your backside out, with a flat back.
Lift the kettlebell and hand it between your legs to the other hand, tracing the shape of a "W". Keep passing it back and forth for several repetitions.
Kettlebell_Pirate_Ships: Stand wide and hold a kettlebell in both hands. Let it hang at waist level with your arms straight. That is the starting position.
Turn to one side and swing the kettlebell up to head height. Pause briefly at the top.
Let the bell drop while you rotate to the other side, and bring it up to head height again.
Carry on for as many repetitions as you want.
Kettlebell_Pistol_Squat: Hold a kettlebell by the horns, picked up in two hands. With one leg held off the floor, squat down on the other leg.
Bend the knee and sit your hips back to squat down, with the kettlebell held up in front of you.
Stay at the bottom for a second, then reverse the movement: drive through the heel, head and chest up.
Kettlebell_Seated_Press: Sit on the floor with your legs spread comfortably.
Bring one kettlebell to your shoulder with a clean.
Push the kettlebell up and out to a lockout overhead, then come back to where you started.
Kettlebell_Seesaw_Press: Bring two kettlebells up to the shoulders with a clean.
One kettlebell goes up in a press.
Lower it and press the other one straight away. Do the same number of reps on each side.
Kettlebell_Sumo_High_Pull: Set a kettlebell on the floor between your feet. Take a wide stance and grip the kettlebell with both hands. Push your hips back as far as you can, knees bent, chest and head up. That is the starting position.
Extend hips and knees and at the same time pull the kettlebell up to your shoulders, lifting your elbows as you go. Reverse the movement to get back to the starting position.
Kettlebell_Thruster: Clean two kettlebells to your shoulders: extend your legs and hips while you pull the kettlebells up, rotating your wrists on the way. That is the starting position.
Bend hips and knees to squat, sinking your hips between your legs. Go as low as you can with your back upright and straight.

At the bottom, change direction and stand up by extending knees and hips, driving through your heels. On the way up, press both kettlebells overhead by stretching your arms straight up; let the momentum of the squat help drive the weights.
Bring the weights back to your shoulders as you start the next repetition.
Kettlebell_Turkish_Get-Up_Lunge_style: On your back on the floor, extend the elbow to press a kettlebell to the top position. Bend the knee on the kettlebell's side.

With the kettlebell locked out the whole time, pivot to the opposite side and let your non-working arm help you drive forward towards the lunge position. Push yourself up to sitting with your free hand, then move on to one knee.
Stand up slowly with your eyes on the kettlebell. Go back the same way to where you started and repeat.
Kettlebell_Turkish_Get-Up_Squat_style: Lie on the floor on your back and bring a kettlebell to the top position by straightening the elbow in a press. The knee on the kettlebell's side is bent.
Pivot to the opposite side and drive forward to the lunge position, helped by your non-working arm. The kettlebell stays locked out throughout.
Push yourself up to sitting with your free hand, then move on to your feet. Look up at the kettlebell and stand up slowly. Reverse the movement to the starting position and repeat.
Kettlebell_Windmill: Put a kettlebell in front of your lead foot, then clean and press it overhead with the opposite arm. For the clean, extend your legs and hips while you pull the kettlebell to your shoulder, rotating the wrist so that the palm faces forward. Then straighten the elbow to press it overhead.

With the kettlebell locked out the whole time, push your backside out towards the side of the locked-out kettlebell. Turn your feet out at a forty-five degree angle from the arm holding the kettlebell. Bend sideways at the hip, backside out, and lean slowly until your free hand can touch the floor. Never take your eyes off the kettlebell above your head.
Pause for a second once you reach the floor, then reverse the movement to the starting position.
Kipping_Muscle_Up: Use a false grip on the rings, so that the base of each palm sits on top of its ring.
Start by swinging your legs back a little.

Answer that swing by driving your legs forward and up, throwing chin and chest back, and pulling with both arms at once. When you get to the top of the pull-up, pull the rings to your armpits and roll your shoulders forward so that your elbows travel straight back behind you. Now you are in the right position to go on into the dip part of the movement.
Stay controlled and stable and straighten your elbows to finish the movement.
Come down to the ground with care.
Knee_Across_The_Body: Lie on the floor with your right leg straight. Bend the left leg and let it drop across your body; your right hand holds the knee down towards the floor. (If you are tight, the knee does not have to touch the floor.)

Rest your left arm comfortably at your side and turn your head to the left. Picture a weight tied to your tailbone: let the tailbone sink back towards the floor while your chest reaches the other way, which stretches your lower back. Change sides.
Knee_Circles: Stand, legs together, hands at your waist.
Circle your knees while breathing normally.
Do as many repetitions as your plan calls for.
Knee_Hip_Raise_On_Parallel_Bars: Get onto the vertical leg raise station: rest your forearms on the pads beside your torso and grip the handles. Your elbows are bent at 90 degrees.
Keep your torso upright, press your lower back into the back pad and let your straight legs hang down toward the floor. This is your starting position.
Breathe out and raise your legs while keeping them straight. Stop when they are about parallel to the floor and hold the contraction for one second. Tip: Do not swing or use momentum at any point.
Breathe in and lower your legs slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Knee_Tuck_Jump: Stand comfortably with a slight bend in your knees. Hold your hands in front of your chest, palms facing down and fingertips touching. This is your starting position.
Drop quickly into a quarter squat and explode straight up without pausing. Pull your knees up toward your chest and try to touch your palms with them.
Jump as high as you can with your knees lifted. Then straighten your legs again for a safe landing and let your knees bend once more to absorb the impact.
Kneeling_Arm_Drill: With this drill you make your arm action more efficient for running. Kneel with your left foot in front and your right knee on the ground. Press down through your front heel so your glutes and hamstrings stay active.
Start blocking with your arms in long swings like a pendulum. Then tighten the arm angle and block the way you would while jogging, build up to a run and finally to a sprint.
In the sprinting motion, speed your hands up forward the moment they pass your hip, so they move as fast as possible.
Change knees and do it again.
Kneeling_Cable_Crunch_With_Alternating_O: Attach a rope to a high cable pulley and lay a mat on the floor in front of it.
With both hands on the rope, kneel roughly two feet back from the tower.
Bring the rope behind your head so your hands are next to your ears.
Leave your hands where they are, tighten your abs and crunch down against the rope until your elbows reach your knees.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then come up slowly and under control to the starting position.
Crunch down again in the same way. Halfway down, start turning one elbow toward the opposite knee.
Hold briefly at the bottom once more, then come up slowly and under control to the starting position.
Do the same movement again, this time turning the other elbow toward the opposite knee.
Keep going through this sequence until failure.
Kneeling_Cable_Triceps_Extension: In front of a high pulley machine, set a bench sideways.
Take a straight bar attachment overhead, palms facing down and hands roughly 6 inches apart.
Turn your back to the machine and kneel down.
Rest your head and the back of your upper arms on the bench, elbows bent and forearms pointing toward the high pulley. You start from here.

Breathe out and push the bar away in a half-circle until your elbows lock and your arms are parallel to the floor. Keep your upper arms close to your head and your elbows in the whole time. Squeeze your triceps hard and hold for one second.
Breathe in and go back slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Kneeling_Forearm_Stretch: Kneel on a mat and put your palms flat down with your fingers pointing back at your knees.
Lean back slowly, palms still flat on the floor, until your wrists and forearms stretch. Hold for 20-30 seconds.
Kneeling_High_Pulley_Row: Use a pulley set above head height and choose a suitable weight. Fix a rope to the cable, kneel a couple of feet away and hold the rope in front of you with both arms straight. This is your starting position.
