Start by bending your elbows and pulling your shoulders all the way back. Draw the rope to your upper chest, elbows pointing out.
Pause for a moment, then go back slowly to the starting position.
Kneeling_Hip_Flexor: Kneel on a mat. Step your right foot forward so its sole is flat on the floor, and stretch your left leg out behind you with the top of the foot resting on the floor.
Move your weight forward until your hip stretches. Hold for 15 seconds, then do the other side.
Kneeling_Jump_Squat: Kneel on the floor with a barbell resting across the back of your shoulders; you can also do this with body weight only. Setting up inside a power rack makes it easier to take the bar out.
With head and chest up, sit your hips back until the glutes touch your feet.
Drive your hips up explosively, with enough power to land with both feet flat on the floor.
Finish the squat: push through your heels and straighten your knees until you are standing.
Kneeling_Single-Arm_High_Pulley_Row: Fix a single handle to a high pulley and choose your weight.
Kneel facing the cable tower and take the handle in one hand with your arm straight. This is your starting position.

Begin with your palm facing forward. Bend your elbow and draw your shoulder blade back to pull the weight down to your torso. Turn your wrist on the way so that your palm faces you at the end of the movement.
Pause briefly, then go back to the starting position.
Kneeling_Squat: Set the bar at the right height in a power rack. Kneel behind it; a mat under your knees can help as padding. Slide under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders. Pull your shoulder blades together and keep the bar tight against your back. Lift the weight out of the rack.
Look straight ahead and sit your hips back until your butt touches your calves.
Reverse the movement and bring your torso upright again.
Landmine_180s: Put one end of a bar into a landmine or wedge it securely into a corner. Load a suitable weight onto the bar.
Lift the bar off the floor with both hands and bring it to shoulder height, arms extended in front of you. Take a wide stance. You start from here.
Turn your trunk and hips and swing the weight all the way down to one side. Your arms stay straight for the whole exercise.
Swing the weight all the way across to the opposite side by reversing the motion.
Keep alternating sides until the set is done.
Landmine_Linear_Jammer: Put a bar into a landmine or, if you have none, wedge it securely into a corner. Load a suitable weight and fit the handle attachment onto the bar.
Lift the bar off the floor and bring the handles to your shoulders. You start from here.
From an athletic stance, squat down by bending at the hips and pushing them back. Keep your arms bent.
Reverse the movement: extend your hips, knees and ankles with power and straighten your elbows at the same time. Do this explosively, going from the squat to full extension as powerfully as you can.
Go back to the starting position.
Lateral_Bound: Get into a half squat, turned 90 degrees to the direction you will travel. This is your starting position.
Shift your weight onto the outside leg, and as you do so let the lead leg swing inward in a countermovement.
Push off right away and extend, trying to bound as far to the side as you can.
As soon as you land, push off the other way and return to where you started.
Do several repetitions, bounding from one side to the other and back.
Lateral_Box_Jump: Stand comfortably with a low box beside you. This is your starting position.
Drop quickly into a quarter squat to trigger the stretch reflex, then reverse at once and jump up and sideways.
Lift your knees high enough for your feet to clear the box easily.
Absorb the impact with your legs as you come down on the center of the box.
Jump down carefully on the far side of the box. Keep going back and forth for several repetitions.
Lateral_Cone_Hops: Set up several cones in a row, a few feet apart.
Your starting position is next to the end of the cones, with your body turned 90 degrees to the direction of travel.
Start the jump with a dip of the knees to trigger the stretch reflex, then reverse at once, push off the ground and jump up and sideways over the cone.
Absorb the landing with your legs and bounce straight into the next jump. Work your way down the row of cones.
Lateral_Raise_-_With_Bands: Stand on an exercise band so that it starts to pull when your arms hang at full length. Hold the handles with a pronated grip (palms facing your thighs), a little narrower than shoulder width. The handles rest against the sides of your thighs. Keep your arms extended with a slight bend in the elbows and your back straight. This is your starting position.

Breathe out and raise the handles out to the sides with your side shoulders. Go on until they are slightly higher than parallel. Tip: Tilt your hands a little on the way up, as if pouring water, and keep your arms extended. Also keep your torso still and pause for one second at the top.
Bring the handles slowly back down to the starting position, breathing in as you do.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Latissimus_Dorsi-SMR: Your starting position: lying on the floor, with a foam roll under one side of your back, just behind the armpit.
Hold the arm of the side you are working behind you and out to the side. Shift your weight onto your lats and keep your upper body off the ground. Hold for 10-30 seconds, then change sides.
Leg-Over_Floor_Press: Lie on the floor and hold one kettlebell by its handle on your chest. Cross the leg of the working side over the other leg. You can stretch your free arm out to the side for support.
Push the kettlebell up until your arm is locked out.
With the kettlebell kept above the elbow, bring the weight down until your elbow touches the ground. Do this for as many repetitions as desired.
Leg-Up_Hamstring_Stretch: To stabilize your spine, lie flat on your back with one knee bent and the foot of that leg flat on the floor.

Raise the other leg into the air. If you are tight, it will not go straight, and that is fine. Extend the knee until the sole of the raised foot faces the ceiling, or gets as close to that as you can.
Slowly straighten your legs as far as you can, then draw the raised leg toward your nose. Change sides.
Leg_Extensions: You need a leg extension machine for this. Pick your weight, sit down with your legs under the pad (feet pointing forward) and hold the side bars. This is your starting position. Tip: Set the pad so it sits on your lower leg, just above your feet. Your upper and lower legs should form a 90-degree angle. An angle below 90 degrees puts the knee over the toes, which loads the knee joint more than it should. If the machine is built that way, find another one, or stop lowering at the 90-degree angle once you are doing the exercise.
Breathe out and straighten your legs as far as they go, using your quadriceps. The rest of your body stays still on the seat. Hold the contracted position for one second.
Breathe in and let the weight down slowly to where you started. Do not go beyond the 90-degree limit.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Leg_Lift: Stand up straight with your feet side by side, about shoulder width apart. Hold on to something sturdy, such as the sides of a squat rack or the top of a chair, to steady yourself and keep your balance.
Keep one leg straight and raise the other behind you, with an ankle weight or without, the way you would in a leg curl, only standing. Exhale during the movement.
Breathe in and lower the raised leg slowly to the floor.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Then do the same with the other leg.
Leg_Press: Sit down in a leg press machine and set your feet on the platform straight in front of you, at a medium, shoulder-width stance. Note: The medium stance trains the legs overall; you can also pick one of the other foot stances.

Release the safety bars that hold the weighted platform and push it all the way up until your legs are fully extended in front of you. Tip: Do not lock your knees. Your torso and legs should form an exact 90-degree angle. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and let the platform come down slowly until your upper and lower legs form a 90-degree angle.
Breathe out and press back to the starting position, pushing mostly through your heels and working with your quadriceps.
Do the recommended number of repetitions and lock the safety pins properly when you finish. A fully loaded platform must not fall on you.
Leg_Pull-In: Lie on an exercise mat with your legs straight. Place your hands beside you with the palms down, or under your glutes. Tip: Hands beside the body is the preferred choice. This is your starting position.

Breathe out, bend your knees and draw your upper thighs in toward your midsection. Keep going until your knees are at about chest height. Tighten your abs during the movement and hold for one second at the top. Tip: Your lower legs (calves) should stay parallel to the floor the whole time.
Breathe in and go back to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Leverage_Chest_Press: Put a suitable weight on the pins and set the seat to your height. When the movement starts, the handles should be level with the lower or middle part of your pectorals.
Lift your chest and head and pull your shoulder blades together. This is your starting position.
Push the handles forward by straightening your elbows.
Pause briefly at the top, then bring the weight back to just above the start position. Keep the muscles under tension: do not let the weight rest on the stops before the set is finished.
Leverage_Deadlift: Put a suitable weight on the pins. Stand exactly between the handles. Take the bottom handles with a comfortable grip, then breathe in and drop your hips. Look straight ahead and keep your chest up. This is your starting position.
Let the weight go back to where you started.
Leverage_Decline_Chest_Press: Put a suitable weight on the pins and set the seat to your height. When the movement starts, the handles should be level with the lower part of your pectorals. Lift your chest and head and pull your shoulder blades together. This is your starting position.
Push the handles forward by straightening your elbows.
Pause briefly at the top, then bring the weight back to just above the start position. Keep the muscles under tension: do not let the weight rest on the stops before the set is finished.
Leverage_High_Row: Put a suitable weight on the pins and set the seat height so you can only just reach the handles above you. Adjust the knee pad so it helps hold you down. Take the handles with a pronated grip. This is your starting position.
Draw the handles toward your torso, bending your elbows and pulling your shoulder blades together.
Pause at the bottom, then let the handles go back slowly to the starting position.
When doing several repetitions, do not let the weight settle fully on the stops, so the working muscles stay under tension.
Leverage_Incline_Chest_Press: Put a suitable weight on the pins and set the seat to your height. When the movement starts, the handles should be level with the upper part of your pectorals. Lift your chest and head and pull your shoulder blades together. This is your starting position.
Push the handles forward by straightening your elbows.
Pause briefly at the top, then bring the weight back to just above the start position. Keep the muscles under tension: do not let the weight rest on the stops before the set is finished.
Leverage_Iso_Row: Put a suitable weight on the pins and set the seat height so the handles are level with your chest. Take the handles with a neutral or a pronated grip. This is your starting position.
Draw the handles toward your torso, bending your elbows and pulling your shoulder blades together.

Pause at the bottom, then let the handles go back slowly to the starting position. When doing several repetitions, do not let the weight settle fully on the stops, so the working muscles stay under tension.
Leverage_Shoulder_Press: Put a suitable weight on the pins and set the seat to your height. When the movement starts, the handles should be level with the top of your shoulders. Lift your chest and head and hold the handles with a pronated grip. This is your starting position.
Push the handles up by straightening your elbows.
Pause briefly at the top, then bring the weight back to just above the start position. Keep the muscles under tension: do not let the weight rest on the stops before the set is finished.
Leverage_Shrug: Put a suitable weight on the pins. Stand exactly between the handles.
Take the top handles with a comfortable grip, then breathe in and drop your hips. Look straight ahead and keep your chest up.

Push your heels into the floor and straighten your hips and knees until you are standing. Your arms stay straight the whole way, and you finish with your shoulders back. This is your starting position.
Shrug your shoulders toward your ears to bring the weight up, in a path that goes straight up and down.
At the top, pause; after that, bring the weight back to where you started.
Linear_3-Part_Start_Technique: With this drill you learn to accelerate into a sprint as fast as possible from a standstill. A line to start from is helpful. Stand with both feet on the line. Set your left foot so its toe is beside your right ankle. Then put your right foot 4-6 inches behind the left.
Set your right hand on the line. Next, lower your nose until it is near your left knee.
Lean forward while you squat down, until your hips are higher than your head and the left leg carries your weight. You are now in the starting position.
Raise your left hand behind you until the arm is parallel to the ground and points backward. Explode out when you are ready.
Linear_Acceleration_Wall_Drill: Lean against a wall at about 45 degrees. Keep your feet together and your glutes tight.
Lift your right knee fast, pause, then drive the foot straight down into the ground.
Change legs: bring the opposite knee up, then attack the ground with a straight downward drive.
Do it one more time with your right leg. The moment the right foot hits the ground, fire off rapid steps, switching left and right as fast as you can.
Linear_Depth_Jump: You need two boxes or benches set a few feet apart. Stand on one box, facing the other platform.
Start by dropping gently to the ground between the two platforms and let your knees and hips bend.
Explode back up to reverse the movement: drive through ankles, knees and hips so that you jump onto the other platform.
Land softly and absorb the impact with your legs.
Log_Lift: Stand with the log in front of you. Take hold of the handles and start to clean the log. While you are bent over at the start of the clean, try to get the log as high as you can and pull it into your chest. Extend your hips and knees to bring it up and finish the clean.

Push your head back and look up, so your chest forms a shelf for the log to rest on. Start the press with a dip: bend your knees slightly and reverse the movement. This push press builds the momentum that gets the log moving vertically. Then straighten your elbows to press the log overhead. Form has no strict rules, so use the technique that is most efficient for you. On every repetition, push your head through as the log goes up and look forward.
Do as many repetitions as you can. Try to control the log on its way back down to the ground.
London_Bridges: Fasten a climbing rope to a cross member or a beam high up. The Smith machine bar underneath must be locked in place with the safeties so that it cannot move; check this. A secure box is an alternative.
Your starting position is standing on the bar, with the rope helping you keep your balance.
With your body held straight, lean back and lower yourself slowly, hand over hand along the rope. Go on until your body is perpendicular to the ground.
Go hand over hand in the opposite direction until you are back at the starting position, with your body still straight.
Looking_At_Ceiling: Get on your knees on the floor and take hold of your heels, one in each hand.
Push your buttocks up and forward and tip your head back to look at the ceiling, so your back arches.
Low_Cable_Crossover: To set up, move the pulleys to the low position, choose the resistance and take one handle in each hand.
Step forward so the cables come under tension. Your palms face forward, your hands are below your waist and your arms are straight. This is your starting position.
Bend your arms slightly and bring your hands up and in toward the midline of your body. They should meet in front of your chest with the palms facing up.
Pause briefly, then return your arms to the starting position.
Low_Cable_Triceps_Extension: Use a seated row machine with a rope attached. Once the desired weight is selected, lie face up on its bench with your head toward the attachment.
Hold the rope ends from the outside with your palms facing each other (neutral grip).

Bend your elbows to 90 degrees and set your upper arms perpendicular (90 degrees) to your torso. Tip: Keep your elbows in. Your upper arms should point at the ceiling and your forearms toward the pulley above your head. This is your starting position.
Breathe out and extend your lower arms until they are straight and vertical. Your upper arms and elbows stay still throughout; only the forearms move. Squeeze your triceps hard for one second.
Breathe in and go back slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Low_Pulley_Row_To_Neck: Take a seat at a low pulley row machine that has a rope attachment on it.

Take the rope ends with your palms facing down. Sit with a straight back and slightly bent knees. Tip: Your back should be almost fully vertical and your arms fully extended in front of you. This is your starting position.

Hold your torso still, raise your elbows and bend them, pulling the rope toward your neck as you breathe out. Your upper arms stay parallel to the floor the whole time. Tip: Go on until your hands are almost beside your ears and your elbows point out, away from your sides. At the end your forearms are not parallel to the floor; they angle slightly upward.
Hold the contraction for about a second, then go back slowly to the starting position as you breathe in. Tip: Once again, your torso should not move at any point.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Lower_Back-SMR: Sit with a foam roll under your lower back, arms crossed in front of you and shoulders protracted. That is the starting position.

Lift your hips off the floor and lean back so your weight rests on your lower back. Then shift slightly to one side, so the weight is on the muscles beside the spine and not on the spine itself. Roll over your lower back and stay on tense spots for 10-30 seconds. Do the same on the other side.
Lower_Back_Curl: Lie face down with your arms out to the sides. This is your starting position.
Extend your spine with your lower back muscles and lift your chest off the ground. Do not push yourself up with your arms. Hold your head up as you move. Do 10-20 repetitions.
Lunge_Pass_Through: Your starting position: standing, torso upright, with a kettlebell held in the right hand.
Take a step forward with your left foot. Bend at the hip and knee to lower your upper body, torso still upright. Go down until your back knee almost touches the ground.
While you lunge, hand the kettlebell over to your opposite hand beneath the front leg.
Come back up to where you started, pushing off through the heel.
Do the recommended number of repetitions, switching legs each time.
Lunge_Sprint: Set the bar of a Smith machine to a suitable height. Get under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders. Lift it out, then split your stance with one foot forward and one foot back. This is your starting position.
Bend your knees and drop your hips, bringing your back knee almost to the ground.
Change direction immediately when you reach the bottom of the descent. Your front heel drives explosively and your back foot adds only light pressure. Jump, and swap the positions of your legs.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Lying_Bent_Leg_Groin: Your starting position: on your back, knees bent, soles of the feet pressed against each other, while your partner holds your knees.
Try to squeeze your knees together while your partner stops any movement.

Once 10-20 seconds have passed, let your muscles relax while your partner pushes your knees gently toward the floor. To prevent injury or overstretching, tell your helper without fail when the stretch is adequate.
Lying_Cable_Curl: Attach a straight bar or an EZ bar to the low pulley. Take it in both hands at shoulder width, palms turned up (underhand grip).
Put an exercise mat in front of the weight stack and lie down on your back. Keep your legs straight and press the soles of your feet against the frame of the machine.
Stretch your arms out, keep the elbows near your sides and bend the arms just a little. You are now in the starting position.
Breathe out and slowly curl the bar towards your chest, tightening the biceps. Your upper arms do not move and your elbows stay near your sides.
Squeeze at the top for a second, then go back slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Lying_Cambered_Barbell_Row: Put a cambered bar on the floor under an exercise bench.
Lie on the bench with your face down. Take the bar wider than shoulder width with your palms turned down (pronated grip). You are now in the starting position.
Breathe out and row the bar upwards with your elbows near your body. Pull to the chest to work the upper middle back, or to the stomach if you want to work the lats.
Hold at the top for a second, then breathe in and lower the bar slowly to the starting position.
Lying_Close-Grip_Bar_Curl_On_High_Pulley: In front of a lat pulldown machine or a high pulley, set down a flat bench.
Take the straight bar attachment at about shoulder width with your palms up (underhand grip).
On your back, position yourself so your head is over the bench's end.
Stretch your arms straight up above your shoulders. Arms and torso form a 90-degree angle, and the elbows point in. You are now in the starting position.

Breathe out and curl the bar down in a half circle until it touches your chin. Squeeze the biceps for a second in this contracted position. Tip: Only your forearms move here. Your upper arms do not move at any point; they stay perpendicular through the whole movement.
Go back slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Lying_Close-Grip_Barbell_Triceps_Extensi: Take a barbell or an EZ bar with a pronated grip (palms facing forward) and lie on your back on a flat bench, your head near the end of it. Tip: Hold a barbell at shoulder width; hold an EZ bar on its inner handles.

Stretch your arms out in front of you. Then, with the arms still straight, slowly move the bar back in a half circle until it is over your head. Your arms are now overhead and parallel to the floor. You are now in the starting position. Tip: Your elbows stay in the whole time.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the bar. Your upper arms do not move. Go down until your forearms are perpendicular to the floor.

Breathe out and push the bar up again in a half circle to the starting position, until your forearms are parallel to the floor too. Tighten the triceps hard for a second at the top. Tip: Once more, only your forearms move. Your upper arms stay still the whole time.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Lying_Close-Grip_Barbell_Triceps_Press_T: Take a barbell or an EZ bar with a pronated grip (palms facing forward) and lie on your back on a flat bench, your head hanging past the end of it. Tip: Hold a barbell at shoulder width; hold an EZ bar on its inner handles.
Stretch your arms out and hold the bar above your chest. Arms and torso form a 90-degree angle, so the arms are perpendicular to your torso. You are now in the starting position.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the bar in a half circle. Your upper arms do not move and your elbows stay in. Go down until the bar touches your chin lightly.

Breathe out and push the bar up again in a half circle to the starting position. Tighten the triceps hard for a second at the top. Tip: Once more, only your forearms move. Your upper arms stay still the whole time.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Lying_Crossover: Lie down on your back and stretch out your legs.

Bend one knee and bring that leg across your body, trying to reach the ground with the knee. Your partner kneels next to you, keeps your shoulder down with one hand and guides the crossed leg with the other. You are now in the starting position.
Try to lift the bent knee from the ground while your partner stops it from actually moving.
Relax the leg after 10-20 seconds and let your partner press the knee gently towards the floor. Do the same on the other side.
Lying_Dumbbell_Tricep_Extension: Lie on a flat bench and hold two dumbbells straight above you. Your arms are fully stretched and form a 90-degree angle with your torso and the floor. Your palms face each other and your elbows are tucked in. You are now in the starting position.
Breathe in and slowly lower the dumbbells until they are close to your ears. Your upper arms do not move and your elbows stay in.
From there, breathe out and lift the dumbbells back to the starting position with your triceps. Again your elbows stay in and your upper arms stay still.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Lying_Face_Down_Plate_Neck_Resistance: Lie face down on a flat bench with your body in a straight line and hold a weight plate behind your head. Tip: Place yourself so that your shoulders are a little past the end of the bench; your upper chest, neck and face are then off the bench. You are now in the starting position.
Hold the plate firmly on the back of your head. Breathe in and slowly lower your head, as if you were nodding "yes".
Breathe out and lift your head in a half circle back to the starting position. Keep the muscles tight for a second.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Lying_Face_Up_Plate_Neck_Resistance: Lie face up on a flat bench with your body in a straight line and hold a weight plate on your forehead. Tip: Place yourself so that your shoulders are a little past the end of the bench; your traps, neck and head are then off the bench. You are now in the starting position.
Hold the plate firmly on your forehead. Breathe in and slowly let your head go back and down in a half circle.
Breathe out and lift your head in a half circle back to the starting position. Keep the muscles tight for a second.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Lying_Glute: Lie down on your back. Your partner kneels next to you.

Bend one leg at the hip and lift it from the floor. Turn the leg until the foot is above the opposite hip and the lower leg is perpendicular to your body. Your partner keeps the knee and the ankle where they are. You are now in the starting position.
Try to press your leg towards your partner, who stops the leg from actually moving.
Relax fully after 10-20 seconds and let your partner push the ankle and the knee gently towards your chest. Tell your helper when the stretch is enough, so that you are not hurt or overstretched.
Lying_Hamstring: Lie down on your back and stretch out your legs. Your partner kneels next to you. Lift one leg towards the ceiling and let your partner hold its ankle. If needed, your partner can support the leg with a shoulder. You are now in the starting position.
While your partner keeps the leg where it is, try to bend the knee and tense the hamstrings for 10-20 seconds.
Now relax the leg and let your partner push it gently towards your head. Tell your helper when the stretch is enough, so that you are not hurt or overstretched. When you are done, change sides.
Lying_High_Bench_Barbell_Curl: Lie face down on a tall flat bench and hold a barbell with a supinated grip (palms up). Tip: Hold a barbell at shoulder width; hold an EZ bar on its inner handles. Place yourself so that your upper chest is over the end of the bench and the bar hangs in front of you, arms straight and perpendicular to the floor. You are now in the starting position.
Breathe out, tighten the biceps and curl the bar up in a half circle. Your elbows stay in and your upper arms do not move. Hold for a second at the top.
Breathe in and go back slowly to the starting position. Tip: Control the weight fully the whole time and do not swing. Remember that only your forearms move during the exercise.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Lying_Leg_Curls: Set the lever of the leg curl machine to your height. Lie face down on the machine so that the lever's pad rests on the back of your legs, a few inches below the calves. Tip: If you can, choose an angled machine and not a flat one, because the angled position recruits the hamstrings better.
Keep your torso flat on the bench, stretch your legs fully and hold the handles at the sides of the machine. Point your toes straight. You are now in the starting position.
Breathe out and curl your legs up as far as you can. Your thighs stay on the pad. Hold for a second when the muscles are fully contracted.
Breathe in and lower your legs to where they started. Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Lying_Machine_Squat: Set the leg machine to a height at which you can get into it with bent knees and your thighs a little below parallel.

Choose the weight, then get into the machine face up, knees bent and thighs a little below parallel to the platform. Your knees must not pass your toes. Hamstrings and calves form an angle of slightly less than 90 degrees, because you start a little below parallel. Your back and head rest on the machine and your shoulders press under the shoulder pads.
Put your hands at the handles. Set your feet shoulder width apart, turned out a little. You are now in the starting position.

Breathe out, push through the balls of your feet and straighten your whole body, tightening the quads. Hold for a second in this contracted position. Tip: Because you start below parallel, you may press your hands on your thighs to help yourself up, but only on the first repetition.
Breathe in and squat down slowly. Do not go all the way to the starting position; stop when your thighs are parallel to the platform. Hamstrings and calves then form a 90-degree angle.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Lying_One-Arm_Lateral_Raise: Take a dumbbell in one hand and lie chest down on a flat bench. For stability, you can hold a leg of the bench with your free hand.
Turn the hand with the dumbbell to a neutral position, palm facing your torso. Keep the arm stretched and the elbow bent a little. You are now in the starting position.

Breathe out and lift the arm with the dumbbell out to the side until the elbow is level with your shoulder and the arm is about parallel to the floor. Tip: The arm stays perpendicular to your torso and stretched through the whole movement. Hold for a second at the top as well.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Lying_Prone_Quadriceps: Lie face down on the floor. Your partner kneels next to you. Bend one knee and lift that leg from the ground, trying to reach your glutes with the foot. Your partner holds the knee and the ankle. You are now in the starting position.
Try to straighten the knee while your partner stops it from actually moving.
Relax the muscles after 10-20 seconds and let your partner push the foot gently towards your glutes. This stretches the quadriceps and the hip flexors further.
Lying_Rear_Delt_Raise: Take a dumbbell in each hand and lie chest down on a flat bench.
Turn your hands to a neutral position, palms facing your torso. Keep your arms stretched and your elbows bent a little. You are now in the starting position.

Breathe out and lift your arms out to the sides until the elbows are level with your shoulders and the arms are about parallel to the floor. Tip: Your arms stay perpendicular to your torso and stretched through the whole movement. Hold for a second at the top as well.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbells slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions, then change to the other arm.
Lying_Supine_Dumbbell_Curl: Lie face up on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Move the dumbbells to your sides. Your arms are straight and your palms face your thighs (neutral grip).

Slowly let your arms sink towards the floor as far as you can. Keep them near your torso, elbows in, stretched with only a small bend at the elbows. When you cannot go lower, fix your upper arms there. You are now in the starting position.

Breathe out and slowly curl the dumbbells up, turning your wrists at the same time until your palms face up. Go on until the biceps are fully contracted and squeeze hard for a second at the top. Tip: Only your forearms move. Your upper arms stay still and your elbows stay in during the whole movement.
Very slowly, come back to where you started.
Lying_T-Bar_Row: Put the weight you want on the T-bar row machine. Set the leg height so that your upper chest is at the top of the pad. Tip: On some machines you can only stand on the step that puts your upper chest at the top of the pad.
Lie face down on the pad and take the handles. Palms down, palms up or palms in: choose by the part of your back you want to stress.
Take the bar out of the rack and stretch your arms out in front of you. You are now in the starting position.

Breathe out, pull the weight up slowly and tighten your back at the top. Tip: Your upper arms stay as near to your torso as they can through the whole movement; this works the back muscles better. Also, never lift your body from the pad, and do not pull the weight up with your biceps.
Hold the contraction at the top for a second, then breathe in and go down slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Lying_Triceps_Press: Lie on a flat bench with your feet on the floor. An EZ bar (preferably) or a straight bar lies on the floor behind your head.

Reach back and take the bar with a medium overhand (pronated) grip. Lift it above you until your arms are straight. Tip: Your arms are perpendicular to your torso and to the floor, and your elbows are tucked in. You are now in the starting position.
Breathe in and slowly lower the bar until it touches your forehead lightly. Your upper arms and elbows do not move.
From there, breathe out and lift the bar back to the starting position with your triceps.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Machine_Bench_Press: Take a seat on the chest press machine and choose the weight.
Press down the machine's foot lever. It brings the handles forward, so that you can take them and stretch your arms fully.

Take the handles with your palms down. Lift your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the floor, out at the sides of your torso. Tip: Because you hold the handles, your forearms point forward. With the handles brought forward and your arms stretched, you are in the starting position.
Breathe in and let the handles come back towards you.
Breathe out and press the handles away, tightening your chest muscles. Hold for a second, then go back to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
At the end, press the foot lever again and bring the handles slowly back to where they were.
Machine_Bicep_Curl: Set the seat to the right height and choose your weight. Rest your upper arms on the pads and take the handles. You are now in the starting position.
Bend your elbows and bring your forearms towards your upper arms.
Stop briefly at the top, then lower the weight slowly to the starting position.
Until the set is finished, do not let the weight go all the way down to the stops. This keeps the working muscles under tension.
Machine_Preacher_Curls: Take a seat on the preacher curl machine and choose the weight.

Rest the back of your upper arms (the triceps) on the preacher pad and take the handles with your palms up (underhand grip). Tip: Keep your elbows in when you lay your arms on the pad. You are now in the starting position.
Breathe out, tighten the biceps and lift the handles. Hold the contraction for a second at the top. Tip: Only your forearms move. Your upper arms stay still and on the pad the whole time.
Breathe in and lower the handles slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Machine_Shoulder_Military_Press: Take a seat on the shoulder press machine and choose the weight.
Take the handles at your sides. Your elbows are bent and in line with your torso. You are now in the starting position.
Breathe out and push the handles up until your arms are fully stretched. Hold the contraction for a second at the top.
Breathe in and lower the handles slowly to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Machine_Triceps_Extension: Set the seat to the right height and choose your weight. Rest your upper arms on the pads and take the handles. You are now in the starting position.
Straighten your elbows and move your forearms away from your upper arms.
Stop briefly at the end of the movement, then let the weight go back slowly to the starting position.
Until the set is finished, do not let the weight go all the way down to the stops. This keeps the working muscles under tension.
Medicine_Ball_Chest_Pass: This exercise needs a partner. If you have none, throw against a wall.
Stand facing your partner and hold the medicine ball in both hands in front of your torso.
Draw the ball in to your chest, then reverse the movement and straighten your elbows to throw. For sports use, you can step forward with the throw.
Have your partner catch the ball and send it back to you with a throw.
Catch it with both hands at chest height.
Medicine_Ball_Full_Twist: You need a medicine ball and a partner. Stand back to back, 2-3 feet from each other. You are now in the starting position.
With the ball held in front of your trunk, turn your shoulders and open your hips simultaneously with your partner.
For a full rotation, both of you twist the same way, for example counter-clockwise.
Hand the ball to your partner. Then both of you twist the other way and repeat.
Medicine_Ball_Scoop_Throw: Stand in a half squat with a medicine ball in your hands. Let your arms hang so that the ball is close to your feet.
Drive your hips forward, straighten your legs and jump up.
As you jump, swing your straight arms up and over your head and let go of the ball at the highest point. Aim to throw the ball as far behind you as you can.
Middle_Back_Shrug: Lie face down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand. Your arms hang down fully stretched and point to the floor. Your palms face each other. You are now in the starting position.
Breathe out, pull your shoulder blades together and hold for a full second. Tip: The movement is the opposite of a hug, or like doing rear lateral raises without arms.
Breathe in and return to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Middle_Back_Stretch: Take a shoulder-width stance and rest your hands on your hips.
Rotate from the waist until a stretch is felt, and stay there for 10 to 15 seconds. Do the same to the other side.
Mixed_Grip_Chin: Take a pull-up bar about 1 inch wider than shoulder width. One palm faces forward, the other faces you. You are now in the starting position.

Breathe out and begin to pull yourself up. Tip: On the side where the palm faces up, focus on doing the movement with the back muscles and keep that elbow near your torso. On the side where the palm faces forward, the elbow is away from the torso but in line with it; there, focus on pulling your body up with the lats.
Hold at the top for a second, then breathe in and come down slowly.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Change the grip on the next set. If your right palm faced you and your left palm faced forward, the right palm now faces forward and the left palm faces you.
Monster_Walk: Put one band around both ankles and a second one around both knees. The bands should be taut when your feet are shoulder width apart.
Start walking forward in short steps, left and right foot in turn.
After a few steps, do the reverse and walk backward to your starting point.
Mountain_Climbers: Start in a push-up position, your weight on your hands and toes. Bend one knee and hip and bring that leg forward until the knee is roughly under the hip. You are now in the starting position.
Switch your legs explosively: stretch the bent leg back until it is straight and rests on the toes, and bring the other foot forward with knee and hip bent. Keep alternating for 20-30 seconds.
Moving_Claw_Series: This drill prepares your running form for better sprinting. While you run, bend the knee and try to kick your glutes as the hip extends.
Load the quad again as the leg swings forward, and attack the ground with the next step.
While you run, block with your arms and punch them through in a fast 1-2 motion.
Muscle_Snatch: Hold a loaded barbell with a wide grip at mid thigh. Your feet are straight below your hips, turned out as much as you need. Lower your hips, keep your chest up and look forward. Your shoulders are just in front of the bar. You are now in the starting position.

Start the pull by pushing through the front of your heels to lift the bar. Go into the second pull by straightening hips, knees and ankles, and drive the bar up as fast as you can. Keep the bar close to your body.
Keep lifting the bar until it is overhead, without bending your knees again.
Muscle_Up: Hold the rings with a false grip: the base of each palm lies on top of the ring. Start a pull-up by bending your elbows and pulling them down to your sides.

When you reach the top of the pull-up, pull the rings to your armpits and roll your shoulders forward, so that your elbows travel straight back behind you. From this position you can go on into the dip part of the movement.
Stay controlled and stable, and straighten your elbows to finish the movement.
Be careful when you let yourself down to the ground.
Narrow_Stance_Hack_Squats: Lean your back against the back pad of the machine and put your shoulders under the shoulder pads.

Set your feet on the platform in a narrow stance, closer than shoulder width, toes turned out a little. The feet are about 3 inches apart or less. Tip: Hold your head up and keep your back on the pad the whole time.
Put your hands on the side handles and release the safety bars. On most machines you do this by turning the side handles from facing front to a diagonal position.
Straighten your legs, but do not lock your knees. You are now in the starting position.

Breathe in and slowly lower the sled by bending your knees. Stay upright, head up, back always on the pad. Go down until upper legs and calves form an angle of slightly less than 90 degrees; your upper legs are then below parallel to the floor.
Breathe out and lift the sled: push against the platform, mostly with your heels, and straighten your legs until you are back in the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Narrow_Stance_Leg_Press: Sit in a leg press machine and put your feet on the platform straight in front of you, in a narrow stance closer than shoulder width, toes turned out a little. The feet are about 3 inches apart or less. Tip: Hold your head up and keep your back on the pad the whole time.

Release the safety bars that hold the loaded platform and press it up until your legs are fully stretched in front of you. Tip: Do not lock your knees. Torso and legs form an exact 90-degree angle. You are now in the starting position.
Inhale while the platform comes down slowly, and stop when there is a 90-degree angle between your upper and lower legs.
Breathe out and return to the starting position, pushing mostly with your heels and working with the quadriceps.
Do the recommended number of repetitions and lock the safety pins properly when you finish. A fully loaded platform must not fall on you.
Narrow_Stance_Squats: For safety, do this lift in a squat rack. Set the bar in the rack at a height that suits you and load it. Then duck under it and rest it across the back of your shoulders, just below your neck.
Grip the bar with a hand on each side. Unrack it by driving up through your legs while you bring your torso upright.

Take a step back from the rack. Set your feet narrower than shoulder width, about 3-6 inches apart, with your toes turned out a little. Look ahead the whole time, because looking down throws you off balance, and keep your back straight. This is your starting position. Note: The stance described here aims at overall development, but you can also choose another stance width.

Bend your knees and lower the bar slowly, staying upright with your head up. Go down until the angle between your thighs and calves is just under 90 degrees, so your thighs end up below parallel to the floor. Breathe in on the way down. Tip: Done correctly, the front of your knees stays in an imaginary straight line with your toes, perpendicular to the front. If your knees travel past your toes, you put needless stress on the knee and the form is wrong.
Breathe out and bring the bar up again: press mainly through your heels into the floor, straighten your legs and return to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Natural_Glute_Ham_Raise: Use the leg pad of a lat pulldown machine or a preacher bench. Kneel on the seat with your back to the machine and hook your ankles under the pads. Stay upright with good posture.
This is your starting position. Lower your body in a controlled way until your knees are nearly straight.
Come back up to where you started, staying in control the whole way.
If you cannot finish a repetition, get help from a band or a partner, or push yourself off a box.
Neck-SMR: Take a muscle roller or a rolling pin and hold it behind your head against your neck. Do not press it straight onto the spine: turn it slightly so it rests on the muscles beside the spine. This is your starting position.
Begin at the top of your neck and roll slowly down along the neck muscles. Where you find a tense point, stay on it for 10-30 seconds.
Neck_Press: Lie on your back on a flat bench. Take a medium-width grip, one that puts your forearms and upper arms at a 90-degree angle halfway through the movement. Unrack the bar and hold it directly above your neck with locked arms. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until it touches your neck.

Pause for a second, then breathe out and press the bar back to the starting position with your chest muscles. Lock your arms, squeeze your chest at the top, hold for a second and lower slowly again. Tip: Lowering should take at least twice as long as pressing up.
Do the prescribed number of repetitions.
Once you finish, put the bar back in the rack.
Oblique_Crunches: Lie on your back on the floor and press your lower back into the ground. Put one hand next to your head and rest the other out to the side on the floor.
Raise your feet and rest them on a flat surface.
Now raise the shoulder on the side of the hand that is at your head.

Lift that shoulder and your upper body until you reach your knee. For example, with your right hand at your head, come up until your right elbow meets your left knee. You can do the same the other way round, bringing your left elbow to your right knee.
Once elbow and knee have met, lower your body back to the starting position.
Breathe in during the eccentric (lowering) phase and breathe out during the concentric (upward) phase.
Keep alternating like this until you have done all recommended repetitions on each side.
Oblique_Crunches_-_On_The_Floor: Lie on your right side with one leg stacked on the other. Bend your knees a little.
Behind your head goes the left hand.
From this position, bring your left elbow up as in a normal crunch, but put the main effort into your obliques.
Crunch up as far as possible and keep the contraction for a second. After that, drop slowly back down to where you started.
Breathe in during the eccentric (lowering) phase and breathe out during the concentric (lifting) phase.
Olympic_Squat: Rest a barbell on top of your traps. Lift your chest and face forward. Stand with your feet hip width apart, turned out as much as you need.

Go down by bending your knees and push your hips back as little as possible. Your knees have to move forward for this; keep them in line with your feet. Aim for a torso that stays as upright as it can. Sink all the way down with your weight on the front of the heel.
As soon as your thighs touch your calves, change direction and drive the weight up.
On-Your-Back_Quad_Stretch: Lying on a step or flat bench, let one arm and one leg hang off the side.
Bend that knee and take hold of the top of the foot. Take care not to arch your lower back while you do it.
Draw your navel toward your spine to stay neutral. Press the foot down and into your hand. For an added hip stretch, raise the hip of the held leg toward the ceiling.
On_Your_Side_Quad_Stretch: Lie on your right side. Bend your right knee to 90 degrees and rest it on the floor in front of you; this steadies your torso.

Take your left foot in your left hand, with the left knee bent behind you. The hip flexor is stretched when you push the left foot back into your hand and press the left hip forward as you do. Then do the other side.
One-Arm_Dumbbell_Row: You need a flat bench with one dumbbell placed on either side.
Your right leg goes on top of one end of the bench and your right hand on the other end, for support. In between, bend your torso forward from the waist until the upper body is parallel to the floor.
Pick the dumbbell up from the floor with your left hand and hold it with your lower back straight. Your palm faces your torso. This is your starting position.

Pull the weight straight up to the side of your chest. Keep your upper arm close to your side and your torso still. Breathe out as you pull. Tip: At the top, focus on squeezing your back muscles. The force should come from your back, not your arms. Your upper torso stays still and only the arm moves. Your forearm only holds the dumbbell, so do not try to pull the weight up with it.
Inhale while the resistance goes straight back down to where you started.
Do the specified number of repetitions.
Do it all again with the other arm after changing sides.
One-Arm_Flat_Bench_Dumbbell_Flye: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting on your thigh. Hold it with a neutral grip.

Kick the dumbbell up with the help of your thigh and hold it in front of you with the working arm fully straight. Keep the neutral grip throughout this exercise. Your free hand holds the side of the bench for more support. This is your starting position.

Bend the elbow of the working arm slightly to spare the biceps tendon. Lower that arm out to the side in a wide arc until your chest feels a stretch. Breathe in during this part. Tip: The arm itself stays fixed throughout; only the shoulder joint moves.
Squeeze your chest muscles and breathe out as you bring the arm back to the starting position. Tip: Follow the same arc you used on the way down.
Hold the contracted position for a second, then do the prescribed number of repetitions.
Change arms and do the exercise again.
One-Arm_High-Pulley_Cable_Side_Bends: Attach a standard handle to a cable tower and move the pulley to its highest position.
Stand side-on to the cable. Reach up with one hand and take the handle with an underhand grip.
Bring the cable down until the handle is by your shoulder and your elbow touches your side.
Set your feet hip-width apart. Put your free hand on your hip so you can feel the pivot point.
Hold your arm fixed in place. Tense your oblique and bring the weight down with a side crunch.
At full contraction, let the weight return slowly to the starting position. Never let the weight stack come to rest; the goal is constant tension during the set.
Keep repeating until you reach failure.
Then turn around and do the same sequence on the other side.
One-Arm_Incline_Lateral_Raise: Lie sideways on an incline bench with a dumbbell in your hand. Press your shoulder against the bench and lay your arm across your body, palm near your navel.
Hold the dumbbell in the arm that is on top, stretched out in front of you and parallel to the floor. This is your starting position.

Do a lateral raise and keep the dumbbell parallel to the floor the whole time. Move your arm straight up until it points to the ceiling. Tip: Breathe out during this movement. Hold the dumbbell there for a second and feel your shoulder contract.
Let the weight down across your body until it is back in the starting position, inhaling as you do.
Do the prescribed number of repetitions.
Change arms and do the movement again.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Clean: Set a kettlebell between your feet. Bend down to grip it with your hips pushed back and your eyes looking ahead.
Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder: straighten your legs and hips while you lift the weight toward the shoulder. Let your wrist rotate on the way up.
Take the weight back to where it started.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Clean_and_Jerk: Grip the handle of a kettlebell.
Clean it to your shoulder: straighten your legs and hips and pull the kettlebell up toward the shoulder. Turn your wrist on the way so your palm faces forward.
Bend your knees for a short dip and keep your torso upright.
Change direction at once and push through your heels, in effect jumping to build momentum. Use that momentum to press the kettlebell overhead, straightening your arm until it locks out.
Catch the weight overhead by dropping back into a squat under it.
Stand up with the weight still overhead. Lower it to the floor before the next repetition.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Floor_Press: Lie on the floor with a kettlebell in one hand and your upper arm resting on the ground. Your palm faces inward.
Turn your wrist while you push the kettlebell up towards the ceiling in a straight line.
Bring the kettlebell down to where you started, then do it again.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Jerk: Take a kettlebell by its handle. Clean it to your shoulder: straighten your legs and hips and pull the kettlebell up toward the shoulder. Turn your wrist on the way so your palm faces forward. This is your starting position.
Bend your knees for a short dip and keep your torso upright.

Change direction at once and push through your heels, in effect jumping to build momentum. Use that momentum to press the kettlebell overhead, straightening your arm until it locks out. Catch the weight overhead by dropping back into a squat under it. Stand up with the weight still overhead.
For the next repetition, bring the weight down.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Military_Press_To_The: Bring a kettlebell to your shoulder with a clean: straighten your legs and hips and pull the kettlebell up toward the shoulder. Turn your wrist on the way so your palm faces inward. This is your starting position.
With your eyes on the kettlebell, push it upward and outward to a lockout overhead.
Lower it under control to your shoulder and repeat. Tense your lat, glutes and stomach hard for more stability and strength.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Para_Press: Bring a kettlebell to your shoulder with a clean: straighten your legs and hips and pull the kettlebell up toward the shoulder. Turn your wrist on the way so your palm faces forward. This is your starting position.
Keep your elbow out to the side as you hold the kettlebell, then push it upward and outward to a lockout overhead.
Lower it under control to your shoulder and repeat. Tense your lat, glutes and stomach hard for more stability and strength.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Push_Press: Take a kettlebell by its handle. Clean it to your shoulder: straighten your legs and hips and pull the kettlebell up toward the shoulder. Turn your wrist on the way so your palm faces forward. This is your starting position.
Bend your knees for a short dip and keep your torso upright.

Change direction at once and push through your heels, in effect jumping to build momentum. Use that momentum to press the kettlebell overhead, straightening your arm until it locks out. Lower the weight before the next repetition.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Row: Set a kettlebell in front of your feet. Bend your knees a little, then push your hips back as far as you can as you lean forward into the starting position. Take the kettlebell and row it to your stomach by drawing your shoulder blade back and bending your elbow. Your back stays straight. Lower the weight and repeat.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Snatch: With a kettlebell on the floor between your feet, get into the proper starting position: knees bent, butt pushed back.
With your eyes straight ahead, let the kettlebell swing back through your legs.

Change direction at once and drive your hips and knees through so the kettlebell speeds upward. When it reaches shoulder height, turn your hand and punch straight up; let the momentum carry the weight to a lockout overhead.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Split_Jerk: Take a kettlebell by its handle. Clean it to your shoulder: straighten your legs and hips and pull the kettlebell up toward the shoulder. Turn your wrist on the way so your palm faces forward. This is your starting position.
Bend your knees for a short dip and keep your torso upright.
Change direction at once and push through your heels, in effect jumping to build momentum. Use that momentum to press the kettlebell overhead, straightening your arm until it locks out.
Catch the weight overhead by dropping into a squat under it, with one leg in front of you and the other behind.
Stand up with the weight still overhead and bring your feet together. Lower the weight before the next repetition.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Split_Snatch: Grip the handle of a kettlebell with one hand.
Squat down toward the floor, then reverse: straighten your hips, your knees and last your ankles to bring the kettlebell overhead.

Once your body is fully extended, drop into a lunge to catch the weight overhead, one leg forward and one back. Drive your hips through and lock the kettlebell out overhead in a single unbroken movement.
Stand up with the weight held overhead and bring your feet together. Lower the weight to get back to the starting position.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Swings: Stand with your feet a little wider than shoulder width and a kettlebell on the floor just in front of you. Push your hips back, keep your back straight and take the handle with one hand.
Swing the kettlebell back between your legs. Keep the working arm straight and hold your free arm out to the side for balance.
Drive your hips forward and straighten your knees so the kettlebell swings up to about chest height. Breathe out as it rises.
Let the kettlebell fall back between your legs under control and go straight into the next repetition. Change arms once your repetitions are done.
One-Arm_Long_Bar_Row: Fix one end of a bar in a landmine or wedge it into a corner so it cannot move. Load a suitable weight on the free end.
Stand beside the bar and grip it with one hand near the collar. Stand up using your hips and legs.
Bend your knees, push your hips back and lift your chest. Your arm is straight. This is your starting position.
Row the weight to your side by drawing your shoulder back and bending your elbow. Do not jerk the weight or cheat.
Pause briefly, then go back to the starting position.
One-Arm_Medicine_Ball_Slam: Your starting position: standing in an athletic, staggered stance, with a medicine ball in the hand that is on your back leg's side.
Wind up your arm and bring the ball above your head. Straighten your hips, knees and ankles at the same time to load up for the slam.
When you reach peak extension, throw the ball hard into the ground directly ahead of you by flexing through hips, spine and shoulders.
When the ball bounces, catch it. Go on like this until you have done the desired number of repetitions.
One-Arm_Open_Palm_Kettlebell_Clean: Between your feet, put down one kettlebell.
Take the handle in one hand and lift the kettlebell fast. Let it flip so that its ball lands in your open palm.
Send the kettlebell out ahead of you with a throw, then catch its handle in one hand.
Bring the kettlebell down to the floor and repeat. Train both arms.
One-Arm_Overhead_Kettlebell_Squats: Clean and press a kettlebell with one arm: straighten your legs and hips and pull the kettlebell up toward your shoulder, turning your wrist on the way. Then straighten your elbow to press the weight overhead. This is your starting position.
Keep your eyes straight ahead, your head and chest up and the kettlebell locked out overhead while you flex at the hips and knees so that your torso lowers between your legs.
Hold the bottom for a second, then push through your heels to stand back up.
One-Arm_Side_Deadlift: Position yourself beside a barbell, level with its middle. Squat down by bending your knees until the bar is within reach.
Take hold of it the way you would pick up a briefcase (the bar lies sideways, so your palm faces you). With a heavy load, a wrist wrap may be needed. This is the starting position.
Breathe out and drive with your legs to raise the barbell. Let your arm straighten completely as the bar comes up, until you are standing upright.
Breathe in and lower the barbell slowly. Tip: Bend your knees as the weight goes down so that you do not get hurt.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Change arms and do the movement again.
One-Arm_Side_Laterals: Take a dumbbell in one hand. With the free hand, hold on to something stable, for example an incline bench. Tilt your body towards the lifting arm, away from the hand on the bench, which helps you stay balanced.
Keep your torso straight and let the dumbbell hang at your side with the arm extended, palm turned towards you. This is the starting position.

Without moving your torso (no swinging), raise the dumbbell out to the side. Keep the elbow slightly bent and tip the hand a little forward, as though you were pouring water into a glass. Go on until the arm is parallel to the floor. Breathe out during the lift and hold at the top for one second.
Breathe in and bring the dumbbell slowly down to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Change arms and do the exercise again.
One-Legged_Cable_Kickback: A leather ankle cuff goes onto a low cable pulley first; after hooking it on, attach the cuff to your ankle.
Stand about two feet away from the weight stack, facing it, and hold the steel frame to steady yourself.

With knees and hips slightly bent and your abs tight, tense your glutes and slowly "kick" the working leg backwards in a semicircular arc, as high as is comfortable, breathing out. Tip: When the leg is fully extended, squeeze your glutes for one second to reach a peak contraction.
Then bring the working leg slowly forward again, holding against the pull of the cable, until you are back in the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Change legs and do the same on the other side.
One_Arm_Against_Wall: Stand and put one bent arm against a wall or a door frame.
Lean slowly toward that arm until your lats feel the stretch.
One_Arm_Chin-Up: First, loop a towel over a chin-up bar.
Take the bar with your palm turned toward you. One hand holds the bar, the other holds the towel.
Lean your torso back by about 30 degrees, arch your lower back and push your chest out. This is your starting position.

Draw your shoulders and upper arms down and back and pull yourself up until the bar touches your upper chest. Breathe out during this part. Tip: At the top, focus on squeezing your back muscles. Your upper torso stays rigid while it travels and only your arms move. Your forearms do nothing more than hold the bar.
Hold the top for a second, then breathe in and lower yourself slowly to the starting position, with your arms fully straight and your lats fully stretched.
Do the prescribed number of repetitions.
Change arms and do the movement again.
One_Arm_Dumbbell_Bench_Press: Lie on a flat bench and rest a dumbbell on your thigh, held in one hand.
Kick the dumbbell up with the help of your thigh and bring it in front of you at shoulder width. Guide it into the right position above you with your free hand.
With the dumbbell at shoulder width, turn your wrist forward until your palm faces away from you. This is your starting position.

Breathe in and lower the weight slowly to your side. Stay in full control of the dumbbell the whole time. Tip: Balancing may be hard at first, so steady the dumbbell with your free hand. Do this only when you need to; otherwise leave that hand resting at your side.

Breathe out and press the dumbbell up with your chest muscles. Lock your arm at the top, squeeze your chest, hold for a second and lower slowly. Tip: Lowering should take at least twice as long as pressing up.
Do the number of repetitions your training program prescribes.
Change arms and do the movement again.
One_Arm_Dumbbell_Preacher_Curl: Take a dumbbell in your right hand and lay your upper arm on the pad of a preacher bench or an incline bench. Hold the dumbbell at shoulder level. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell slowly until your arm is straight and your biceps is fully stretched.

Breathe out and curl the weight up with your biceps until the muscle is fully contracted and the dumbbell is level with your shoulder. For a full contraction, bring your little finger higher than your thumb.
Squeeze your biceps hard for a second at the top, then do the recommended number of repetitions.
Change arms and do the movement again.
One_Arm_Floor_Press: Lie on the floor or an exercise mat with your back flat against it. Bend your knees.

Let a partner pass the bar into one hand. At the start your arm is almost fully straight, as at the start of a barbell bench press. Here, though, you use a neutral grip, with the palm facing your torso.
Keep the hand that is not lifting at your side.
Start by lowering the barbell until your elbow touches the floor. Breathe in here, as this is the eccentric (lowering) phase.
Then press the barbell back up to where you started. Breathe out during the concentric (lifting) phase.
Keep going until all your recommended repetitions are done.
Change arms and do the movement again.
One_Arm_Lat_Pulldown: Choose a suitable weight and set the knee pad so that it holds you down. Take the handle with a pronated grip. This is your starting position.
Pull the handle down: bend your elbow and squeeze it in against your side.
Pause at the bottom, then let the handle return slowly to the starting position.
When you do several repetitions, do not let the weight return all the way, so the working muscles stay under tension.
One_Arm_Pronated_Dumbbell_Triceps_Extens: Lie on your back on a bench and hold a dumbbell at arm's length, with your arm perpendicular to your body. The exercise needs a pronated grip, so your palm faces your feet.
Rest your free hand on the biceps of the working arm for support.
Breathe in and slowly lower the dumbbell.
Then contract your triceps and raise the dumbbell again. Breathe out during the concentric (lifting) phase.
Continue until you have done the repetitions of your set.
Change arms and do the movement again.
One_Arm_Supinated_Dumbbell_Triceps_Exten: Lie on your back on a bench and hold a dumbbell at arm's length, with your arm perpendicular to your body. The exercise needs a supinated grip, so your palm faces your face.
Rest your free hand on the biceps of the working arm for support.
Breathe in and slowly lower the dumbbell.
Then contract your triceps and raise the dumbbell again. Breathe out during the concentric (lifting) phase.
Continue until you have done the repetitions of your set.
Change arms and do the movement again.
Change arms once more and do the movement again.
One_Half_Locust: Lie on the floor, face down.
To pad your hip and pubic bone, slip your left hand beneath the left hipbone.
Your right knee bends, so that your right hand can take hold of the foot.

Raise the foot and lift your shoulders off the floor at the same time. This also stretches the right hip flexor, the chest and the shoulders. Change sides. If your back is fine with it, try it with both arms and both legs at once.
One_Handed_Hang: Take a chin-up bar in one hand with a pronated grip. Your feet stay on the floor or on a step. Let most of your weight hang from that hand while your feet remain on the ground. Hold for 10-20 seconds, then change sides.
One_Knee_To_Chest: Pull one knee to your chest while the other leg is extended straight. Protect the kneecap by gripping under the knee joint.
Pull that knee gently toward your nose.
Do the other side. On the bent leg, this stretches the lower back and buttocks; on the straight leg, the hip flexor.
One_Leg_Barbell_Squat: Stand about 2 to 3 feet in front of a flat bench, with your back to it. A barbell lies on the floor in front of you. Tip: Keep your feet shoulder width apart.
Bend your knees, take the barbell with a pronated grip wider than shoulder width and lift it until it rests on your chest.

Now raise the barbell over your head and set it on the base of your neck. Step back with one foot and rest its toes on the bench. The other foot stays in place in front of you. Look ahead the whole time, because looking down throws you off balance, and keep your back straight. Tip: Keep your back straight and your chest out throughout the exercise.
Breathe in and slowly lower yourself on the front leg until its thigh is parallel to the floor. Your knee is now above your toes and your chest is directly above the middle of your thigh.
Breathe out and come back up to the starting position, leading with your chest and hips and tensing your quadriceps.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Change legs and do the movement again.
Open_Palm_Kettlebell_Clean: Set a kettlebell down between your feet. Clean it: extend your legs and hips and bring the kettlebell up towards your shoulders.
Let go of the kettlebell on its way up so that it flips over and its ball comes to rest in the palms of your hands.
Release the kettlebell so that it goes out in front of you, and catch the handle in both hands. Then bring it back down to where you started and do it again.
Otis-Up: Anchor your feet and lie back on the floor with bent knees. Hold a weight against your chest with both hands. This is the starting position.
Start by flexing your hips and spine so that your torso rises from the floor.
Push the weight upwards on the way up, so that it is overhead when you reach the top.
Reverse the sit-up, bringing the weight back to your chest as you go down. Make sure you do not descend completely to the floor.
Overhead_Cable_Curl: First choose a comfortable weight on both sides of the cable machine. Note: The weight must be the same on each side.
Then set the pulleys on both sides to a height above your shoulders.

Stand in the middle between the two sides and take each handle with an underhand grip (palms towards the ceiling). Stretch your arms out fully, parallel to the floor, and place your feet shoulder-width apart. Your body should be in line with the handles. This is the starting position.
Breathe out and slowly contract the biceps on both sides until forearms and biceps touch.
Breathe in and bring your forearms back to the starting position. Note: Apart from the forearms, your whole body stays still in this exercise.
Do the number of repetitions your program prescribes.
Overhead_Lat: Sit upright on the floor, your partner behind you. Lift one arm straight up and bend the elbow, trying to reach your back with your hand. Your partner holds your triceps and wrist. This is the starting position.
Try to pull your upper arm down to your side while your partner stops you from actually doing it.
Relax the arm once 10-20 seconds have passed. Your partner then stretches the lat further by pressing gently on the tricep. Stay for 10-20 seconds before you switch sides.
Overhead_Slam: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, a medicine ball in both hands. This is the starting position.
Start the countermovement: lift the ball overhead and stretch your body out fully.
Then reverse and slam the ball onto the ground right in front of you with all your strength.
Catch the ball with both hands as it bounces and do the movement again.
Overhead_Squat: Begin with a barbell on the floor in front of you. Place your feet wider than shoulder-width apart.

Bend your knees and take the barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing you). Before you lift, set your hands wider than shoulder-width apart. When you are in position, raise the barbell until it rests on your chest.

Bring the barbell overhead and slightly behind your head, with your arms fully extended. Hold your head up the whole time and keep your back straight. Pull your shoulder blades together. This is the starting position.

Breathe in and slowly lower the weight by bending your knees until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Tip: A straight back throughout the exercise prevents injuries, and your arms stay extended above your head the whole time.
Then breathe out and push through your feet and legs to bring the weight back up to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Overhead_Stretch: Stand up straight, interlace your fingers and turn your palms towards the ceiling. Stretch your arms upwards while your shoulders stay down.
For a stretch of the whole torso, draw your tailbone downwards and hold your torso stable as you do so. Stretch the muscles at the front as well as at the back of the torso.
Overhead_Triceps: Sit upright on the floor, your partner behind you. Lift one arm straight up and bend the elbow, trying to reach your back with your hand. Your partner holds your elbow and wrist. This is the starting position.
Try to straighten the arm up into the air while your partner stops you from actually doing it.
Once 10-20 seconds have passed, let the arm relax. Your partner now presses gently on the wrist, which stretches the tricep further. Stay for 10-20 seconds before you switch sides.
Pallof_Press: Attach a standard handle to a cable tower and, if you can, set the cable at shoulder height. Otherwise a low pulley will do.
Stand side-on to the cable, take the handle in both hands and step away from the tower. Stand roughly an arm's length from the pulley, so that the weight keeps the cable under tension.
Your starting position: feet hip-width apart, knees slightly bent, and the cable held at the middle of your chest.
Push the cable away from your chest until both arms are fully extended. Keep your core tight and engaged.
Hold for several seconds, then go back to the starting position.
When the set is finished, do it again facing the other way.
Pallof_Press_With_Rotation: Set the cable of a tower to the height of your shoulders and hook a standard handle onto it.

Stand side-on to the cable, take the handle in one hand and step away from the tower. Stand roughly an arm's length from the pulley, so that the weight keeps the cable under tension. Line your outstretched arm up with the cable.
With feet hip-width apart, draw the cable in to your chest and take the handle with your other hand as well. Both hands are now on the handle.
Looking straight ahead, push the cable away from your chest. Keep your core tight and engaged.
Twist your torso away from the pulley through a full quarter rotation while your hips stay straight.
Keep your stance rigid and your arms straight. Come back to the neutral position slowly and under control. Your arms are extended in front of you.
While the sideways tension still works your core, bring your hands to your chest and press out again at once until the arms are fully extended. That is one rep.
Carry on with repetitions until failure.
Then set yourself up again and do the same sequence of movements on the opposite side.
Palms-Down_Dumbbell_Wrist_Curl_Over_A_Be: On one side of a flat bench, lay down two dumbbells to begin with.
Go down on both knees, facing the flat bench.
Pick up both dumbbells with a pronated grip (palms facing down) and lift them so that your forearms lie on the flat bench. Let your wrists hang over the edge.
Begin by curling your wrists up as you breathe out.
Breathe in and slowly let your wrists down to the starting position.
Keep your forearms still: the wrists are the only part that moves in this exercise.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Palms-Down_Wrist_Curl_Over_A_Bench: On one side of a flat bench, lay down a barbell to begin with.
Go down on both knees, facing the flat bench.
Pick up the barbell with a pronated grip (palms down) and lift it so that your forearms lie on the flat bench. Let your wrists hang over the edge.
Begin by curling your wrists up as you breathe out.
Breathe in and slowly let your wrists down to the starting position.
Keep your forearms still: the wrists are the only part that moves in this exercise.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Palms-Up_Barbell_Wrist_Curl_Over_A_Bench: At one side of a flat bench, set a barbell down as your first step.
Go down on both knees, facing the flat bench.
Pick up the barbell with a supinated grip (palms up) and lift it so that your forearms lie on the flat bench. Let your wrists hang over the edge.
Begin by curling your wrists up as you breathe out.
Breathe in and slowly let your wrists down to the starting position.
Keep your forearms still: the wrists are the only part that moves in this exercise.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Palms-Up_Dumbbell_Wrist_Curl_Over_A_Benc: At one side of a flat bench, set two dumbbells down as your first step.
Go down on both knees, facing the flat bench.
Pick up both dumbbells with a supinated grip (palms up) and lift them so that your forearms lie on the flat bench. Let your wrists hang over the edge.
Begin by curling your wrists up as you breathe out.
Breathe in and slowly let your wrists down to the starting position. Take care to breathe in during this part of the exercise.
Keep your forearms still: the wrists are the only part that moves in this exercise.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Parallel_Bar_Dip: Stand between two parallel bars. Put one hand on each bar and hop up a little to reach the starting position with your arms locked out.
Start by bending your elbows and lower your body until your arms pass 90 degrees. Do not swing, and hold a good posture all the way down.
Reverse the movement: straighten your elbows and push yourself back up to the starting position.
Carry on until you have done as many repetitions as you want.
Pelvic_Tilt_Into_Bridge: Lie on your back with your feet on the floor and your heels right below your knees.
To stretch your lower back, send just your tailbone up toward the ceiling. (The entire spine stays down for now.) Pull your stomach in.
To move into a bridge, raise the whole spine apart from the neck.
Peroneals-SMR: Lie on your side. Support your weight on your forearm and on a foam roller under the outer side of your lower leg. Your top leg can rest on the bottom leg or be crossed in front of you. This is the starting position.
Lift your hips off the ground and roll along the side of the leg from below the knee to above the ankle. Stop at tense points for 10-30 seconds. Do the same on the other leg.
