Peroneals_Stretch: Sit down and loop a belt, rope or band around one foot. This is the starting position.
Extend the leg and keep its heel off the ground. Invert the foot by pulling on the belt, which draws the inside of the foot towards you. Stay for 10-20 seconds before you switch sides.
Physioball_Hip_Bridge: Lie back on a ball so that it supports your upper back while your hips are free. Place both feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart or wider. This is the starting position.
Start by extending your hips with your glutes and hamstrings, so that the hips rise into a bridge.
Hold briefly at the top, then go back to the starting position.
Pin_Presses: Pin presses take the eccentric phase out of the bench press and so build starting strength. You can also use them to train a chosen range of motion.

Set the bench up inside a power rack. Put the pins at the point of your range of motion you want, be it only the lockout or an inch above your chest. Move the bar onto the pins and get it ready for the lift.

Lie down on the bench with the bar right above the point where it touches you in a regular bench press. Tuck your feet under you and arch your back. Using the bar to help carry your weight, raise your shoulders off the bench and retract them, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Push with your feet to drive your traps into the bench. Hold this tight body position for the whole movement.
Your grip can be a standard bench grip, or shoulder width if the triceps are to be the focus. At all times, keep elbow, wrist and bar in line. Think about squeezing the bar and try to pull it apart.
Press the bar up as forcefully as you can. Keep your elbows tucked in until lockout.
Lower the bar back onto the pins and pause before the next repetition.
Piriformis-SMR: Sit on a foam roll with your buttocks. Bend your knees and cross one leg so that its ankle lies over the other knee. This is the starting position.

Lean your weight towards the side of the crossed leg and roll over the buttock until you feel tension in the upper glute. You can help the stretch by pulling the bent knee towards your chest with one hand. Stay there for 10-30 seconds, then change sides.
Plank: Lie face down on the floor and support your weight on your toes and forearms. Your arms are bent and sit right under your shoulders.
Hold your body in a straight line the whole time and stay in this position for as long as you can. To make it harder, lift an arm or a leg.
Plate_Pinch: Take two plates with wide rims and place them together, smooth sides turned outwards.
Hold the two plates together with your fingers on the outside of one plate and your thumb on the other side. This is the starting position.
Press the plates together with fingers and thumb. Hold for as long as you are able to.
Do the number of sets your program prescribes.
Change arms and do the movements again.
Plate_Twist: On the floor or an exercise mat, lie down with your upper body upright and your legs extended fully. With your arms slightly bent, hold the plate by its sides in both hands, out in front of your abdominals.

Slowly cross your legs near the ankles and raise them off the ground. Bend your knees slightly as well. Note: Lean your upper body back a little to help you stay balanced during the exercise. This is the starting position.
Bring the plate over to your left side and touch the floor with it, breathing out as you do.
Breathe in as you return to the starting position, then do the same movement to the right side of your body. Tip: Move slowly and under control the whole time. Jerky movements can injure your back.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Platform_Hamstring_Slides: You need a wooden floor or something similar for this movement. Lie on your back with your legs stretched out. Put a gym towel or a light weight under your heel. This is the starting position.
Start by bending the knee while the other leg stays straight.
Keep drawing the heel towards you, sliding it along the floor.
When the knee is fully bent, reverse the movement and go back to the starting position.
Plie_Dumbbell_Squat: Stand up straight and hold a dumbbell by its base with both hands. Set your legs wider than shoulder-width apart, with your knees slightly bent.
Point your toes outwards. Note: Your arms stay still during the exercise. This is the starting position.
Bend your knees slowly and go down until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Breathe in here, since this is the eccentric part of the exercise.
Push mostly through your heels to bring your body back up to the starting position, breathing out.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Plyo_Kettlebell_Pushups: With a kettlebell on the floor, take a pushup position: toes down, elbows extended, one hand holding the kettlebell and one hand on the ground. That is the starting position.
With a straight back, go down as low as you can to begin.
Reverse quickly and forcefully and push yourself up and over to the other side of the kettlebell, changing hands on the way. Go down again and keep repeating the movement from side to side.
Plyo_Push-up: Get down on the floor face down and carry your weight on your hands and toes.
Extend your arms fully, hands about shoulder-width apart. Your body stays straight during the whole movement. This is the starting position.
Go down by bending your elbows, bringing your chest towards the ground.
At the lowest point, reverse and push yourself up as fast as you can by extending your elbows. Try to push your upper body so high that your hands come off the ground.
Go back to the starting position and do the exercise again.
To make it harder, clap your hands while you are in the air.
Posterior_Tibialis_Stretch: Sit down and loop a belt, rope or band around one foot. This is the starting position.
Extend the leg and keep its heel off the ground. Evert the foot by pulling on the belt, which draws the outside of the foot towards you. Stay for 10-20 seconds before you switch sides.
Power_Clean: Place your feet a little wider than shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly outwards.
Go down into a squat and take a closed, pronated grip on the bar. Grip slightly wider than shoulder width, with your hands outside the knees and the elbows extended fully.
Position the bar over the balls of your feet, roughly 1 inch away from the front of your shins.
Retract your shoulder blades, hold your chest up and out, and have a back that is flat or arched slightly.
Hold your head neutral (in line with the spine, neither tilted nor rotated) and look straight ahead. Breathe in during this phase.

Breathe out and lift the bar off the floor by extending hips and knees forcefully. Tip: Your upper torso keeps the same angle. Do not bend at the waist yet, and do not let your hips rise before your shoulders (that would push the glutes into the air and stretch the hamstrings).
Your elbows stay fully extended, your head neutral and your shoulders over the bar.
While the bar rises, keep it as near to your shins as you can.
When the bar passes your knees, thrust your hips forward and bend your knees slightly so that they do not lock. Tip: Your thighs should now be against the bar.
Your head stays neutral, your elbows fully extended and your back flat or arched slightly. Tip: Your breath is held until the next phase.
Breathe in, then extend your hips and knees forcefully and quickly and rise onto your toes.

Keep the bar as near to your body as you can. Tip: Your back is flat, your elbows point out to the sides and your head is neutral. Also keep your shoulders over the bar and your arms straight for as long as possible.
Once the joints of your lower body are fully extended, shrug your shoulders up rapidly, without bending the elbows yet. Breathe out in this part of the movement.
When your shoulders are at their highest point, bend your elbows to start pulling your body under the bar.

Keep pulling with your arms as high and as long as you can. Tip: Because this phase is explosive, your torso will be upright or your back arched, your head tilted back slightly, and your feet may leave the floor.
Once the bar is close to its maximal height and your lower body has extended fully, pull yourself under the bar while your arms rotate around and under it.
At the same time, bend your hips and knees into a quarter squat.

As soon as your arms are under the bar, inhale. Then bring the elbows up so that your upper arms are parallel to the floor, and rack the bar across the front shoulder muscles and the front of the collar bones.
Catch the bar with an upright, tight torso, a neutral head and your feet flat. Breathe out during this movement.
Stand up by extending hips and knees until you are fully upright.
To lower the bar, gradually ease the tension in your arm muscles so that the bar descends to your thighs under control. Breathe in during this movement.
At the same time, bend your hips and knees to cushion the bar's impact on the thighs.
With your elbows extended fully, squat down until the bar is touching the floor.
Begin again at phase 1 and do the recommended number of repetitions.
Power_Clean_from_Blocks: Set a barbell on boxes of the height you want and grip it just outside your legs. Drop your hips with your weight on the heels, back straight, head facing forward, chest up and shoulders just in front of the bar. This is the starting position.
Start the first pull by pushing through your heels and extending your knees. Keep the angle of your back unchanged and your arms straight. When the bar nears mid-thigh, start to extend your hips.

Accelerate as if jumping: extend hips, knees and ankles and use speed to send the bar upwards. You should not need to pull actively with your arms to accelerate the weight. When the second pull ends, your body is fully extended and leans back slightly, arms still straight.

On reaching full extension, move into the third pull: shrug hard and bend your arms, elbows up and out. At peak extension, pull yourself far enough under the bar to rack it on your shoulders, turning your elbows under the bar as you go. Rack the bar on the protracted shoulders, where it lightly touches the throat, with relaxed hands.
Recover at once by pushing through your heels, torso upright and elbows up. Keep going until you stand, and finish the repetition by putting the weight back on the boxes.
Power_Jerk: Stand with the weight racked on the front of your shoulders and start with the dip. Feet right under your hips, bend your knees without letting the hips move back. Dip only a little, then reverse as powerfully as you can.
Push through your heels to produce as much speed and force as you can, and make sure your head is out of the way when the bar leaves your shoulders.

The moment your feet leave the floor, get them into the receiving position as fast as you can. In the short moment when your feet are not pushing against the platform, your effort to press the bar up drives you down. Move your feet to a slightly wider stance, knees partly bent.
Catch the bar overhead with locked-out arms.
Power_Partials: Stand with an upright torso and a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging at full length. Keep your elbows close to your torso.
Turn your palms towards your torso and place your feet about shoulder-width apart. This is the starting position.
With straight arms and a still torso, breathe out and raise the weights out to the sides to about shoulder height.

Feel the contraction for one second, then breathe in and lower the weights to the starting position. Tip: While raising and lowering, keep your palms facing down and the little finger slightly higher; this puts the stress mainly on your shoulders.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Power_Snatch: Start with a loaded barbell on the floor. Stand so that the bar is close to your shins or touches them, and take a wide grip. Place your feet right under your hips, turned out as much as you need. Drop your hips, chest up, eyes forward. Your shoulders are just in front of the bar. This is the starting position.
Start the first pull by pushing through the front of your heels to lift the bar off the ground. Keep the angle of your back unchanged until the bar is past your knees.

Move into the second pull: extend hips, knees and ankles and drive the bar up as fast as you can. Keep the bar close to your body. At peak extension, shrug your shoulders and let your elbows bend out to the sides.

While your feet move to the receiving position, which is slightly wider, pull yourself under the bar and lift it overhead. Receive the bar in a partial squat. Keep raising it until you hold it locked out overhead.
Stand up again with the weight overhead.
Power_Snatch_from_Blocks: Load a barbell and rest it on boxes or stands set to the height you want. Take hold of it with a wide grip. Stand with your feet straight under your hips and turn them out as far as you need. Sink your hips while your chest stays high and your eyes look ahead. Your shoulders sit slightly ahead of the bar and your elbows point outward. This is the starting position.
Start the first pull: push through the front part of your heels and lift the bar off the boxes.

Move into the second pull by straightening your hips, knees and ankles so the bar shoots up as fast as you can make it. Keep it near your body. Once you are fully stretched out, shrug your shoulders and let your elbows bend out to the sides.

While your feet shift to the receiving position, pull yourself hard under the bar and bring it up overhead. Your feet land just outside your hips, turned out as far as needed. Catch the bar with your arms locked out overhead, above a full squat.
Hold the bar over the front of your heels, keep head and chest high, and push through your heels until you are standing. Set the weight back on the boxes with care.
Power_Stairs: Power stairs means carrying implements up a staircase. In training, a tire or a box does the job.
Grip the implement with both hands. Take a wide stance and keep your head and chest high. Push your heels into the ground and straighten knees and hips to lift the weight off the floor.
Lean back and try to swing the weight up onto the step, which is usually about 16-18" high. Your legs may help to push the weight onto the step.
Do 3-5 repetitions, then carry on with a heavier weight, moving as quickly as you can.
Preacher_Curl: You need a preacher bench and an E-Z bar for this exercise. Take the bar at its narrow inner grips; ideally someone hands it to you, otherwise pick it up from the bar rest at the front that most preacher benches have. Your palms face forward and, because of the bar's shape, tilt slightly inward.
Press your upper arms and your chest against the pad of the bench and hold the bar at shoulder height. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until your arms are stretched out and you feel a full stretch in the biceps.
Breathe out and curl the weight up with your biceps until the muscle is fully tightened and the bar has reached shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps firmly and stay there for one second.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Preacher_Hammer_Dumbbell_Curl: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms turned toward each other (neutral grip) and lay both upper arms on the pad of the preacher bench.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbells slowly until your arms are stretched out and the biceps is at full stretch.
Breathe out and curl the weight up with your biceps until the muscle is fully tightened and the dumbbells are level with your shoulders.
At the top, squeeze the biceps firmly for one second, then repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Press_Sit-Up: Lie back on an abdominal bench and rest a barbell on your chest. Hook your legs firmly into the leg support of the bench. This is the starting position.

Breathe in and tense your abs and glutes. Then, breathing out, curl your torso up as in a sit-up and at the same time press the barbell overhead. Tip: Let your arms push the barbell out during the movement, but keep your attention on the abdominal muscles.
Bring your upper body down to the starting position again and let the barbell come back to your torso. Breathe in on the way down.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Prone_Manual_Hamstring: This exercise needs a partner. Lie on your stomach with straight legs. Your partner puts a hand on your heel.
Bend your knee to curl the leg upward. Your partner pushes against it, lightly at first and harder as the movement goes on. Talk to each other so the resistance stays at the right level.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring the leg back to the start while your partner now resists in the opposite direction.
Prowler_Sprint: Set the sled on a suitable surface and load it with a fitting weight. It should be heavy enough that you have to work, yet not so heavy that it slows you down noticeably.
Use either the upright or the low handles. Grip them with straight arms and lean into the sled.
Keep a good posture and push off the ground with short, alternating steps. Go as fast as you can over a short distance.
Pull_Through: Attach a rope or handle to a low pulley and stand a few feet in front of it. Turn your back to the machine and set your feet wide apart with the cable running between your legs.

Start by bending at the hips and reaching back between your legs as far as you can. Your knees stay slightly bent. With straight arms, straighten your hips until you stand fully upright. Do not pull upward with your shoulders; the whole movement comes from the hips.
Pullups: Take the pull-up bar with your palms facing forward in the grip your plan calls for. Note: In a wide grip your hands are further apart than your shoulders. In a medium grip they are as far apart as your shoulders, and in a close grip they are closer together than your shoulders.
Hang from the bar with both arms stretched out at the grip width you chose, lean your torso back by about 30 degrees, arch your lower back and push your chest out. This is your starting position.

Draw your shoulders and upper arms down and back to pull your torso up until the bar touches your upper chest. Breathe out during this part. Tip: At the top, focus on squeezing your back muscles. Your upper torso stays rigid while it travels, and only your arms move. Your forearms do nothing more than hold the bar.
Stay at the top for one second, then begin to breathe in and lower your torso slowly to the starting position, where your arms are fully straight and your lats fully stretched.
Repeat the movement for the planned number of repetitions.
Push-Up_Wide: Place your hands far apart and hold yourself up on hands and toes in a plank. Your elbows are straight and your body forms a line. Don't let your hips drop. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and bend your elbows so your chest sinks toward the floor.
Straighten your elbows and push your upper body back up to the start with your chest muscles. Breathe out as you do so.
Pause at the top with your muscles tight, then repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Push-Ups_-_Close_Triceps_Position: Lie face down on the floor and set your hands narrower than shoulder width, in a close hand position. Hold your torso up with your arms straight.
Breathe in and lower yourself until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Push your upper body back up to the start with your triceps and part of your chest muscles, and squeeze your chest. Breathe out as you do so.
Pause for a second at the top with your muscles tight, then repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Push-Ups_With_Feet_Elevated: Lie face down on the floor, set your hands about 36 inches apart and hold your torso up with your arms straight.
Put your toes on a flat bench so that your body is raised. Note: The higher the bench, the harder the exercise becomes.
Breathe in and lower yourself until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Push your upper body back up to the start with your chest muscles and squeeze your chest. Breathe out as you do so.
Pause for a second at the top with your muscles tight, then repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Push-Ups_With_Feet_On_An_Exercise_Ball: Lie face down on the floor, set your hands about 36 inches apart and hold your torso up with your arms straight.
Put your toes on an exercise ball so that your body is raised.
Breathe in and lower yourself until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Push your upper body back up to the start with your chest muscles and squeeze your chest. Breathe out as you do so.
Pause for a second at the top with your muscles tight, then repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Push_Press: Stand with your feet about hip width apart and hold the barbell on the front of your shoulders, hands slightly wider than your shoulders and elbows a little in front of the bar.
Bend your knees slightly for a short dip, keeping your torso upright and your heels on the floor.
Drive up hard through your legs and use that momentum to press the bar overhead until your arms are locked out.
Lower the bar under control back to your shoulders, cushioning it with your knees, and repeat.
Push_Press_-_Behind_the_Neck: Stand with the bar resting on the back of your shoulders and start with the dip. Feet straight under your hips, bend your knees without letting your hips travel backward. Dip only a little, then turn the movement around as explosively as you can. Push through your heels to build as much speed and force as possible and move the bar straight up.
Use that momentum and straighten your arms to finish pressing the weight overhead.
Come back to the starting position and let your legs cushion the impact.
Push_Up_to_Side_Plank: Set up for a push-up on your toes, hands slightly wider than your shoulders.
Bend your elbows to do a push-up. Your body stays in a straight line on the way down.
After one push-up, as you rise, shift your weight to the left side of your body and rotate sideways, lifting your right arm toward the ceiling into a side plank.
Put the arm back down on the floor, do one more pushup, and this time twist to the opposite side.
Keep going, switching sides each time, for 10 or more reps.
Pushups: Get face down on the floor, set your hands about 36 inches apart and hold your torso up with straight arms.
Then breathe in and sink down until your chest is just above the floor.
Now exhale and push your upper body up to the start again, squeezing your chest as you go.
Pause briefly at the top with your chest tight, then start lowering yourself again, for as many repetitions as you need.
Pushups_Close_and_Wide_Hand_Positions: Lie face down with your body straight and your toes on the floor. For the wide hand position, set your hands wider than your shoulders; for the close hand position, set them narrower than your shoulders. Hold your torso up with your arms straight.
Breathe in and lower yourself until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Push your upper body back up to the start with your chest muscles and squeeze your chest. Breathe out as you do so.
Pause for a second at the top with your muscles tight, then repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Pyramid: Roll forward over the ball with your torso until your hips lie on top of it and are the highest point of your body.

Put your hands and feet on the floor. Depending on the ball's size, your flexibility and how long your limbs are, your arms and legs may be straight or slightly bent. The position also builds stabilizing strength in your torso and shoulders.
Quad_Stretch: Lie on your side. Put a belt, rope or band around the foot of your upper leg. Bend the knee and stretch the hip, trying to bring the foot to your glutes while your hands hold the belt. This is your starting position.
Hold the belt over your shoulder or above your head and pull gently to deepen the stretch in the quadriceps. Stay for 10-20 seconds, then change sides.
Quadriceps-SMR: Lie face down on the floor, propped on your hands or forearms. Put a foam roll under the quadriceps of one leg and keep that foot off the floor. Let the leg go as loose as you can. This is your starting position.
Put as much weight on that leg as you can tolerate and roll from just above the knee to just below the hip, stopping on tense spots for 10-30 seconds. Change sides.
Quick_Leap: Stand facing the box, 1-2 feet away from its edge.
Use your hips to hop onto the box and land on both legs. Make sure your legs are bent and your feet are flat when you land.
The moment you land, stretch your whole body out and swing your arms overhead to explode off the box. Let your legs cushion the landing.
Rack_Delivery: With this drill you learn to bring the barbell into the rack position on your shoulders. Hold a bar in the scarecrow position: upper arms parallel to the floor, forearms hanging down. Take a hook grip, fingers wrapped over your thumbs.

Turn your elbows around the bar so that it lands on your shoulders. Loosen your grip as the elbows come to the front. Push your shoulders forward so they form a shelf for the bar, which touches your throat lightly.
Keep the bar close to your body the whole time: with a heavier load, any gap leads to an unwanted collision. Once the movement gets smoother, you can add speed and load before moving on.
Rack_Pull_with_Bands: Lay the bar on the pins of a power rack. Set the pins to the height you want: just below the knees, just above them, or at mid thigh. Fix bands to the base of the rack or hold them down with dumbbells, and fasten the other end to the bar. You may have to choke the bands to get tension.

Step up to the bar in a proper deadlift position: feet under your hips, hands shoulder width apart, back arched and hips pushed back so the hamstrings engage. The weight is usually heavy, so a mixed grip, a hook grip or straps can help you hold it.
Look straight ahead, straighten your hips and knees and pull the weight up and back until you are locked out. Pull your shoulders back as you finish. Set the weight down on the pins again and repeat.
Rack_Pulls: Lay the bar on the pins of a power rack. Set the pins to the height you want: just below the knees, just above them, or at mid thigh. Step up to the bar in a proper deadlift position: feet under your hips, hands shoulder width apart, back arched and hips pushed back so the hamstrings engage. The weight is usually heavy, so a mixed grip, a hook grip or straps can help you hold it.
Look straight ahead, straighten your hips and knees and pull the weight up and back until you are locked out. Pull your shoulders back as you finish.
Set the weight down on the pins again and repeat.
Rear_Leg_Raises: Get down on your hands and knees on an exercise mat. Look forward, and bend your knees so that hamstrings and calves form a 90-degree angle. This is your starting position.
Stretch one leg up and back, straightening both knee and hip. Do 5-10 repetitions, then change sides.
Recumbent_Bike: Sit down on the bike and set the seat to suit your height.

Choose what you want from the menu. You may need to start pedaling to switch it on. Use the manual setting or pick a program. Usually you can enter your age and weight so the calories burned during exercise can be estimated. You can change the resistance level at any time during the workout. The handles can track your heart rate, which helps you stay at a suitable intensity.

Recumbent bikes are convenient, good for the cardiovascular system and lower in impact than other activities. Cycling at a moderate pace for 30 minutes burns about 230 calories for a 150 lb person, compared with 450 calories or more for running.
Return_Push_from_Stance: Take an athletic stance, 2 or 3 point, to begin.
On the signal, get into position to receive your partner's pass.
Use both hands to catch the medicine ball, then throw it back to your partner immediately.
Run different routes to vary the drill.
Reverse_Band_Bench_Press: Put a bench inside a power rack and set the bar to the right height. Anchor bands to band pegs or to the top of the rack, and make sure you will be lying correctly under them. Fasten the other end to the barbell.

Lie down on the bench, pull your feet in under you and arch your back. Let the bar carry part of your weight, lift your shoulders off the bench and pull them back, pressing the shoulder blades together. Push with your feet to drive your traps into the bench. Stay this tight for the whole movement. Whatever grip width you choose, your hands should cover the ring on the bar.

Take the bar out of the rack without letting your shoulders come forward. Squeeze the bar and try to pull it apart. Bring it down to your lower chest or upper stomach. Bar, wrist and elbow stay in one line throughout.
Pause once the barbell touches your torso, then press it up as forcefully as you can. Keep your elbows tucked in until lockout.
Reverse_Band_Box_Squat: Stand in a power rack with a box of suitable height behind you. Hang the bands from band pegs or from the top of the rack so that they will be straight above the bar during the squat. Fasten the other end to the bar.

Step under the bar and lay it across the back of your shoulders. Press your shoulder blades together and turn your elbows forward as if to bend the bar over your shoulders. Lift the bar out of the rack with a tight arch in your lower back and step back into position. A wider stance puts more emphasis on the back, glutes, adductors and hamstrings; a narrower one develops the quads more. Keep facing forward.

Keep your back, shoulders and core tight and push your knees and butt out as you start down. Sit back with your hips until you are sitting on the box. Ideally your shins are perpendicular to the ground. Pause on the box and relax the hip flexors. Never bounce off a box.

With the weight on your heels and your feet and knees pushed out, drive up off the box, leading with your head. Keep rising and stay tight from head to toe. Put the barbell back in the rack with care.
Reverse_Band_Deadlift: Place the bar in a power rack. Fix bands to the top of the rack, on band pegs or on the frame itself, and fasten their other end to the bar.

Step up so that the bar is centered over your feet, which are about hip width apart. Bend at the hips and grip the bar at shoulder width, letting your shoulder blades move forward. Usually you take an overhand grip, or an over/under grip for heavier sets.

Once feet and grip are set, take a deep breath, then drop your hips and bend your knees until your shins touch the bar. Look ahead, keep your chest up and your back arched, and push through your heels to start the weight moving up.
When the bar has passed your knees, pull it back aggressively: draw your shoulder blades together and drive your hips forward into the bar.
Bend at the hips to lower the bar and guide it down to the floor.
Reverse_Band_Power_Squat: Stand in a power rack with pins and bar at a suitable height. Load the bar, then fix bands to the top of the rack, on pegs or on the frame itself, and fasten their other end to the bar.

Step under the bar and lay it across the back of your shoulders. Press your shoulder blades together and turn your elbows forward as if to bend the bar over your shoulders. Lift the bar out of the rack with a tight arch in your lower back and step back into position. Take a wide stance to put more emphasis on the back, glutes, adductors and hamstrings.

Keep facing forward. Keep your back, shoulders and core tight and push your knees and butt out as you start down. Sit back with your hips as far as you can. Ideally your shins are perpendicular to the ground. A lower bar position requires more forward lean of the torso so that the bar stays over the heels. Go down until you break parallel, meaning the crease of the hip is in line with the top of the knee.
With the weight on your heels and your feet and knees pushed out, drive up, leading with your head. Keep rising, tight from head to toe, until you are back in the starting position.
Reverse_Band_Sumo_Deadlift: Inside a power rack, start with a loaded bar lying on the floor. Hang bands from the rack's top, either from pegs or from the frame itself, and fix their free end to the barbell.

Step up so that the bar crosses the middle of your feet. Set your feet very wide, close to the collars. Bend at the hips and grip the bar. Your arms hang straight below your shoulders, inside your legs; a pronated grip, a mixed grip or a hook grip all work. Relax your shoulders, which effectively makes your arms longer.
Breathe in, then drop your hips, eyes forward and chest up. Push through the floor as if spreading your feet apart, with your weight on the rear half of your feet. Straighten your hips and knees.
Once the bar passes the knees, pull your shoulder blades together, lean back and drive your hips into the bar.
Bend at the hips to bring the weight down to the ground, keeping it under control on the way.
Reverse_Barbell_Curl: Stand tall with an upright torso and hold a barbell at shoulder width, elbows close to your body. Your palms face down (pronated grip). This is your starting position.

Keep your upper arms still and, breathing out, curl the weight up by contracting the biceps. Only your forearms move. Go on until the biceps are fully contracted and the bar is level with your shoulders. Stay there for a second and squeeze the muscle.
Breathe in and slowly return the bar to the start.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Reverse_Barbell_Preacher_Curls: With your palms down (a pronated grip) and your hands shoulder width apart, take hold of an EZ-bar.
Lay both upper arms on the pad of the preacher bench with your arms stretched out. This is your starting position.
Breathe out and curl the weight up with your biceps until they are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. At the top, squeeze the biceps firmly for one second.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until your upper arms are stretched out and the biceps is at full stretch.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Reverse_Cable_Curl: Attach a bar to a low pulley. Stand with an upright torso and hold the bar with a pronated (palms-down) grip at shoulder width. Keep your elbows close to your body as well. This is your starting position.

Keep your upper arms still and, breathing out, curl the weight up by contracting the biceps. Only your forearms move. Go on until the biceps are fully contracted and the bar is level with your shoulders. Stay there for a second and squeeze the muscle.
Breathe in and slowly return the bar to the start.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Reverse_Crunch: Lie on the floor with your legs stretched out and your arms beside your torso, palms on the floor. Your arms stay still throughout the exercise.
Your starting position: thighs moved up until they are perpendicular to the floor, feet together and parallel to the floor.
Breathe in and bring your legs toward your torso, rolling your pelvis back and lifting your hips off the floor. At the end, your knees touch your chest.
Hold the tension for a second, then breathe out and return your legs to the start.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Reverse_Flyes: Lie face down on an incline bench with your chest and stomach pressed against the pad. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms turned toward each other (neutral grip).
Stretch your arms out in front of you so they are perpendicular to the angle of the bench. Keep your legs still and press the balls of your feet into the floor. This is the starting position.

Keep the slight bend in your elbows and, breathing out, move the weights out to the sides and away from each other in an arc. Tip: Squeeze your shoulder blades together to get the most out of this exercise.
Raise your arms until they are parallel to the floor.
Feel the contraction, then breathe in and lower the weights slowly to the start.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Reverse_Flyes_With_External_Rotation: Set an incline bench to a 30-degree angle and lie on it face down, chest and stomach pressed against the pad.

Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing the floor. Your arms hang in front of you, perpendicular to the angle of the bench. Tip: Keep a slight bend in your elbows. Keep your legs still and press the balls of your feet into the floor (your heels stay off the floor). This is the starting position.
Keep the slight bend in your elbows and, breathing out, move the weights out and away from each other in an arc.

While lifting, rotate your wrists outward by 90 degrees, so that the palms-down (pronated) grip turns into a neutral grip with the palms facing each other. Tip: Squeeze your shoulder blades together to get the most out of this exercise.
Raise your arms until they are level with your head.
Feel the contraction, then breathe in and lower the weights slowly to the start.
Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
Reverse_Grip_Bent-Over_Rows: Take a barbell with an underhand grip, palms turned up, and stand tall.

With a slight bend in your knees, hinge at the waist and lean your torso forward until it is nearly parallel to the floor; your back stays straight. Tip: Keep your head up. Let the barbell hang right in front of you, arms perpendicular to both the floor and your torso. This is the starting position.

Breathe out and pull the barbell up without moving your torso. Keep your elbows tucked in to your body, and let your forearms do nothing more than hold the weight. At the top, squeeze your back muscles and hold for a second.
Breathe in and bring the weight slowly back down to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Reverse_Grip_Triceps_Pushdown: Attach a bar, straight or E-Z, to a high pulley.

Stand facing the bar and take it at shoulder width with an underhand grip, palms up. Use your lats to bring the bar down until your arms are fully straight at your sides. Tip: Tuck your elbows in at your sides and set your feet shoulder width apart. This is the starting position.
Breathe in and let the bar rise slowly until it is level with your chest. Move only your forearms; your elbows and upper arms stay fixed at your sides the whole time.
Then breathe out and press the bar back down to the starting position, contracting your triceps hard.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Reverse_Hyperextension: Load a suitable weight, then put your feet between the pads. Lie on the top pad with your hips hanging off the back edge, and hold the handles to keep yourself in place.
Start the movement by flexing your hips so that your legs are drawn forward.
Then extend your hips and kick your legs back. It is very important that you do not over-extend the hips here: stop before the end of your full range of motion.
Flex your hips again to return, drawing the carriage as far forward as you can.
Do it again until you reach the number of repetitions you want.
Reverse_Machine_Flyes: Set the handles all the way to the rear. Choose a suitable weight and set the seat height so that the handles are level with your shoulders. Hold the handles with your palms facing inwards. This is the starting position.
Pull your hands out to the sides and back in a half circle, contracting your rear delts.
Keep a slight bend in your arms from start to finish; all of the motion comes from the shoulder joint.
At the rear of the movement, pause. Then let the weight go slowly back to where it started.
Reverse_Plate_Curls: Stand upright and hold a weight plate in both hands with your arms fully straight. Grip it overhand, palms down, with your fingers on the rough side of the plate and your thumbs on the smooth side. Note: For the best results, hold the plate at the 11:00 and 1:00 o'clock positions.
Set your feet shoulder width apart and hold the plate close to your groin. This is the starting position.
Breathe out and slowly raise the plate until your biceps and forearms touch; keep your elbows in and your upper arms still. At this point the plate should be evenly in line with your torso.
Feel the contraction for a second, then breathe in and lower the weight back to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Reverse_Triceps_Bench_Press: Lie on your back on a flat bench. Take the bar from the rack with a close underhand grip, about shoulder width, and hold it straight above you, arms locked out and perpendicular to the floor. This is the starting position.

Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until you feel it on the middle of your chest. Tip: Unlike in a regular bench press, keep your elbows close to your torso the whole time, so that the triceps do as much of the work as possible.

Pause for a second, then breathe out and press the bar back to the starting position with your triceps. Lock your arms at the top, hold for a second, then begin to lower slowly again. Tip: The way down should take at least twice as long as the way up.
Do the prescribed number of repetitions.
Rack the bar again once you have finished.
Rhomboids-SMR: Lie on the floor on your back. Put a foam roll under your upper back and cross your arms in front of you so that your shoulders are drawn forward. This is the starting position.
Lift your hips off the floor so that your weight rests on the foam roll. Lean to one side at a time and roll over your middle and upper back. Where you find tension, stay for 10-30 seconds.
Rickshaw_Carry: Set the frame at the starting point and load it with a suitable weight. Stand in the middle of the frame, grip the handles and push through your heels to lift it. Keep your chest and head up and your back straight.
Start walking briskly right away, with quick, controlled steps. Chest up, head facing forward, and do not stop breathing. Once you reach the end point, set the frame down on the ground.
Rickshaw_Deadlift: Load the frame with the weight you want. Stand centred between the handles with your feet about hip width apart. Hinge at the hips to grip the handles and let your shoulder blades spread forward.

Once your feet and grip are set, take a big breath, then lower your hips and bend your knees. Look ahead, keep your chest up and your back arched, and push through your heels to move the weight up. As it rises, draw your shoulder blades together and drive your hips forward.
Bend at the hips to bring the weight down, guiding it to the ground.
Ring_Dips: With a ring gripped in each hand, make a small jump; it helps you reach the starting position, arms locked out.
Bend your elbows and lower your body until your arms pass 90 degrees. Do not swing, and keep good posture all the way down.
Then straighten your elbows and push yourself back up to the starting position.
Keep going for as many repetitions as you want to do.
Rocket_Jump: Hold your arms close to your body and take a relaxed, shoulder-width stance to begin.
To start, drop into a half squat and explode upward as high as you can.
Stretch your whole body out and reach overhead as far as you can. When you land, let your legs absorb the impact.
Rocking_Standing_Calf_Raise: For safety, this exercise is best done inside a squat rack. First set the bar in the rack at the height that suits you best. With the height set and the bar loaded, step under it and rest it across the back of your shoulders, slightly below your neck.
Hold the bar with both hands, one on each side, and lift it off the rack by pushing with your legs while you straighten your torso.

Step back from the rack and take a medium stance, feet shoulder width apart and toes pointing slightly out. Keep your head up the whole time; looking down throws you off balance. Keep your back straight too, and your knees slightly bent, never locked. This is the starting position.

Breathe out and raise your heels by extending your ankles as high as you can and flexing your calves. Your knees must stay still throughout: apart from the slight bend you set when you took your stance, they do not bend at any time. Hold the contraction for a second before you go back down.
Breathe in and return slowly to the starting position: lower your heels, bending the ankles, until your calves are stretched.
Now breathe out and lift your toes by contracting the shin muscles at the front of your lower legs.
Hold for a second, then breathe in and lower them again.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Rocky_Pull-Ups_Pulldowns: Take a wide grip on the pull-up bar with your palms facing forward.
Hanging from the bar with both arms straight at your chosen grip width, lean your torso back about 30 degrees, arch your lower back and push your chest out. This is the starting position.

Pull yourself up until the bar touches your upper chest by drawing your shoulders and upper arms down and back. Breathe out during this part. Tip: At full contraction, concentrate on squeezing your back muscles. Your upper torso should stay rigid as it travels, and only your arms should move. Your forearms should hold the bar and do nothing else.
Hold the contraction for a second, then breathe in and lower yourself slowly to the starting position, with your arms fully straight and your lats fully stretched.

Now do the same movement again, but this time keep your torso straight on the way up and let the bar touch the back of your neck rather than your upper chest. Tip: Tilt your head slightly forward; it helps you do this part of the exercise properly.
When you are back down in the starting position, repeat the exercise for the number of repetitions your program prescribes.
Romanian_Deadlift: Place a barbell on the ground in front of you and take it with an overhand grip, palms down, a little wider than shoulder width. Tip: Depending on the weight, you may need wrist wraps, and a raised platform too, for a better range of motion.
Bend your knees a little, with your shins vertical, your hips back and your back straight. This is the starting position.
Breathe out and lift the bar with your hips, keeping your back and arms completely straight the whole time. Tip: Move steadily and under control, not fast.

When you are standing fully upright, lower the bar by pushing your hips back; unlike in a squat, your knees bend only slightly. Tip: Take a deep breath at the start of the movement and keep your chest up. Hold your breath on the way down and exhale as you finish the movement.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Romanian_Deadlift_from_Deficit: Stand holding a bar in front of you with your arms straight. If you stand on a raised platform, the range of motion gets longer.

Bend your knees slightly, then hinge at the hips: push your butt back as far as you can and lower your torso as far as your flexibility allows. Your back must stay fully extended the whole time, and the bar stays in contact with your legs. Done properly, you feel heavy tension in your hamstrings.
Go back the same way until you are where you started again.
Rope_Climb: Take hold of the rope above your head with both hands. Pull down on it and take a small jump.
Wrap the rope around one leg and pinch it between your feet. Reach as high as you can with your arms and grip the rope tightly.
Let your feet release the rope and pull yourself up with your arms, drawing your knees towards your chest.
Clamp the rope with your feet again, then stand up and take another high hold. Carry on until you reach the top of the rope.
To come down, loosen your feet's hold on the rope and slide down, moving hand over hand.
Rope_Crunch: With a rope attached to a cable system, kneel 1-2 feet in front of it.
Choose a suitable weight, reach overhead and take the rope in both hands. In the starting position your torso is upright.
To start, curl your spine and pull the cable down, trying to bring your rib cage towards your legs.
Pause at the bottom, then return slowly to the starting position.
You can also do these with a twist or to the side to work the obliques.
Rope_Jumping: Hold one end of the rope in each hand, with the rope on the ground behind you. Lift your arms and swing the rope over your head and down in front of you. Jump over it when it reaches the ground. Find a turning pace you can keep up. For variation, use different speeds and techniques.
Jumping rope is exciting, challenges your coordination and takes a lot of energy. In 30 minutes of jumping rope a 150 lb person burns about 350 calories, compared to over 450 calories for running.
Rope_Straight-Arm_Pulldown: Fix a rope to a high pulley and choose your weight. Stand a couple of feet back from the pulley with your feet staggered and hold the rope in both hands. Lean forward from the hips with a straight back and your arms stretched up in front of you. This is the starting position.
With straight arms, extend your shoulders and pull the rope down to your thighs.
Squeeze your lats while you pause at the bottom of the movement.
Go back to the starting position, but do not let the weight come to rest fully on the stack.
Round_The_World_Shoulder_Stretch: Holding a broomstick or bodybar, stand straight with your legs together.
Hold the pole behind your hips, hands wider than shoulder width, palms facing down and thumbs pointing out.
Slowly raise your arms up behind your head. If it gets hard to go further, do not force it.
Rowing_Stationary: Sit down on the rower. Check that your heels rest comfortably against the base of the foot pedals and that the straps are fastened. If the machine offers programs, choose the one you want. Sit up straight and lean forward from the hips.

Rowing has three phases of movement. In the first you come forward on the rower: your knees are bent and against your chest, and your upper body leans slightly forward in good posture. Next, push against the foot pedals and straighten your legs while you pull your hands to your upper abdomen and squeeze your shoulders back. Work mainly with your leg and hip muscles, so that you do not strain your back.
To recover, you only need to straighten the arms, let the knees bend and move your body forward once more; that takes you back into the first phase.
Runners_Stretch: The easiest way into this stretch is from standing: step one leg back and slowly lower your torso towards the floor.
The front heel must stay on the floor. Should it lift up, scoot the other leg further back.

Put your hands down on either side of your front leg. For a deeper stretch, push your butt up towards the ceiling and then lower it gradually back towards the floor. This stretches the hip flexor of the back leg and the hamstring and buttocks of the front leg.
Running_Treadmill: Step onto the treadmill and choose the option you want from the menu. Most treadmills have a manual setting, or you can pick a program to run. You can usually enter your age and weight for an estimate of the calories you burn while exercising. Change the elevation to change how intense the workout is.

Treadmills are convenient, good for your cardiovascular system and usually lower in impact than running outside. Running at 8 miles per hour for 30 minutes, a 150 lb person burns over 450 calories. Run with proper posture and hold the handles only when you need to, for example when getting off or checking your heart rate.
Russian_Twist: Lie on the floor with your knees bent. Hook your feet under something that will not move, or have a partner hold them.
Lift your upper body until it and your thighs make an imaginary V-shape. Clasp your hands and extend your arms fully in front of you, perpendicular to the torso. You are now in the starting position.
Breathe out and rotate your torso to the right until your arms are parallel to the floor.
After holding the contraction for a second, breathe out as you return to the starting position. Then go to the opposite side with the same techniques you used on the right side.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Sandbag_Load: For loading sandbags or other objects, the implements start a distance from the loading platform; 50 feet is typical.

Start by lifting the sandbag. Sandbags are extremely awkward, and how you lift one depends on the particular bag. Get your arms as far around it as you can and extend your hips and knees to pull it up high. Putting it on your shoulder is usually not allowed.
Get to the platform as fast as you can and load the bag: extend your hips, knees and ankles to raise it as high as possible. Set it on the platform and make sure it does not fall off.
Go back to the start for the next sandbag and repeat until the event is finished.
Scapular_Pull-Up: Hang from the bar and lift yourself a few inches without using your arms. To do this, pull your shoulder girdle down, like a shrug in reverse.
When the movement is complete, pause. Go slowly back to where you started before you do more repetitions.
Scissor_Kick: Lie down with your back pressed to the floor; an exercise mat is optional. Stretch your arms fully out to the sides, palms down. Note: Your arms do not move at any time.
Bend your knees slightly and lift your legs so that the heels are about 6 inches off the ground. You are now in the starting position.
Now raise your left leg to an angle of about 45 degrees while you lower your right leg until its heel is about 2-3 inches from the ground.
Switch: raise your right leg and lower your left. Remember to keep breathing during this exercise.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Scissors_Jump: Get into a lunge stance: one foot forward with its knee bent, the back knee almost touching the ground.
Check that your front knee is over the midline of the foot. Push off through both legs and jump as high as you can, swinging your arms for extra lift.
At the height of the jump, swap your legs: the front leg goes to the back and the back leg to the front.
When you land, sink into the lunge position so that your legs absorb the impact, then repeat.
Seated_Band_Hamstring_Curl: A couple of feet away from a band that you have secured near the ground, set up a bench.
Sit on the bench and loop the band behind your ankles, starting with straight legs. This is the starting position.
Bend your knees and draw your feet towards the bench. You may have to lean back a little so that your feet do not hit the floor.
When the movement is complete, pause; go slowly back to where you started.
Seated_Barbell_Military_Press: Sit on a military press bench with a bar behind your head. Either have a spotter hand you the bar, which is easier on the rotator cuff, or pick it up carefully yourself with an overhand grip, palms facing forward. Tip: Grip wider than shoulder width, so that your forearm and upper arm form a 90-degree angle as the barbell comes down.
Pick up the barbell with the correct grip length, then lock your arms to lift the bar over your head. Hold it slightly in front of your head at about shoulder level. That is the starting position.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly to your collarbone.
Breathe out and press the bar back up to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Seated_Barbell_Twist: Sit at the end of a flat bench with a barbell lying across your thighs. Set your feet shoulder width apart.
Take the bar with your palms facing down and your hands wider than shoulder width. Raise the barbell over your head until your arms are fully straight.
Next, let the barbell come down behind your head so that it rests along the base of your neck. You are now in the starting position.

Keep your feet and head still and turn your waist from side to side so that you feel your obliques contract. Go only as far to each side as your waist lets you; stretching or moving too far can cause an injury. Tip: Move slowly and with control.
Remember to breathe out as you twist to the side and to breathe in as you come back to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Seated_Bent-Over_One-Arm_Dumbbell_Tricep: With a dumbbell in one arm, held in a neutral grip (the palm of the hand faces you), take a seat at the end of a flat bench.
With a slight bend in your knees, hinge at the waist and lean your torso forward with a straight back until it is nearly parallel to the floor. Keep your head up.

Hold the upper arm with the dumbbell close to your torso and in line with it: raised until it is parallel to the floor, with the forearm pointing down to the floor and the hand holding the weight. Tip: Your forearm and upper arm should form a 90-degree angle. This is the starting position.

Breathe out and, without moving the upper arm, lift the weight with your triceps until your forearm is parallel to the floor and the whole arm is straight. As in many other arm exercises, only the forearm moves.
Hold the contraction at the top for a second, then breathe in and slowly lower the dumbbell to the starting position.
Do the prescribed number of repetitions.
Change arms and do the exercise again.
Seated_Bent-Over_Rear_Delt_Raise: In front of a flat bench, put down a couple of dumbbells so they look forward.
With the dumbbells behind your calves, take a seat on the bench's end and keep your legs together.
Hinge at the waist with a straight back to pick up the dumbbells. Your palms face each other as you take them. This is the starting position.

With your torso leaning forward and still, and your elbows slightly bent, raise the dumbbells straight out to the sides until both arms are parallel to the floor. Breathe out as you lift. Note: Do not swing your torso, and do not move your arms backwards instead of out to the sides.
Hold the contraction at the top for one second, then slowly lower the dumbbells to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Seated_Bent-Over_Two-Arm_Dumbbell_Tricep: With a dumbbell in both arms, held in a neutral grip (the palms of the hands face you), take a seat at the end of a flat bench.
Bend your knees a little and lean your torso forward from the waist, back straight, until it is almost parallel to the floor. Keep your head up.

Hold your upper arms close to your torso and in line with it: raised until they are parallel to the floor, with the forearms pointing down to the floor and the hands holding the weights. Tip: Your forearms and upper arms should form a 90-degree angle. This is the starting position.

Breathe out and, with your upper arms still, lift the weights with your triceps until your forearms are parallel to the floor and your arms are fully straight. As in many other arm exercises, only the forearms move.
Hold the contraction at the top for a second, then breathe in and slowly lower the dumbbells to the starting position.
Do the prescribed number of repetitions.
Seated_Biceps: Sit on the floor with bent knees; your partner stands behind you. Stretch your arms straight out behind you, palms facing each other, and let your partner hold your wrists. This is the starting position.
Your partner prevents any actual movement while you attempt to flex your elbows.

Once 10-20 seconds have passed, let your arms relax; your partner stretches your biceps by pulling your wrists up gently. To prevent injury or overstretching, make certain your partner knows when the stretch is appropriate.
Seated_Cable_Rows: You need a low pulley row machine with a V-bar for this exercise. Note: With the V-bar you hold a neutral grip, your palms facing each other. To get into position, sit down on the machine and put your feet on the front platform or crossbar, with your knees slightly bent and not locked.
Grab the V-bar handles by leaning over, with the natural alignment of your back kept.

With straight arms, pull back until your torso is at a 90-degree angle to your legs. Arch your back slightly and push your chest out. Holding the bar in front of you, you should feel a good stretch in your lats. This is the starting position of the exercise.

Without moving your torso, pull the handles towards it until they touch your abdominals; your arms stay close to your body. Breathe out as you pull. Squeeze your back muscles hard at this point. Hold the contraction for a second, then breathe in and go slowly back to where you started.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Seated_Cable_Shoulder_Press: Set a suitable weight, sit down and take the handles. Hold your upper arms at about 90 degrees to your body, head and chest up, and your elbows bent to about 90 degrees as well. This is the starting position.
Start by straightening your elbows and pressing the handles together above your head.
Pause at the top, then bring the handles back to the starting position. Make sure the cables stay under tension.
Another way to execute this movement: alternate hands and keep your back off the pad.
Seated_Calf_Raise: Sit on the machine and put your toes on the lower part of the platform so that your heels hang off it. Point your toes whichever way you prefer: forward, in or out.
Slide your lower thighs under the lever pad; it has to be adjusted to the height of your thighs. Then put your hands on top of the lever pad so that it cannot slip forward.
Push your heels up to lift the lever slightly and release the safety bar. This is the starting position.
Breathe in and slowly lower your heels by bending your ankles until your calves are fully stretched.
Breathe out and raise your heels as high as you can by extending your ankles and contracting your calves. Hold the contraction at the top for a second.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Seated_Calf_Stretch: Take a seat on an exercise mat with your back upright.
Keep your torso steady by bending one knee and setting that foot down on the floor.
Extend the other leg and flex the ankle.
Draw your toes toward you with a band, a towel, or your hand if it reaches that far. Stay there for 10 to 20 seconds, then change sides.
Seated_Close-Grip_Concentration_Barbell_: Take a seat on a flat bench with a barbell or E-Z bar lying in front of you, between your legs. Keep your legs apart, knees bent and feet on the floor.

Lift the bar with your arms and rest the backs of your upper arms on your inner thighs, roughly three and a half inches behind the front of the knee. This exercise calls for an underhand (supinated) grip with the hands closer together than shoulder width. Tip: Your arms should be stretched to full length with the bar off the floor. This is your starting position.

Breathe out and curl the weight forward by tightening your biceps, keeping your upper arms still. Nothing but the forearms should move. Keep going until the biceps are fully contracted and the weight has reached shoulder level. Squeeze the biceps and hold at the top for a second.
Breathe in while you slowly lower the bar to the starting position. Tip: Do not swing at any point.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Seated_Dumbbell_Curl: Take a seat on a flat bench, a dumbbell in each hand and your arms hanging at full length. Keep your elbows near your torso.
Turn your palms so they face your torso. This is your starting position.

Keep your upper arms still and curl the weights; as soon as the dumbbells have passed your thighs, begin twisting your wrists so your palms face forward when the movement ends. Breathe out and tighten the biceps as you lift, and let nothing but the forearms move. Keep going until the biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells have reached shoulder level. Squeeze the biceps and hold at the top for a second.
Breathe in and slowly lower the dumbbells to the starting position, turning your wrists back to a neutral grip on the way.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Seated_Dumbbell_Inner_Biceps_Curl: Sit at the end of a flat bench, a dumbbell in each hand and your arms hanging at full length. Keep your elbows near your torso.
Turn your palms inward to a neutral position. This is your starting position.
Keep your upper arms still and curl the dumbbells outward and up. Turn your palms out as you lift, and keep your forearms lined up with your outer deltoids.
Tip: Nothing but the forearms should move. Keep going until the biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells have reached shoulder level. Squeeze the biceps and hold at the top for a second.
Breathe in and slowly lower the dumbbells to the starting position. Do not forget to rotate your arms on the way down, so you end in a neutral grip again.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Seated_Dumbbell_Palms-Down_Wrist_Curl: In front of a flat bench, put two dumbbells down on the floor to begin with.
Take a seat on the edge of the bench with your legs roughly shoulder width apart. Your feet stay on the floor.
Pick up both dumbbells and lift them until your forearms lie on your thighs, palms facing down. Let your wrists hang past the edge of your thighs.
Begin by curling your wrists up while you breathe out.

Breathe in while you slowly bring your wrists down to the starting position. Be sure to inhale in this part of the movement. Tip: Keep your forearms still; the wrists are the only thing that has to move in this exercise.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Once you are done, just set the dumbbells down on the floor.
Seated_Dumbbell_Palms-Up_Wrist_Curl: To begin with, two dumbbells go on the floor, right before a flat bench.
Take a seat on the edge of the bench with your legs roughly shoulder width apart. Your feet stay on the floor.
Pick up both dumbbells and lift them until your forearms lie on your thighs, palms facing up. Let your wrists hang past the edge of your thighs.
Begin by curling your wrists up while you breathe out.

Breathe in while you slowly bring your wrists down to the starting position. Be sure to inhale in this part of the movement. Tip: Keep your forearms still; the wrists are the only thing that has to move in this exercise.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Once you are done, just set the dumbbells down on the floor.
Seated_Dumbbell_Press: Pick up a couple of dumbbells. Sit down on a utility bench with back support or on a military press bench, and stand the dumbbells upright on top of your thighs.
Bring the dumbbells up one after the other, kicking each with your thigh until it is at shoulder height at your side.
Turn your wrists so your palms face forward. This is your starting position.
Breathe out and press the dumbbells up until they meet at the top.
Pause for a second, then breathe in and slowly lower to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Seated_Flat_Bench_Leg_Pull-In: Sit on a bench and grip its sides with your hands. Stretch your legs out in front of you, a little below parallel, and lean your torso back at roughly 45 degrees to the bench. This is your starting position.
Draw your knees toward you and bring your torso toward them at the same time. Breathe out during this movement.
Pause for a second, then breathe in and return to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Seated_Floor_Hamstring_Stretch: Sit on a mat with your right leg stretched out in front of you. Bend your left leg and rest that foot against the inside of your right thigh.
From the hips, lean forward and reach for the ankle until a stretch is felt in the hamstring. Stay for 15 seconds, then do the same on the other side.
Seated_Front_Deltoid: Sit upright on the floor with bent legs while your partner stands behind you. Hold your arms straight out to the sides, palms toward the ground. Try to bring them as far back behind you as you can while your partner holds your wrists. This is your starting position.
With straight elbows, try to bring your arms forward for 10-20 seconds while your partner gently holds you back so that nothing actually moves.
Next, let your muscles relax so that your partner can gently increase the stretch on chest and shoulders. Stay there for 10 to 20 seconds.
Seated_Glute: Sit with your knees bent and lay one ankle across the opposite knee. Your partner stands behind you. Lean forward while your partner braces your shoulders with their hands. This is your starting position.
For 10-20 seconds, try to press your torso backward while your partner keeps it from actually moving.
Then relax your muscles while your partner gently pushes your torso forward for 10-20 seconds to deepen the stretch.
Seated_Good_Mornings: Place a box inside a power rack and set the pins to a suitable height. Step under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders, not on top of your traps. Pull your shoulder blades together and turn your elbows forward, as if you were trying to bend the bar around your shoulders.

Lift the bar out of the rack with a tight arch in your lower back. Keep looking straight ahead. With your back, shoulders and core tight, push your knees and butt out as you start to descend. Sit back with your hips until you are sitting on the box. This is your starting position.
Keep the bar tight and bend forward from the hips as far as you can. With the pins set where parallel would be, you have a safety in case you fail and you also know where to stop.
Just above the pins, pause. Then go back the other way until your torso is upright.
Seated_Hamstring: Sit with your legs extended and your partner standing behind you. Lean forward now, with your partner's hands bracing your shoulders. That is the starting position.
For 10-20 seconds, try to press your torso backward while your partner keeps it from actually moving.
Then relax your muscles while your partner gently pushes your torso forward for 10-20 seconds to deepen the stretch.
Seated_Hamstring_and_Calf_Stretch: Around one foot, loop a band, rope or belt. Your starting position is seated, with both legs extended.
Lean forward a little and pull on the belt so the toes of that foot come back toward you. Stay there for 10-20 seconds, then do the same with the other leg.
Seated_Head_Harness_Neck_Resistance: Lay a neck strap on the floor at the end of a flat bench. After choosing the weights, sit at the end of the bench with your feet set wider than shoulder width and your toes pointing outward.

Slowly lean your torso forward until it is nearly parallel to the floor. Fit the neck strap securely around your head with both hands. Tip: Leave the weights lying on the floor while you do this, so your neck is not strained. Then take hold of the weight with both hands and raise your torso until it is nearly perpendicular to the floor. Note: For this exercise your head and torso have to lean slightly forward.
Next, rest your two hands on the tops of the knees. You are then in the starting position.
Breathe in and slowly lower your head until your chin touches your upper chest.
Breathe out and raise your neck back to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Seated_Leg_Curl: Set the lever of the machine so that it fits your height. Then take your seat, leaning your back against the back support pad.

Rest the backs of your lower legs on the padded lever, just a few inches below the calves, and fix the lap pad against your thighs just above the knees. Take hold of the side handles, point your toes straight (either of the other two foot positions works too) and make sure your legs are completely straight in front of you. This is your starting position.
Breathe out and bend your knees to pull the lever as far as you can toward the backs of your thighs. Your torso stays still the whole time. Hold the contraction for a second.
Breathe in and slowly return to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Seated_Leg_Tucks: Sit on a bench, holding on to its sides. Extend your legs in front of you, a little below parallel, and lean your torso back at roughly 45 degrees to the bench. This is your starting position.
Pull your knees in while moving your torso toward them at the same time. Breathe out as you do so.
Pause for a second, then breathe in and go back to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Seated_One-Arm_Dumbbell_Palms-Down_Wrist: With a dumbbell in your right hand, take a seat on a flat bench.
Set your feet flat on the floor, a little wider apart than shoulder width.
Lean forward and lay your right forearm on your upper right thigh, palm facing down. Tip: The back of your wrist should rest on your knee. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and let the dumbbell sink as low as it will go, gripping it tightly.
Then breathe out and curl the dumbbell as high as you can by tightening your forearm. Hold the contraction for a second before lowering again. Tip: All of the movement should come from the wrist.
Do the recommended number of repetitions, then change arms and repeat.
Seated_One-Arm_Dumbbell_Palms-Up_Wrist_C: Hold a dumbbell in your right hand and sit down on a flat bench.
Set your feet flat on the floor, a little wider apart than shoulder width.
Lean forward and lay your right forearm on your upper right thigh, palm facing up. Tip: The front of your wrist should rest on your knee. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and let the dumbbell sink as low as it will go, gripping it tightly.
Then breathe out and curl the dumbbell as high as you can by tightening your forearm. Hold the contraction for a second before lowering again. Tip: All of the movement should come from the wrist.
Do the recommended number of repetitions, then change arms and repeat.
Seated_One-arm_Cable_Pulley_Rows: To set up, sit down at the machine and put your feet on the front platform or crossbar, with your knees slightly bent rather than locked.
Lean forward with your back in its natural alignment and take the single handle in your left hand, palm facing down.

With your arm straight, pull back until your torso is at 90 degrees to your legs. Arch your back slightly and push your chest out. You should feel a good stretch in your lat while holding the handle in front of you. Your right arm can stay at your waist. This is the starting position.

Keep your torso still and pull the handle back toward it with your arm close to your body. Turn your wrist as you pull, so your hand is in a neutral position (palm facing the torso) when it reaches your abdominals. Breathe out during this movement. At this point, squeeze your back muscles hard.
Hold the squeeze for a second, then breathe in and slowly return to the original position. Tip: Turn your wrist on the way back as well, so your palm faces down again at the start.
Do the recommended number of repetitions, then do the same movement with your right hand.
Seated_Overhead_Stretch: On an exercise mat, sit upright and straight.
With your feet six to eight inches in front of your hips, let their soles touch each other.
Put one hand on the floor next to you and the other behind your head.
Raise your elbow toward the ceiling while leaning your torso to the opposite side. Stay there for 10 to 20 seconds, then change sides.
Seated_Palm-Up_Barbell_Wrist_Curl: Take a barbell in both hands with your palms facing up and your hands roughly shoulder width apart.
Set your feet flat on the floor, a little wider apart than shoulder width.
Lean forward and lay your forearms on your upper thighs, palms up. Tip: The fronts of your wrists should rest on your knees. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and let the bar sink as low as it will go, gripping it tightly.
Then breathe out and curl the bar as high as you can by flexing your forearms. Hold the contraction at the top for a second. Tip: Nothing but the wrists should move.
Seated_Palms-Down_Barbell_Wrist_Curl: Take a barbell in both hands with your palms facing down and your hands roughly shoulder width apart.
Set your feet flat on the floor, a little wider apart than shoulder width.
Lean forward and lay your forearms on your upper thighs, palms down. Tip: The backs of your wrists should rest on your knees. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and let the bar sink as low as it will go, gripping it tightly.
Then breathe out and curl the bar as high as you can by flexing your forearms. Hold the contraction at the top for a second. Tip: Nothing but the wrists should move.
Seated_Side_Lateral_Raise: Take a pair of dumbbells and sit at the end of a flat bench, feet planted firmly on the floor. Let your arms hang straight at your sides at full length, palms facing in. This is your starting position.

Keep your torso still, without swinging, and raise the dumbbells out to the sides. Bend your elbows slightly and tip your hands a little forward, like pouring water into a glass. Lift until your arms are parallel to the floor. Breathe out during the lift and pause at the top for a second.
Breathe in and slowly bring the dumbbells down to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Seated_Triceps_Press: Sit on a bench with back support, take one dumbbell in both hands and hold it overhead with your arms at full length. Tip: It is better to have someone pass it to you, above all when it is very heavy. The weight should rest in your palms with your thumbs wrapped around it, and your palms should face inward. This is your starting position.

Keep your upper arms near your head, elbows in, and perpendicular to the floor. Lower the weight behind your head in a half-circle until your forearms touch your biceps. Tip: Keep the upper arms still and move only the forearms. Breathe in during this step.
Use your triceps to lift the dumbbell back to the starting position. Breathe out during this step.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Seated_Two-Arm_Palms-Up_Low-Pulley_Wrist: Set a bench in front of a low pulley fitted with a straight bar or EZ curl attachment.
Move the bench far enough back that the weight stack lifts and the cable is under tension once the handle is on top of your thighs.
Then grip the handle with both hands at shoulder width, palms facing up.
Step back and sit on the bench, feet planted firmly on the floor roughly shoulder width apart.
Leaning forward, rest your forearms on the thighs so that the back of each wrist is over a knee. That is the starting position.
Breathe in and let the bar sink as low as it will go, gripping it tightly.
Then curl the bar as high as you can by tightening your forearms. Tip: The movement comes from the wrists alone, not from the forearms.
Hold the contraction at the top for a second, then breathe in and return to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
See-Saw_Press_Alternating_Side_Press: With a dumbbell grabbed in each hand, stand erect.
Lift (clean) the dumbbells to chest/shoulder level. Then rotate the wrists until the palms face you, like getting ready for an Arnold Press. That is the starting position.

Press your left arm overhead, turning the wrist on the way up so the palm ends facing forward. Let your elbows travel outward as the weight rises. At the same time, bend at the hip toward the opposite side. Tip: Done correctly, it looks as though you were reaching with your left arm for something above the right side of your body. Breathe out during this movement.
Breathe in when you reach the top. Then, with the weight at full stretch overhead and your body bent to the right, start the movement toward the left side.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Shotgun_Row: On a low cable, fasten a single handle.
Choose a suitable weight, then stand a couple of feet back in a wide split stance. Keep your arm straight and let your shoulder come forward. This is your starting position.
Pull by drawing your shoulder back and bending your elbow. Supinate your wrist as you pull, so the palm turns upward along the way.
Pause briefly, then go back to the starting position.
Shoulder_Circles: Relax your shoulders and let your arms hang loosely at your sides, or rest them in your lap when seated. Gently roll your shoulders forward, up, back and down.
Then roll them the other way. You can circle one shoulder at a time in alternation, or both together.
