Shoulder_Press_-_With_Bands: Start by standing on an exercise band so that it becomes taut with your arms at full length. Take the handles and raise them until your hands are at shoulder height on either side.
Turn your wrists so your palms face forward. Bend your elbows and keep upper arms and forearms in line with your torso. This is your starting position.
Breathe out and press the handles up until your arms are fully straight overhead.
Shoulder_Raise: Let your arms hang relaxed at your sides, lift your shoulders toward your ears and lower them again.
Shoulder_Stretch: With your left arm held straight, reach it across your body.
Side-Lying_Floor_Stretch: Start on your left side, with the left knee bent in front of you; this stabilizes the torso (your abdominal muscles also help to hold you upright; use them).

Extend your right leg and set the right foot on the floor behind the left one. Reach your right arm straight over your head and pull gently on the right wrist, so the whole right side of your body is stretched. Change sides.
Side_Bridge: Lie on your side with your legs straight and one on top of the other. Prop yourself on your lower forearm with the elbow directly under your shoulder.
Tighten your abdominals and lift your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from head to feet.
Hold this position while breathing steadily. Do not let your hips sag or rotate.
Lower your hips to the floor, then repeat on the other side.
Side_Hop-Sprint: Position yourself beside a cone or hurdle.
Start the drill with a sideways hop over the obstacle, then bounce straight out of the landing and hop back to your starting spot.
Do the prescribed number of hops as fast as you can. End the drill with a short sprint as soon as you land the last hop.
Side_Jackknife: Lie on your side with your legs straight and one on top of the other. Rest your lower arm on the floor in front of you and place your upper hand behind your head.
Breathe out and raise your upper leg toward the ceiling while lifting your torso sideways, bringing your elbow toward the leg.
Hold the contraction in the side of your abdominals for a moment, then breathe in and lower your leg and torso under control.
Do the recommended number of repetitions, then switch to the other side.
Side_Lateral_Raise: Take a pair of dumbbells and stand with your torso straight. Hold the dumbbells at your sides with your arms at full length, palms turned toward you. This is your starting position.

Keep your torso still, with no swinging, and lift the dumbbells out to the sides. Bend your elbows slightly and tip your hands a little forward, like pouring water into a glass. Keep lifting until your arms are parallel to the floor. Breathe out during the lift and pause at the top for a second.
Breathe in and slowly bring the dumbbells down to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Side_Laterals_to_Front_Raise: Your starting position: standing, with a pair of dumbbells held at your side.
With a slight bend in your elbows, lift the weights straight in front of you to shoulder height. Do not swing or cheat.
At the top, move the weights out in front of you with your arms kept straight.
On the following repetition, lift the weights in front of you to shoulder height first, then move them sideways out to your sides.
Let the weights come back down to where you started.
Side_Leg_Raises: Stand beside a chair; you can hold on to it for support. Balance on one leg. This is your starting position.
Lift the other leg, kept straight, out to the side as far as you can, then swing it back down and let it cross the standing leg.
Do this swing 5-10 times, making the range of motion larger as you go.
Side_Lying_Groin_Stretch: Begin lying on your right side. Bend your right knee in front of you to keep your torso steady.
Your head rests on your right shoulder or hand. Bring the left leg upward and hold it by the foot (harder) or by the back of the knee (easier).
Draw your left knee toward your left shoulder while pressing your foot or knee down toward the floor. For a stronger stretch, straighten the left leg. Change sides.
Side_Neck_Stretch: With relaxed shoulders, gently tip your head toward one shoulder.
Support the stretch by pulling gently on the side of your head.
Side_Standing_Long_Jump: Stand in an athletic stance, feet hip width apart. Keep your head and chest up and bend your knees and hips slightly. This is your starting position.
Lean to your right and extend your hips, knees and ankles to leave the ground. Lead the movement by blocking with your arms and jump as far to the right as possible.
Land facing the same way as before, feet hip width apart, and absorb the impact with your lower body.
Side_To_Side_Chins: Take a wide grip on the pull-up bar with your palms facing forward.
Hanging from the wide grip with both arms straight, lean your torso back by roughly 30 degrees, arch your lower back and push your chest out. This is your starting position.

Lean toward your left side and pull your torso up until the bar nearly touches your upper chest, drawing your shoulders and upper arms down and back. Breathe out during this part of the movement. Tip: Focus on squeezing your back muscles once you are fully contracted. Your upper torso should stay rigid as it travels, without swinging, and only your arms should move. Your forearms should do nothing more than hold the bar.
Hold the contraction for a second, then breathe in and return to the starting position.

Now lean toward your right side and pull your torso up until the bar nearly touches your upper chest, drawing your shoulders and upper arms down and back. Breathe out during this part of the movement. Tip: Focus on squeezing your back muscles once you are fully contracted. Your upper torso should stay rigid as it travels, and only your arms should move. Your forearms should do nothing more than hold the bar.
Hold the contraction for a second, then breathe in and return to the starting position.
Go through steps 3-6 again until you have done the prescribed number of repetitions on each side.
Side_Wrist_Pull: Standing is the best position for this stretch. Bring your left arm across the midline of your body and grip the left wrist with your right hand, down at hip level. Begin the stretch with your left arm bent.
Slowly straighten the arm, pull it and raise it to shoulder height. The stretch should start in your back rather than your shoulders; do not pull too hard on the shoulder joint. Change sides.
Side_to_Side_Box_Shuffle: With your left foot resting on the middle of the box, stand to one side of it.
Begin with a jump up and over the box to its other side, so that you land with the left foot on the floor and the right foot on top of the box. Aid the movement by swinging your arms.
Keep shuffling from side to side across the box.
Single-Arm_Cable_Crossover: Set both pulleys high, choose your resistance and grab one handle with each hand.
Take a step forward so you stand in front of the two pulleys, arms straight out ahead and hands together. Lean forward with head and chest lifted and one foot ahead of the other. Start from here.
Hold the left arm still and let the right arm open out to the side with the elbow slightly bent, until it is at about shoulder height and at a right angle to your body.
Pull the hand back to the centre line of your body to bring the arm to the start again.
Pause at the start for one second, then do the same with the other arm. Keep switching sides until you have done the planned number of repetitions.
Single-Arm_Linear_Jammer: Put one end of a bar into a landmine or wedge it firmly into a corner. Add a suitable weight to the bar.
Lift the bar off the floor and bring it up to your shoulders, using one hand or both. Set your feet wide apart. Start from here.
Press the weight up by straightening the elbow. Be explosive and fully straighten hips and knees so you generate as much force as possible.
Single-Arm_Push-Up: Lie face down on the floor. Push up so that your toes and one arm carry your weight. The working arm is completely straight, with the hand right below the shoulder. Keep the legs straight; you may need a broader base here, with your feet wider apart than for a regular push-up.
Hold your body in good alignment and put the free hand behind your back. Start from here.
Bend the elbow and sink down until you reach the floor.
Go down slowly, then straighten the arm to push back up to the start.
Single-Cone_Sprint_Drill: The drill trains fast feet and needs just one cone. Stand beside the cone, one arm forward and the other back.
Take short, choppy steps as fast as you can and pump the arms. Run around the cone with high knees and aggressive footwork.
After three laps of the cone, take a rest.
Single-Leg_High_Box_Squat: Set a box inside a rack and fasten a band or rope above it.
Stand facing the box and step up on it until you are fully upright, with the other leg hanging free. Hold the band to keep your balance.
Keep stepping up and down with the same leg, then change to the other side.
Single-Leg_Hop_Progression: Set up cones in a line ahead of you. Stand relaxed and balanced on one leg, with the other knee lifted. Start from here.
Hop forward over the cone, taking off and landing on the same leg.
Dip before each hop to get from one cone to the next.
Turn around at the end and come back, this time on the other leg.
Single-Leg_Lateral_Hop: Position yourself beside a cone or hurdle. For the start position, balance on one leg with a slight bend in the knee.
Dip quickly and hop sideways across the cone.
Land on the same leg and bounce straight back to where you started.
Keep hopping from side to side.
Single-Leg_Leg_Extension: Sit in the machine and set it up to fit you. The pad rests on the lower shin without touching the ankle. Move the seat until your knee lines up with the machine's pivot point. Pick a weight that suits your level.
Sit tall and straighten one leg all the way, holding briefly at the top.
Lower to the start without letting the weight come to rest, so the muscle stays under tension.
Do as many repetitions as you planned.
Single-Leg_Stride_Jump: Stand beside a box and put the foot nearest to it on top, near the edge.
Swing your arms up and push through the leg on the box to jump as high as you can. Try to drive the other knee up.
Land in the position you started in and absorb the impact with the inside leg.
Single_Dumbbell_Raise: Stand with your feet wide apart and hold one dumbbell in both hands, gripping its head rather than the handle. Let your straight arms hang at waist level. This is your starting position.
With your arms kept straight, lift the weight until it is above shoulder level. Your torso and hips stay still throughout.
Go back to the starting position and do the recommended number of repetitions.
Single_Leg_Butt_Kick: Stand on one leg and lift the other knee, keeping it bent. Start from here.
Dip briefly and jump straight up, driving through the hip, knee and ankle of the leg on the ground.
Bend that knee right away and try to bring the heel of the jumping leg up to your butt.
Bring the leg back under your hips, slightly bent, and land on it. The other leg holds roughly the same position for the whole drill.
Single_Leg_Glute_Bridge: Lie on your back on the floor, knees bent and the soles of your feet on the ground.
Lift one foot off the floor and draw that knee towards your chest. Start from here.
Press through the heel of the standing foot and push your hips up so your glutes leave the floor.
Push the hips as high as you can, hold briefly, then lower back to the start.
Single_Leg_Push-off: Stand on the floor and put one foot on the box, with its heel near the edge.
Drive off the foot on the box and straighten its hip and knee to jump as high as you can.
Come down with that same foot on the box and let the other foot go back to where it started.
Sit-Up: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent. Hook your feet under something that stays put, or ask a partner to hold them.
Put your hands behind your head and interlace the fingers. Start from here.
Raise your upper body until it forms a V with your thighs. Exhale as you come up.
Feel the contraction for a second, then inhale and lower your upper body to the start.
Do as many repetitions as recommended.
Sit_Squats: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Start from here.
Bend at the knees and hips and push your hips back as if to sit.
Go only part of the way down, staying above parallel, then quickly come back up to the start. Do 5-10 repetitions.
Skating: Roller skating is fun and can build cardiorespiratory fitness and muscular endurance. You need fairly good balance and coordination. Learn the basics first, including how to turn and stop, and wear protective gear so you do not get hurt.

Skate for 30 minutes without a break at a pace that feels comfortable. For a harder cardio session, skate in intervals: out of every five minutes, go fast for two and recover for the other three. At a comfortable pace, a person weighing 150 lb burns around 175 calories in 30 minutes, about as much as brisk walking.
Sled_Drag_-_Harness: Put the weight you want on the sled and fasten the pulling strap. Pull by handles, wear a harness, or clip the strap to a weight belt.
Forwards or backwards, lean towards where you are going and move by straightening your hips and knees.
Sled_Overhead_Backward_Walk: Fasten two handles to a sled with a rope or chain. Put a light weight on the sled.
Stand facing the sled and walk backwards until the line is slightly taut. Hold your hands straight above your head, elbows straight. Start from here.
Walk backwards with your arms still overhead. Move smoothly, without jerking.
Sled_Overhead_Triceps_Extension: Fasten two handles to a sled with a rope or chain. Put a suitable weight on the sled.
Turn your back to the sled and walk away from it until the line is taut. Lift your hands overhead, held together with palms facing each other. Bend the elbows and point them up. Start from here.
Straighten your arms at the elbow. Hold the upper arms still so the triceps does the work alone.
When your arms are straight, step forward until the line is taut again. For more stability, you can stand with one foot ahead of the other.
Sled_Push: Put the weight you want on the pushing sled.

Get into an athletic stance, grip the handles and lean into the sled with straight arms. Push it as fast as you can and concentrate on straightening hips and knees, which strengthens your posterior chain.
Sled_Reverse_Flye: Fasten two handles to a sled with a rope or chain. Put a light weight on the sled.

Stand facing the sled and walk backwards until the line is slightly taut. Hold both handles with straight arms at about waist height. Bend your knees a little and lift chest and head. Start from here.
Keep the elbows straight and pull the handles up and apart in a reverse fly, rotating the arms slightly outward. Your palms face forward during the pull.
Come back to the start and take a couple of steps backwards so the line is taut again.
Sled_Row: Fasten two handles to a sled with a rope or chain. Put a suitable weight on the sled. Stand facing it and walk backwards until the line is slightly taut.
Hold one handle in each hand, bend your knees a little, lift head and chest, and start with straight arms.
Bend your elbows and squeeze your shoulder blades together to pull the sled towards you.
Step back once or twice until the line is taut, then repeat.
Sledgehammer_Swings: For this exercise you need a tire and a sledgehammer. Stand facing the tire, roughly two feet from it, one foot ahead of the other. Take hold of the sledgehammer.
Right-handers hold the end of the handle with the left hand and place the right hand higher up, nearer the head.

While you lift the hammer, slide the right hand towards the head; on the way down, let it slide back to meet the left hand. Hit the tire as hard as you can and keep the rebound of the hammer under control.
Do the same on the other side.
Smith_Incline_Shoulder_Raise: Put an incline bench under the Smith machine. Set the bar at a height you can reach lying down with your arms almost straight. Choose your weight, lie back on the bench and check that your shoulders are directly below the bar.
Grip the bar shoulder-width with palms facing forward (pronated), take it out of the rack and hold it straight above you with the elbows slightly bent. Start from here.
Exhale and push the bar up until your arms are completely straight. Note: You should feel the contraction around your shoulders.
Pause for a second, then inhale and lower the bar to the start.
Do the planned number of repetitions.
Once you finish, return the bar to the rack.
Smith_Machine_Behind_the_Back_Shrug: Set the bar at thigh height and put on a suitable weight.
Stand so the bar is behind you, grip it shoulder-width with a pronated grip and unhook it. Stand upright, head and chest lifted, arms straight. Start from here.
Shrug your shoulders straight up. Keep arms and wrists from bending as you do.
Pause briefly, then lower the weight to the start.
Do the number of repetitions you want, then turn the hooks in to rack the weight.
Smith_Machine_Bench_Press: Put a flat bench under the Smith machine. Set the bar at a height you can reach lying down with your arms almost straight. Choose your weight and lie down on the bench. Take a pronated grip wider than your shoulders, unlock the bar and hold it straight above you with locked arms. Start from here.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly until it touches the middle of your chest.

Pause for a second, then exhale and press the bar back up to the start with your chest muscles. Lock your arms at the top, hold for a second and begin lowering slowly again. Tip: Lowering should take at least twice as long as pressing up.
Do the planned number of repetitions.
Once you finish, lock the bar into the rack again.
Smith_Machine_Bent_Over_Row: Set the bar of the Smith machine roughly 2 inches below knee height.
Bend your knees a little and hinge forward at the waist with a straight back until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Tip: Keep your head up.
Grip the bar overhand (pronated) and unlock it from the rack. Let it hang straight down in front of you, arms straight and at a right angle to the floor and to your torso. Start from here.

Hold your torso still, exhale and pull the bar up with your elbows close to your body; the forearms only hold the weight and do no other work. At the top, squeeze your back muscles and hold for a second.
Inhale and lower the weight slowly to the start.
Do as many repetitions as recommended.
Smith_Machine_Calf_Raise: Put a block or a weight plate under the bar of the Smith machine. Set the bar to suit your height. With the height set and the bar loaded, step on the plates with the balls of your feet and rest the bar across the back of your shoulders.
Hold the bar with both hands, palms facing forward. Turn the bar to release it. Start from here.
Push off the balls of your feet and lift your heels as high as you can, tensing the calves at the top. Keep your knees straight. Hold the top for a second before lowering.
Inhale and lower your heels slowly to the start.
Do as many repetitions as recommended.
Smith_Machine_Close-Grip_Bench_Press: Put a flat bench under the Smith machine. Set the bar at a height you can reach lying down with your arms almost straight. Choose your weight and lie down on the bench. Take a close pronated grip (palms facing forward) at about shoulder width, unlock the bar and hold it straight above you with locked arms. Start from here.

Inhale and lower the bar slowly until it touches the middle of your chest. Tip: Unlike in a regular bench press, keep your elbows tight to your torso the whole time so the triceps works as much as possible.

Pause for a second, then exhale and press the bar back up to the start with your triceps. Lock your arms at the top, hold for a second and begin lowering slowly again. Tip: Lowering should take at least twice as long as pressing up.
Do the planned number of repetitions.
Once you finish, lock the bar into the rack again.
Smith_Machine_Decline_Press: Place a decline bench in the rack so the bar sits over your chest. Put on a suitable weight and lie down on the bench.
Turn the bar to unhook it and straighten your arms fully. Arch your back slightly and pull your shoulder blades together. Start from here.
Bend your arms and lower the bar to your chest.
Hold briefly, then straighten your arms and press the weight back to the start.
When you have done the repetitions you want, turn the bar to rack the weight.
Smith_Machine_Hang_Power_Clean: Set the bar at knee height and put on a suitable weight.

Grip the bar pronated, wider than your shoulders, and unhook it from the machine. Arms are completely straight, head and chest lifted. Elbows point outward, shoulders are back and down. Push your hips back so the tension loads your hamstrings. Start from here.
Drive hips and knees straight with force and accelerate the bar. Keep your arms straight through this phase.
Once fully stretched, bend hips and knees again to drop into a lower receiving position.
Now let your arms bend and whip your elbows around the bar to catch it on your shoulders.
Straighten hips and knees and stand up with the bar resting on your shoulders to finish the movement.
Smith_Machine_Hip_Raise: Place a bench in the rack and put a suitable weight on the bar. Lie on the bench and set the soles of your feet against the bar. Unlock the bar and straighten your legs; your hands can help if needed. Hold the sides of the Smith machine for extra stability. Start from here.
Tilt your pelvis and round your spine to lift your hips off the bench. Keep your knees slightly bent the whole way.
Pause briefly, then lower your hips to the bench.
Do as many repetitions as you planned.
Smith_Machine_Incline_Bench_Press: Put an incline bench under the Smith machine. Set the bar at a height you can reach lying down with your arms almost straight. Choose your weight, lie back on the bench and check that your upper chest lines up with the bar. Take a pronated grip (palms facing forward) wider than your shoulders, unlock the bar and hold it straight above you with locked arms. Start from here.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly until it touches your upper chest.

Pause for a second, then exhale and press the bar back up to the start with your chest muscles. Lock your arms at the top, hold for a second and begin lowering slowly again. Tip: Lowering should take at least twice as long as pressing up.
Do the planned number of repetitions.
Once you finish, return the bar to the rack.
Smith_Machine_Leg_Press: Set the bar of a Smith machine a couple of feet above the floor and make sure it rests on the safeties. Put on a suitable weight and lie down under the bar. Place the middle of each foot on the bar and pull your knees towards your chest. Start from here.
Push through your feet to move the bar up, straightening hips and knees. Stop short of locking the knees.
Hold briefly at the top, then come back to the start.
Smith_Machine_One-Arm_Upright_Row: Set the bar at thigh height and put on a suitable weight.
Grip the bar wide and unhook the weight, then take the non-working hand off the bar. Stand upright with the arm straight, head and chest lifted. Start from here.
Bend the elbow and lift the upper arm with the elbow pointing outward, until the upper arm is parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly, then lower the weight to the start.
Do the number of repetitions you want, then turn the hooks in to rack the weight.
Smith_Machine_Overhead_Shoulder_Press: Put a flat bench, or better one with a back rest, under a Smith machine. Set the bar so high that, sitting on the bench, you have to stretch your arms almost fully to reach it.

With the height set, sit slightly behind the bar so that a straight line could be drawn from the tip of your nose to the bar. Keep your feet still. Grip the bar with palms facing forward, unlock it and press it up until your arms are completely straight. Start from here.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly to chin level.
Exhale and press the bar back up to the start with your shoulders.
Do as many repetitions as recommended.
Smith_Machine_Pistol_Squat: Set the bar to suit your height. Step under it and rest it across the back of your shoulders.
Hold the bar with palms facing forward, unlock it and straighten your legs to lift it out of the rack.

Place one foot roughly 12 inches ahead of the bar. Stretch the other leg out in front and keep it off the floor. Look ahead the whole time and keep your spine neutral or slightly arched. Start from here.
Stay in good alignment and lower yourself by bending knee and hip, as deep as your mobility lets you.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then push through your heel and straighten knee and hip to come back to the start.
Smith_Machine_Reverse_Calf_Raises: Set the bar of the Smith machine to suit your height and put a raised platform directly below it.
Step on the platform so your heels rest firmly on it and the balls of your feet hang over the edge. Point your toes forward, feet shoulder-width apart.

Keep your feet in that position, get your shoulders under the bar and push it up by straightening hips and knees until you stand upright. Keep a slight bend in your knees and never lock them. Start from here. Tip: The bar on your back only helps you balance.

Exhale and lift the balls of your feet, pulling your toes up as high as you can and tensing your calves. Hold the knees still throughout; they must not bend at any point. Hold the top for a second before lowering.
Inhale and slowly lower the balls of your feet and your toes to the start.
Do as many repetitions as recommended.
Smith_Machine_Squat: Set the bar to suit your height. With the height set and the bar loaded, step under it and rest it across the back of your shoulders, just below the neck.
Grip the bar with both arms, one at each side and palms facing forward. Unlock the bar, then take it off the rack: push with your legs first and straighten your torso at the same time.

Set your feet shoulder-width apart in a medium stance, toes turned out slightly. Keep your head up the whole time and your back straight. Start from here. Note: The medium stance used here develops the legs overall; you can also pick any of the three stances.

Bend your knees and lower the bar slowly, upright and with your head up. Go down until the angle between thighs and calves is just under 90 degrees, which is where the thighs drop below parallel to the floor. Inhale on the way down. Tip: Done correctly, the front of your knees lines up with your toes on an imaginary straight line perpendicular to the front. If your knees go beyond that line, past your toes, the knees take needless stress and the exercise is done wrong.
Exhale and raise the bar by pressing your heels into the floor and straightening your legs until you are back at the start.
Do as many repetitions as recommended.
Smith_Machine_Stiff-Legged_Deadlift: Set the bar of the Smith machine at about mid-thigh height. With the height set and the bar loaded, take a shoulder-width pronated grip (palms forward). With heavy weight you may need wrist wraps.
Straighten your arms fully to lift the bar, back straight. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart or closer and knees slightly bent. Start from here.

Without moving your knees, hinge at the waist with a straight back and lower the bar to just above the tops of your feet. Keep going as though picking something up off the floor, until your hamstrings stretch. Exhale during this part.
As soon as you feel that stretch, straighten your hips and waist to bring your torso upright and return to the start. Inhale during this part.
Do as many repetitions as recommended.
Smith_Machine_Upright_Row: Set the bar of the Smith machine at about mid-thigh height. With the height set and the bar loaded, take a shoulder-width pronated grip (palms forward). With heavy weight you may need wrist wraps.
Lift the bar and straighten your arms fully, back straight. Keep a slight bend in the elbows. Start from here.

Exhale and raise the bar with the side of your shoulders, keeping it close to your body, until it almost touches your chin. Tip: Lead with your elbows; while lifting, they always stay higher than your forearms. Hold your torso still and pause for a second at the top.
Lower the bar slowly to the start. Inhale on the way down.
Do as many repetitions as recommended.
Smith_Single-Leg_Split_Squat: Put a flat bench 2-3 feet behind the Smith machine. Set the bar to a height that suits your body size. With the height set and the plates on, get under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders, a little below your neck.
Grip the bar on both sides with your palms facing forward, unlock it, and take it off the rack by pressing up with your legs while you straighten your torso.
Set one foot a little forward beneath the bar, stretch the other leg back and rest the top of that foot on the bench. This is your starting position.

Bend the front knee to lower the bar slowly, staying upright with your head up. Go down until the angle between thigh and calf is a little under 90 degrees, where the thigh is below parallel to the floor. Breathe in on the way down. Tip: Done correctly, the front of your knee and your toes form an imaginary straight line that is perpendicular to the front. If the knee travels beyond that line, past the toes, the knee takes needless stress and the exercise is done wrong.
Breathe out and bring the bar back up, pressing mainly through the heel into the floor while your leg straightens, until you are in the starting position again.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Change legs and do the movement again.
Snatch: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, the barbell lying just above the point where your toes join the rest of the foot.

Bend your knees and, with a flat back, take the bar with your palms facing down and your hands wider than shoulder width. Lower your hips, letting your body sink as though sitting down on a chair. This is your starting position.
Press your feet into the floor as though it were a moving platform and, at the same moment, begin to lift the barbell, keeping it near your legs.
When the bar gets to mid-thigh, drive your legs into the floor and explosively stretch your body out completely.
Shrug your shoulders back while the bar travels up, raising your elbows out to the sides and holding them over the bar as long as you can.
Once the barbell is high enough to be controlled, move your body under it very quickly and powerfully: drop into a squat while you lock your arms and hold the barbell overhead.
Complete the lift by standing up from the squat. At the end, both feet are in line and your arms are fully straight with the barbell overhead.
Snatch_Balance: Start with a wide snatch grip, your feet in the pulling position and the bar racked across the back of your shoulders.
Dip and drive your knees abruptly to pop the bar up, then push yourself hard under it while your feet shift into the receiving position.
Catch the bar overhead with locked arms close to the bottom of the squat. Keep your torso vertical and let your hips sink between your legs.
Keep going down to full depth, then stand back up. Lower the weight carefully.
Snatch_Deadlift: This lift strengthens the first pull of the snatch. Set the barbell on the platform and take a wide snatch grip. Place your feet right under your hips with the toes turned out. Squat down to the bar with your back fully extended and your head facing forward.
Start by pushing through your heels and lifting your hips. Hold the same back angle until the bar has passed your knees.
From there, push your hips through toward the bar and lean back. Reverse the movement to set the bar back on the platform.
Snatch_Pull: Place a barbell on the floor near your shins and take a wide snatch grip. Drop your hips, weight on your heels, back straight, head facing forward and chest up, with your shoulders just ahead of the bar. This is your starting position.
Start the first pull by pushing through your heels and straightening your knees. Keep the same back angle and straight arms. Lift the weight in a controlled way until it is above your knees.

The second pull follows; it gives the pull most of its acceleration. When the bar nears mid-thigh, start to extend your hips. Accelerate as if jumping: extend hips, knees and ankles and use speed to send the bar upward.

You should not need to pull actively with your arms to speed the weight up; when the second pull ends, your body is fully extended and leans back a little. Make the full extension violent and abrupt, and do not hold it longer than needed.
Snatch_Shrug: Take a wide grip and let the bar hang at mid-thigh. A hook grip or an overhand grip both work. Keep your back straight and tilted a little forward.
Pull your shoulders up toward your ears. This exercise can usually be loaded heavier than a snatch, but do not load it so much that the movement becomes slow.
Snatch_from_Blocks: Set a loaded barbell on boxes or stands at the height you want. Take a wide grip. Stand with your feet right under your hips, toes turned out as much as you need. Drop your hips, lift your chest and look forward. Your shoulders are just ahead of the bar and your elbows point outward. This is the starting position.
Start the first pull by pushing through the front of your heels so the bar comes off the boxes.

Move into the second pull: extend your hips, knees and ankles and drive the bar up as fast as you can, keeping it close to your body. At the top of the extension, shrug your shoulders and let your elbows bend out to the sides.

While your feet move into the receiving position, pull yourself forcefully under the bar and bring it overhead. Your feet land just outside your hips, turned out as needed. Catch the bar as low as you can with your arms fully straight overhead.
Hold the bar over the front of your heels, keep your head and chest up, and push through your heels to stand up. Set the weight back on the boxes carefully.
Speed_Band_Overhead_Triceps: Fix a band to the ground for this exercise. One way is to anchor it to the base of an incline bench and stand over the bench. You can also stand on the band instead.
Begin by pulling the band behind your head, with your elbows up and a pronated grip on it. That is the starting position.
Straighten your arms by extending at the elbows, and keep your upper arms still.
After a pause, come back to where you started.
Speed_Box_Squat: Fasten bands to the bar and anchor them securely close to the ground. To get enough tension you may have to choke the bands.
Pick a box of suitable height. Load the bar so that it still takes effort but is not so heavy that you lose speed. As a rule this is 50-70% of your one rep max.
Set the bar on your upper back, pull your shoulder blades together, arch your back and stay tight from head to toe. This is the starting position.
Take the bar out of the rack and stand in front of the box. Push your hips back until you sit on the box; go down under control and do not crash onto it.
Pause for a moment, then explode up from the box by extending your hips and knees.
Speed_Squats: For safety, do this exercise inside a squat rack. Set the bar on the rack at a height that suits your body size. With the height set and the plates on, get under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders, a little below your neck.
Grip the bar on both sides and take it off the rack by pressing up with your legs while you straighten your torso.

Step back from the rack and take a medium, shoulder-width stance with your toes turned out slightly. Keep your head up the whole time, since looking down throws you off balance, and keep your back straight. This is your starting position. Note: The medium stance is used here because it develops the legs overall, but you can pick any of the three stances.

Bend your knees to lower the bar, staying upright with your head up. Go down until the angle between thighs and calves is a little under 90 degrees, where the thighs are below parallel to the floor. Breathe in on the way down. Tip: Done correctly, the front of your knees and your toes form an imaginary straight line that is perpendicular to the front. If the knees travel beyond that line, past the toes, they take needless stress and the exercise is done wrong.

Breathe out and drive the bar up as quickly as you can without using momentum, pressing mainly through your heels into the floor while your legs straighten, until you are back in the starting position. Note: Do these as fast as you can, but never at the cost of perfect form and never with momentum.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Spell_Caster: Take a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated grip. Stand with a wide stance, hips and knees straight. This is your starting position.
Start by turning your torso and drawing both dumbbells to one side, beside your hip.
With straight arms and the dumbbells parallel to the floor, turn your torso and swing the weights over to the other side.
Keep alternating, turning from side to side, until you finish the set.
Spider_Crawl: Lie face down on the floor. Hold yourself up on your hands and toes, feet together and body in a straight line. Bend your arms to 90 degrees. This is your starting position.
Start by lifting one foot off the floor. Rotate that leg outward and draw the knee toward your elbow, as far forward as you can.
Bring the leg back to the starting position and do the same on the other side.
Spider_Curl: Lay the bar on the seat part of the preacher bench. Place it so that it is balanced and cannot fall off.
Go to the front of the preacher bench, where the arms normally rest, and lean on it at a 45 degree slant with your torso and stomach pressed against that front side.
Plant your feet, the toes above all, firmly on the floor and rest your upper arms on the pad on the inner side of the preacher bench.
Take the bar with a supinated grip, palms facing up, with your hands about shoulder-width apart or a little closer.
Breathe out and curl the bar up slowly. Squeeze your biceps and hold the top position for a second.
Breathe in and slowly lower the bar to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Spinal_Stretch: Sit on a chair with a straight back and your feet flat on the floor.
Lock your fingers together behind your head, elbows pointing out and chin lowered.
Turn your upper body to one side as far as you can, about 3 times. After that, lean forward and rotate your torso so that your elbow reaches toward the floor on the inside of your knee.
Sit upright again, then do the same on the other side.
Split_Clean: Place a barbell on the floor near your shins and grip it overhand just outside your legs. Drop your hips, weight on your heels, back straight, head facing forward and chest up, with your shoulders just ahead of the bar. This is your starting position.
Start the first pull by pushing through your heels and straightening your knees. Keep the same back angle and straight arms. Lift the weight in a controlled way until it is above your knees.

The second pull follows; it gives the clean most of its acceleration. When the bar nears mid-thigh, start to extend your hips. Accelerate as if jumping: extend hips, knees and ankles and use speed to send the bar upward. You should not need to pull actively with your arms to speed the weight up; when the second pull ends, your body is fully extended and leans back a little, and your arms are still straight.

Once you are fully extended, go into the third pull: shrug hard and bend your arms with the elbows up and out. At the top of the extension, pull yourself down aggressively and turn your elbows under the bar as you go.

Catch the bar in a split, driving one foot forward and the other back. The bar rests on your shoulders, which are pushed forward, and lightly touches your throat while your hands stay relaxed. Keep sinking to the bottom position; this helps the recovery.
Recover at once by pushing through your heels with an upright torso and high elbows. Bring your feet together while you stand up.
Split_Jerk: Stand with the weight resting on the front of your shoulders and start with the dip. Feet right under your hips, bend your knees without letting your hips move back.

Dip only a little, then change direction as powerfully as you can. Push through your heels to produce as much speed and force as possible, and move your head out of the way when the bar leaves your shoulders. As your feet come off the floor, get them into the receiving position as fast as you can.

For the short moment in which your feet are not pushing against the platform, your effort to press the bar up pushes you down. Move your feet into a split stance, one in front and one behind, knees partly bent. Catch the bar overhead with locked arms.
Stand up again and bring your feet together.
Split_Jump: Get into a lunge stance: one foot in front with the knee bent, the back knee almost touching the floor.
The front knee must be over the foot's midline; make sure of it.
Push off with both legs and jump as high as you can, swinging your arms for extra lift.
In the air, bring your feet together, then return them to where they started as you land.
Cushion the landing by sinking back into the starting position.
Split_Snatch: Set a loaded barbell on the floor, near your shins or touching them, and take a wide grip. Stand with your feet right under your hips, toes turned out as much as you need. Drop your hips, lift your chest and look forward. Your shoulders are just ahead of the bar. This is the starting position.
Start the first pull by pushing through the front of your heels so the bar leaves the floor. Hold the same back angle until the bar has passed your knees.

Move into the second pull: extend your hips, knees and ankles and drive the bar up as fast as you can, keeping it close to your body. At the top of the extension, shrug your shoulders and let your elbows bend out to the sides.

While your feet move into the receiving position, pull yourself forcefully under the bar and bring it overhead. Drive your feet into a split, one in front and one behind. Catch the bar as low as you can with your arms fully straight overhead.
Hold the bar over the front of your heels, keep your head and chest up, and push through your heels to stand up while you bring your feet together.
Set the weight back on the floor carefully.
Split_Squat_with_Dumbbells: Take a staggered stance with your back foot raised and your front foot ahead of you.
Your starting position: one dumbbell in each hand, both hanging at your sides.
Start going down: bend your knee and hip so your body sinks. Keep good posture all the way through, and keep your front knee in line with the foot.
At the bottom, push through your heel and straighten knee and hip to come back to the starting position.
Split_Squats: Start standing. Jump into a split, one leg in front and one behind, bending your knees and dropping your hips a little as you land.
On the way down, change direction right away: stand up, jump and swap the position of your legs. Do 5-10 repetitions on each leg.
Squat_Jerk: Stand with the weight resting on the front of your shoulders and start with the dip. Feet right under your hips, bend your knees without letting your hips move back. Dip only a little, then change direction as powerfully as you can. Push through your heels to produce as much speed and force as possible, and move your head out of the way when the bar leaves your shoulders.

As your feet come off the floor, get them into the receiving position as fast as you can. For the short moment in which your feet are not pushing against the platform, your effort to press the bar up pushes you down. Drive your feet to just outside your hips, turned out as needed. Catch the bar in a full squat with your arms fully straight overhead.
Hold the bar over the front of your heels, keep your head and chest up, and push through your heels to stand up. Set the weight back on the floor carefully.
Squat_with_Bands: Loop the bands over the sleeves of the bar and fix them to band pegs, the rack or dumbbells so that the tension is right.

Get under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders. Pull your shoulder blades together and turn your elbows forward, as if trying to bend the bar over your shoulders. Take the bar out of the rack with a tight arch in your lower back and step back into place. A wide stance puts more work on the back, glutes, adductors and hamstrings. Look straight ahead.

Keep your back, shoulders and core tight and push your knees and butt out as you start to go down. Sit back with your hips as far as you can. Ideally your shins stay perpendicular to the floor. The lower the bar sits, the more your torso has to lean to keep the bar over your heels. Go down until you break parallel, meaning the crease of your hip is level with the top of your knee.
With your weight on your heels and your feet and knees pushed out, drive up, leading with your head. Stay tight from head to toe and keep rising until you are back in the starting position.
Squat_with_Chains: Set up the chains by looping the leader chain over the sleeves of the bar. Attach the heavy chain with a snap hook. Set the length of the leader chain so that a few links still lie on the floor at the top of the movement.

Get under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders. Pull your shoulder blades together and turn your elbows forward, as if trying to bend the bar over your shoulders. Take the bar out of the rack with a tight arch in your lower back and step back into place. A wide stance puts more work on the back, glutes, adductors and hamstrings. Look straight ahead.

Keep your back, shoulders and core tight and push your knees and butt out as you start to go down. Sit back with your hips as far as you can. Ideally your shins stay perpendicular to the floor. The lower the bar sits, the more your torso has to lean to keep the bar over your heels. Go down until you break parallel, meaning the crease of your hip is level with the top of your knee.
With your weight on your heels and your feet and knees pushed out, drive up, leading with your head. Stay tight from head to toe and keep rising until you are back in the starting position.
Squat_with_Plate_Movers: Set the bar on a rack just below shoulder height. Lay a weight plate on the floor a couple of feet behind the rack. With the bar loaded, get under it and rest it across the back of your shoulders.
Grip the bar with both hands and take it off the rack by pressing up with your legs while you straighten your torso.
Move away from the rack. Take a wide stance with one foot on the weight plate and the toes pointed slightly out, and keep your head up at all times. That is the starting position.
Bend your knees and hips to lower the bar slowly. Go down until the angle between thighs and calves is a little under 90 degrees.
Breathe out and lift the bar, pressing your heels into the floor while you extend your hips and knees.
At the top, take a side step so that your feet come together on the other side of the plate.
With your inside foot, push the plate and slide it over the floor to the spot where you just stood.
For the next repetition, take a wide stance by putting your inside foot on the weight plate.
Squats_-_With_Bands: First make sure the band is split evenly between the left and right side of your body. To do that, take both ends of the band in your hands and stand with both feet on its middle, shoulder-width apart.
Hold the band at the same height on both sides. Use a pronated grip, palms facing forward, with the handles beside your face. This is the starting position.
Breathe out while you slowly bend your knees and sink until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Breathe out and press through your heels to push yourself up to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Stairmaster: Step onto the stair climber and pick the option you want from the menu. You can set it manually or run a program. Usually you can enter your age and weight so the machine can estimate the calories you burn.

Move your legs up and down in a steady rhythm, pressing the pedals down without letting them reach the floor. Keeping hold of the handles is recommended so that you do not fall. The handles can also track your heart rate, which helps you stay at a suitable intensity.

Stair climbers are convenient, good for the cardiovascular system and usually lower in impact than running outdoors. They are generally much harder than other cardio machines. A person weighing 150 lb typically burns more than 300 calories in 30 minutes, against roughly 175 calories when walking.
Standing_Alternating_Dumbbell_Press: Stand, a dumbbell in each hand. Your starting position is with the dumbbells raised to the shoulders, elbows pointed out and palms facing forward.
Straighten one arm and press its dumbbell straight up while the other hand stays where it is. Do not lean or jerk the weight.
Pause briefly, then lower the weight to the starting position.
Do the same with the other arm and keep alternating.
Standing_Barbell_Calf_Raise: For safety, do this exercise inside a squat rack. Set the bar on the rack at a height that suits your body size. With the height set and the plates on, get under the bar and rest it on the back of your shoulders, a little below your neck.
Grip the bar on both sides and take it off the rack by pressing up with your legs while you straighten your torso.

Step back from the rack and take a medium, shoulder-width stance with your toes turned out slightly. Keep your head up the whole time, since looking down throws you off balance, and keep your back straight. Hold your knees slightly bent and never lock them. This is your starting position. Tip: For more range of motion you can put the balls of your feet on a wooden block, but take care: this needs more balance and a sturdy block.

Breathe out and lift your heels by extending your ankles as high as you can and tensing your calves. Your knees stay still the whole time and do not bend at any point. Hold the top position for a second before you go down again.
Breathe in and return slowly to the starting position: lower your heels and bend your ankles until your calves are stretched.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Standing_Barbell_Press_Behind_Neck: Do this exercise inside a squat rack, which makes picking up the bar easier. Set the bar on the rack at a height that suits your body size. With the height set and the plates on, get under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders, a little below your neck.
Grip the bar on both sides and take it off the rack by pressing up with your legs while you straighten your torso.
Step back from the rack and take a medium, shoulder-width stance with your toes turned out slightly. Keep your back straight throughout the exercise. This is your starting position.
Breathe out and press the barbell overhead until your arms are fully straight.
Hold for a second at the top, then breathe in and lower the barbell to the starting position.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Standing_Bent-Over_One-Arm_Dumbbell_Tric: Hold a dumbbell in one hand, palm turned towards your body. Soften your knees and hinge forward at the waist with a flat back until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Keep your head lifted.

Tuck the upper arm in beside your torso so that it runs parallel to the floor, and let the forearm hang straight down with the weight in your hand. Tip: Forearm and upper arm should form a 90-degree angle. Start from here.

Hold the upper arm still and breathe out while your triceps raises the weight, until the forearm is parallel to the floor and the arm is completely straight. As in many arm exercises, nothing but the forearm moves.
Squeeze at the top for one second, then breathe in and bring the dumbbell slowly down to where you started.
Do as many repetitions as your plan calls for.
Change to the other arm and do the exercise again.
Standing_Bent-Over_Two-Arm_Dumbbell_Tric: Take one dumbbell in each hand, palms turned towards your body. Soften your knees and hinge forward at the waist with a flat back until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Keep your head lifted. Tuck the upper arms in beside your torso so that they run parallel to the floor, and let the forearms hang straight down with the weights in your hands. Tip: Forearms and upper arms should form a 90-degree angle. Start from here.

Hold the upper arms still and breathe out while your triceps raise the weights, until the forearms are parallel to the floor and both arms are completely straight. As in many arm exercises, nothing but the forearms move.
Squeeze at the top for one second, then breathe in and bring the dumbbells slowly down to where they started.
Do as many repetitions as your plan calls for.
Standing_Biceps_Cable_Curl: Fix a curl bar to a low pulley and stand tall with it in your hands. Take a shoulder-width grip, tuck your elbows in at your sides and turn your palms upward (supinated grip). Start from here.

Breathe out and curl the bar up by tightening your biceps, with the upper arms held still. Nothing but the forearms moves. Keep going until the biceps are fully shortened and the bar has reached shoulder height. Squeeze the muscle there for one second.
Breathe in and let the bar travel slowly down to where you started.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Standing_Biceps_Stretch: Join your hands behind your back, palm against palm. Stretch your arms out straight, then turn them until the palms point down.
Lift your arms and stay there once you feel the stretch in your biceps.
Standing_Bradford_Press: Set a loaded bar in a rack at the height of your shoulders. Take it shoulder-width with an overhand grip and rest it across the front of your shoulders. Start from here.
Begin by straightening your elbows so the bar travels overhead. Do not lock the elbows out while you guide the weight behind your head.
Bring the bar down behind your head until your elbows are bent to a right angle.
Straighten the elbows to press the bar up over your head again.
Bring the bar down in front to where you started.
Keep alternating front and back like this until the recommended number of repetitions is done.
Standing_Cable_Chest_Press: Set both pulleys to chest height and choose a suitable weight. Take a handle in each hand and stand a foot or two forward of the cables. For a steadier stance, put one foot ahead of the other.
Bring your upper arms to a 90 degree angle and pull your shoulder blades together. Start from here.
Hold the rest of your body still and straighten your elbows to push the handles forward until they meet in front of you.
Hold briefly at the end of the press, then come back to the start.
Standing_Cable_Lift: Fix a standard handle to a cable tower and slide the pulley down to its lowest setting.

Stand side-on to the cable, take the handle in one hand and step away from the tower. Stop about an arm's length from the pulley, where the cable is pulled taut by the weight. Your straight arm should be in line with the cable.
Set your feet shoulder-width apart, drop into a squat and take the handle with both hands. Both arms stay completely straight.
In a single movement, draw the handle upward and across your body until your arms are stretched out fully above your head.
For a full range of motion, pivot on your back foot and straighten your legs, with your arms close to your body and a straight back.
Bring your arms back first and your body after them. Come back to the neutral position slowly and under control.
Repeat until you cannot do another repetition.
Then set up on the other side and go through the same movements there.
Standing_Cable_Wood_Chop: Fix a standard handle to a cable tower and slide the pulley up to its highest setting.

Stand side-on to the cable, take the handle in one hand and step away from the tower. Stop about an arm's length from the pulley, where the cable is pulled taut by the weight. Your straight arm should be in line with the cable.
Set your feet shoulder-width apart, reach up with the free hand and take the handle with both hands. Both arms stay completely straight.
In a single movement, draw the handle downward and across your body to your front knee, turning your torso as you go.
Hold your back and arms straight and your core braced while you turn on your back foot and bend your knees, so that you use the full range of motion.
Stay in your stance with straight arms. Come back to the neutral position slowly and under control.
Repeat until you cannot do another repetition.
Then set up on the other side and go through the same movements there.
Standing_Calf_Raises: Fit the calf raise machine's padded lever to your height.

Get your shoulders under the pads and point your toes forward (or choose one of the two other foot positions). Stand with the balls of your feet firmly on the calf block and your heels hanging over its edge. Straighten your hips and knees to lift the lever until you are standing upright. Leave a slight bend in the knees and never lock them. The toes may point forward, outward or inward. Start from here.

Breathe out and lift your heels as high as they go by extending the ankles and tightening the calves. The knees stay still the whole time and must not bend at any point. Stay at the top for one second before you come down.
Breathe in and come slowly back to the start: let the ankles bend and the heels sink until you feel the calves stretch.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Standing_Concentration_Curl: Pick up a dumbbell with the hand that will work and lean forward. Let that arm hang straight down, at a right angle to the ground, with the elbow turned outward. Start from here.
Bend the elbow to curl the weight up while the upper arm stays still. At the top, tighten the biceps and hold briefly.
Bring the dumbbell down again to the start.
Do as many repetitions as your plan calls for.
Standing_Dumbbell_Calf_Raise: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Put the balls of your feet on a firm, stable wooden board (about 2-3 inches high) so that your heels hang off it and rest on the floor. Start from here.

Point your toes straight ahead (to work all parts evenly), inward (to stress the outer head more) or outward (to stress the inner head more). Breathe out and tighten your calves to lift the heels from the floor. Stay at the top for one second.
Breathe in and let the heels sink slowly back to the start.
Do this as many times as recommended.
Standing_Dumbbell_Press: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and a dumbbell in each hand. Bring the dumbbells up to the height of your head, elbows out to the sides and bent to roughly 90 degrees. Start from here.
Stay strict: no push from the legs and no leaning back. Straighten your elbows to press both weights up until they meet right above your head.
Hold briefly, then bring the weights slowly back to the start.
Standing_Dumbbell_Reverse_Curl: Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand in a pronated grip (palms turned down). Let your arms hang fully straight and set your feet shoulder-width apart. Start from here.

Breathe out and curl the weights up by tightening your biceps, with the upper arms held still. Nothing but the forearms moves. Keep going until the biceps are fully shortened and the dumbbells have reached shoulder height. Squeeze the muscle there for one second.
Breathe in and let the dumbbells travel slowly down to where you started.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Standing_Dumbbell_Straight-Arm_Front_Del: Hold the dumbbells in front of your thighs with your palms turned towards them.
Keep the arms straight apart from a small bend in the elbows, and fix the elbows at that angle. Start from here.
Breathe out and lift the dumbbells in a half circle until they are overhead at arm's length.
Breathe in and come slowly back down along the same arc to the start.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Standing_Dumbbell_Triceps_Extension: Stand up holding one dumbbell with both hands, feet roughly shoulder-width apart. Take hold of the dumbbell with both hands and raise it slowly above your head until both arms are completely straight.
Let the weight rest in your palms with your thumbs wrapped around it. Your palms point up to the ceiling. Start from here.

Keep your upper arms near your head, elbows tucked in and at a right angle to the floor. Lower the weight in a half circle behind your head until your forearms touch your biceps. Tip: The upper arms stay still and only the forearms move. Breathe in during this step.
Use your triceps to lift the dumbbell back to the start. Breathe out during this step.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Standing_Dumbbell_Upright_Row: Take a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated grip (palms forward), hands a little closer than shoulder width. Let the dumbbells rest on the front of your thighs. Keep your arms long with a small bend in the elbows and your back straight. Start from here.

Breathe out and lift the dumbbells with the side of your shoulders. Keep them near your body on the way up and lead with the elbows. Lift until they almost reach your chin. Tip: The elbows lead the movement. While you lift, the elbows always stay higher than the forearms. Keep your torso still as well, and hold for one second at the top.
Bring the dumbbells slowly down to the start. Breathe in during this part of the movement.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Standing_Elevated_Quad_Stretch: Stand with your back to a bench or step, about two to three feet in front of it.
Raise one leg behind you and put the foot on the step. Rest it on the instep or on the ball of the foot, whichever feels more comfortable.
Leave a slight bend in the knee of the standing leg and do not let that knee travel past your toes. Change sides.
Standing_Front_Barbell_Raise_Over_Head: Stand upright with a barbell in your hands. Hold the bar with your palms turned down and your hands closer together than shoulder width.
Set your feet shoulder-width apart and bend your elbows a little. Start from here.
Breathe out and raise the barbell until it is right above your head. Keep that small bend in the elbows on every repetition.
When you feel the muscles contract, breathe in and start bringing the barbell down to the start.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Standing_Gastrocnemius_Calf_Stretch: Put your right heel on a step with the knee straight, lean forward and take hold of your right toes with your right hand. Bend your left knee a little and keep your back straight.
With your weight supported on the left leg, put your left hand on the left thigh.
Draw the toes of your right foot towards the knee until you feel the calf stretch.
Standing_Hamstring_and_Calf_Stretch: Loop a belt, band or rope around one foot. Stand up and set that foot in front of you.
Bend the rear leg and keep the front leg straight. Now lift the toes of the front foot from the ground and lean forward.
Pull on the top of the foot with the belt to deepen the stretch in the calf. Hold for 10-20 seconds, then do the same with the other foot.
Standing_Hip_Circles: Stand on one leg and hold on to an upright support.
Lift the knee of the free leg to 90 degrees. Start from here.
Open the hip as wide as you can and try to draw a large circle with your knee.
Do a number of slow repetitions, then repeat on the other side.
Standing_Hip_Flexors: Stand tall with your spine vertical and your left foot a little ahead of the right.

Bend both knees, lift the rear heel from the floor and push the right hip forward. A thorough, deep stretch is not possible here, though, because the hip flexor can hardly relax while you are standing on it. Change sides.
Standing_Inner-Biceps_Curl: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging at full length. Tuck your elbows in at your sides. Set your legs roughly shoulder-width apart.
Turn your palms inward to a neutral position. Start from here.
Breathe out and curl the weights up and outward by tightening your biceps, with the upper arms held still. Turn your wrists on the way so that you finish at the top in a supinated grip (palms up).
Nothing but the forearms moves. Keep going until the biceps are fully shortened and the dumbbells have reached shoulder height. Tip: Keep your forearms in line with the outer part of your deltoids.
Stay in that position for one second and squeeze the biceps.
Breathe in and let the dumbbells travel slowly down to the start. Turn your wrists back on the way down so that you return to a neutral grip.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Standing_Lateral_Stretch: Stand with your feet a little wider than your hips and your knees slightly bent.
To support the spine, your right hand goes on your right hip.
Lift your left arm straight up and lay the left hand behind your head. Leave it there while you tilt your torso to the right.
Spread your weight evenly over both legs (do not sink into your left hip). Change sides.
Standing_Leg_Curl: Set the machine's lever to suit your height. Lean into the machine facing forward, torso bent at the waist by around 30-45 degrees (an angled position recruits the hamstrings better). The lever pad sits on the back of your right leg, a few inches below the calf, and the front of the right leg rests against the machine pad.
Stay bent forward, check that your leg is fully straight and hold the handles at the sides of the machine. Point your toes straight. Start from here.
Breathe out and curl your right leg up as far as it goes while the upper leg stays on the pad. When the muscle is fully contracted, hold for one second.
Breathe in and let the leg return to where it started. Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Now do the same exercise with the left leg.
Standing_Long_Jump: Sand or another soft surface to land on suits this drill best. Make sure you have a way to measure distance. Stand in a partial squat with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Swing your arms hard, dip with your legs for a countermovement and jump as far forward as you can.
Try to land with your feet ahead of you, reaching as far forward with your legs as possible.
Measure how far your landing point is from the start and keep a record of the results.
Standing_Low-Pulley_Deltoid_Raise: Stand to the right of a low pulley. Reach across your body with your left hand and take a single handle fixed to the low pulley in a pronated grip (palm turned down). Let the arm rest in front of you. Hold the machine with your right hand for more support and balance.
Check that your back is upright and your feet are shoulder-width apart. Start from here.
Breathe out and draw the left hand across your body and out to the side until it is at shoulder height.
Feel the muscle work at the top for one second, then breathe in and bring the handle slowly down to where it started.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Change to the other arm and do the exercise again.
Standing_Low-Pulley_One-Arm_Triceps_Exte: Stand beside the low pulley machine and take a single handle with your left hand. Turn your back to the machine, holding the handle at your side with the arm fully straight. Now lift the handle with both hands until it is right above your head, palm turned forward. Hold the upper arm fully vertical (at a right angle to the floor) and steady the left elbow with your right hand. Start from here.

Keep your upper arm near your head (elbow tucked in) and at a right angle to the floor. Lower the weight in a half circle behind your head until the forearm touches the biceps. Tip: The upper arm stays still and only the forearm moves. Breathe in during this step.
Use your triceps to lift the handle back to the start. Breathe out during this step.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Change to the other arm and do the exercise again.
Standing_Military_Press: Set a barbell at about chest height in a squat rack. When the weight is loaded, take the bar in a pronated grip (palms turned forward), with your hands wider than shoulder width.
Bend your knees a little and bring the barbell onto your collarbone. Lift it out so that it rests on your chest. Step back once and set your feet shoulder-width apart.
With the bar held at the right grip width, press it up over your head until your arms lock. Hold it roughly above your shoulders and a little in front of your head. Start from here.
Breathe in and bring the bar slowly down to your collarbone.
Breathe out and press the bar up again to the start.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Standing_Olympic_Plate_Hand_Squeeze: Stand upright with a weight plate in each hand, held by its rim at arm's length in a neutral grip (palms turned in). Set your feet shoulder-width apart. Start from here.
Let the plates sink until your fingers are almost straight but can still hold the weight. Breathe in while they sink.
Now breathe out and close your hands to bring the plates back up to the start.
Do the number of repetitions your programme prescribes.
Standing_One-Arm_Cable_Curl: Stand beside the low pulley machine and take a single handle. Move far enough away from the machine for your arm to be carrying the weight.
Hold the upper arm still and at a right angle to the floor, elbow tucked in and palm turned forward. Put the hand of the other arm on your waist. That helps you keep your balance.
Breathe out and curl the handle slowly up, with the upper arm still, until the forearm touches the biceps. Tip: Only the forearm moves.
Stay in the contracted position and squeeze the biceps, then breathe in and bring the handle down to the start.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Change arms and do the exercise with the other one.
Standing_One-Arm_Dumbbell_Curl_Over_Incl: Stand behind an incline bench, where a spotter would stand. Hold a dumbbell in one hand and lay that arm over the bench in a supinated grip (palm up).
Put your free hand on the corner or side of the bench. Press your chest against the top of the incline and plant your feet on the floor in a wide stance. Start from here.

Breathe out and curl the dumbbell up by tightening your biceps, with the upper arm held still. Nothing but the forearm moves. Keep going until the biceps is fully shortened and the dumbbell has reached shoulder height. Stay there for one second.
Breathe in and let the dumbbell travel slowly down to the start.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Change arms and do the exercise with the other one.
Standing_One-Arm_Dumbbell_Triceps_Extens: Stand up with a dumbbell in one hand, feet roughly shoulder-width apart. Stretch the arm with the dumbbell out fully above your head. Tip: Your little finger points to the ceiling and your palm is turned forward. The dumbbell is above your head.

Keep your upper arm near your head (elbow tucked in) and at a right angle to the floor. Lower the weight in a half circle behind your head until the forearm touches the biceps. Tip: The upper arm stays still and only the forearm moves. Breathe in during this step.
Use your triceps to lift the dumbbell back to the start. Breathe out during this step.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Change to the other arm and do the exercise again.
Standing_Overhead_Barbell_Triceps_Extens: Stand up with a barbell or e-z bar in a pronated grip (palms turned forward), hands closer together than shoulder width. Set your feet roughly shoulder-width apart.
Now lift the bar above your head until your arms are completely straight. Keep the elbows tucked in. Start from here.

Keep your upper arms near your head, elbows tucked in and at a right angle to the floor. Lower the weight in a half circle behind your head until your forearms touch your biceps. Tip: The upper arms stay still and only the forearms move. Breathe in during this step.
Use your triceps to lift the bar back to the start. Breathe out during this step.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Standing_Palm-In_One-Arm_Dumbbell_Press: Hold a dumbbell in one hand in a neutral grip, the arm hanging fully straight at your side. Hold on to an incline bench with the other arm for balance.

Set your feet shoulder-width apart. Now raise the dumbbell slowly until your arm is bent to a 90 degree angle. Note: The forearm is at a right angle to the floor. Keep the neutral grip for the whole exercise.
Press the dumbbell slowly up until the arm is completely straight. Start from here.
Breathe in and lower the weight until the arm is back at a 90 degree angle.

Feel the muscle work for one second, then breathe out and press the weight up towards the start. Keep holding the incline bench and keep your feet planted so that you stay balanced during the exercise.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Change to the other arm and do the exercise again.
Standing_Palms-In_Dumbbell_Press: Hold a dumbbell in each hand in a neutral grip, arms hanging fully straight at your sides. Set your feet shoulder-width apart. Now raise the dumbbells slowly until your arms are bent to a 90 degree angle. Note: The forearms are at a right angle to the floor. Start from here.
Keep the neutral grip for the whole exercise. Press the dumbbells slowly up until your arms are completely straight.
Breathe in and lower the weights until your arms are back at a 90 degree angle.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
Standing_Palms-Up_Barbell_Behind_The_Bac: Stand upright and hold a barbell behind your glutes at arm's length in a pronated grip (palms turned back, away from the glutes), hands shoulder-width apart.
Look straight ahead and set your feet shoulder-width apart. Start from here.
Breathe out and raise the barbell slowly by curling your wrists up towards the ceiling in a half circle. Note: In this exercise the wrists are the only part of the body that moves.
Stay at the top for one second, then breathe in and let the barbell sink to the start.
Do the recommended number of repetitions.
When you are done, bend your knees to put the barbell down on the squat rack or the floor. Tip: Picking it up from a squat rack or having a partner hand it to you is the easiest way.
Standing_Pelvic_Tilt: Stand with your feet as far apart as your hips.
Bend your knees a little so that they stay soft and springy.
If you like, rock your pelvis forward and back a few times before you hold the tailbone forward for this stretch.
Standing_Rope_Crunch: Fix a rope to a high pulley and choose a suitable weight.
Stand with your back towards the cable tower. Take the rope over your shoulders with both hands and hold it against your upper chest. Start from here.
Round your spine to crunch the weight down as far as you can.
Stay briefly at the point of strongest contraction, then come back to the start.
Standing_Soleus_And_Achilles_Stretch: Stand with your feet as far apart as your hips, one of them a little ahead of the other.
Bend both knees and keep the rear heel on the floor. Change sides.
Standing_Toe_Touches: Stand where you have some room in front of you and behind you.
With straight legs, bend at the waist until your upper body can hang down in front of you and you can relax. Your arms and hands hang down naturally too. Stay for 10 to 20 seconds.
Standing_Towel_Triceps_Extension: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and grip one end of a towel with both hands, arms stretched straight overhead. Tuck your elbows in, keep your arms vertical to the floor and turn your palms towards each other. That is your starting position.

Tell your partner to take hold of the towel's other end and pull against you. With your elbows in and your upper arms vertical beside your head, let the towel travel down behind your head in a half circle until forearms and biceps meet. Tip: Hold your upper arms still; the forearms alone do the moving. Inhale during this part.
Raise the towel again with the strength of your triceps until you reach the starting position. Exhale during this part.
Do as many repetitions as your plan calls for.
Standing_Two-Arm_Overhead_Throw: Take a medicine ball in both hands and set your feet shoulder width apart. Start by bending your knees a little, leaning back and bringing the ball far behind your head.
Hurl the ball forward with full force. Bend at the hip and put your entire body into the throw.
Throw to a partner, or against a wall and catch the ball when it rebounds.
Star_Jump: Stand loosely, feet shoulder width apart, arms held near your body.
Start by dropping into a half squat, then jump up explosively, as high as you can. Stretch your whole body out and spread arms and legs wide.
On the way down, pull your arms and legs back in and cushion the landing with your legs.
Step-up_with_Knee_Raise: Face a box or bench of suitable height and stand with your feet together. That is your starting position.

Start by placing your left foot on top of the bench. Straighten the hip and knee of that front leg until you are standing on the box. While your left leg carries you, bend the right hip and knee and lift the knee as high as possible.
Go back the same way to step down from the box, then do the same sequence with the other leg.
Step_Mill: Get onto the stepmill and pick what you want from the menu: either a manual setting or a ready-made program. Most machines let you enter age and weight so they can estimate the calories you burn. Climb carefully so you do not trip. Keeping your hands on the handles is advised so you do not fall.

A stepmill is convenient, trains your cardiovascular system and is usually gentler on the joints than running outdoors, at a similar calorie burn. It tends to be far harder than other cardio machines. In 30 minutes, someone weighing 150 lb usually burns more than 300 calories, against roughly 175 calories when walking.
Stiff-Legged_Barbell_Deadlift: Take a bar with an overhand grip, palms turned down. With heavy weight you may need wrist wraps.
Stand with a straight torso and your feet shoulder width apart or closer. Bend your knees slightly. That is your starting position.

Keep your knees fixed and your back straight, and bend at the hips to lower the barbell to just above your feet. Reach forward, as though picking something up off the floor, until your hamstrings stretch. Inhale on the way down.
Extend your hips to bring your torso upright again until you reach the starting position. Exhale on the way up.
Do as many repetitions as your plan calls for.
Stiff-Legged_Dumbbell_Deadlift: Take two dumbbells and let them hang at your sides with straight arms.
Stand with a straight torso and your feet shoulder width apart or closer. Bend your knees slightly. That is your starting position.

Keep your knees fixed and your back straight, and bend at the waist to lower the dumbbells to just above your feet. Reach forward, as though picking something up off the floor, until your hamstrings stretch. Exhale on the way down.
Extend your hips and waist to bring your torso upright again until you reach the starting position. Inhale on the way up.
Do as many repetitions as your plan calls for.
Stiff_Leg_Barbell_Good_Morning: For safety, do this exercise inside a squat rack. First set the bar on the rack at the height that suits you best. With the height set and the bar loaded, duck under it and rest it across the back of your shoulders, just below the neck.
Grip the bar with one hand on each side. Lift it out of the rack by pushing with your legs while you straighten your torso.
